News.title: Brutal DZ Mafia using kids for gang murders & behind brazen attacks on mayor and TV star in Brit holiday hotspot
News.content:
IN the dead of night, armed police shook Christophe Rivenq awake in his southern France home and rushed him and his family to safety amid fears of an incoming attack by the country’s most feared gang.

Cops had been tipped off that a car bomb was about to explode outside the house of the Alès Mayor – on the orders of DZ Mafia, a brutal drug cartel that has left a grim trail of blood and destruction in its wake in a popular tourist hotspot.





Armed with Kalashnikovs and commissioning “child killers” to carry out their dirty work, DZ Mafia is blamed for well over 100 murders in the last three years amid a terrifying turf war.

A state of panic has long gripped areas of the clan’s main haunt, the huge Mediterranean city of Marseille, a short car ride away from millionaires’ playgrounds like Saint-Tropez and Cannes on the famed Côte d’Azur French Riviera.

But experts say the gang’s presence in the small city of Alès, 86 miles northwest, is only a small step in a bold operation to expand its reign of terror.

Organised crime expert Fabrice Rizzoli told The Sun: “In more than 30 years I have never seen anything like the DZ Mafia.

“It is violence without restraint. Innocent civilians, judges, police and politicians are all targets.

“People are scared, they will not speak or give their names in investigations out of fear they will be targeted.”





Two days after the foiled plot against Mayor Christophe, the car of influencer and French TV reality star Carla Moreau was set on fire and destroyed in front of her Marseille home.

At the scene, police found a mobile phone and a note demanding over £50,000 bearing the signature of DZ Mafia.

The phone – a pre-paid burner – is a common tactic of the gang to force targets to contact them via encrypted messaging apps and demand money for protection.

While an official link has not yet been made by investigators, DZ Mafia is known to target influencers and high profile influencers for raise quick cash for ongoing turf wars.

Just a few days ago the popular Marseille rapper Jul was forced to leave his home in the city following similar threats from the DMZ Mafia, according to Le Parisien.

Unknown to police until 2023, DZ Mafia has rapidly evolved into a criminal syndicate with its own branding and social media presence.

The DZ in its name refers to country code for Algeria – the origin of its founding members.

Police were first alerted to the clan after it posted pictures of a victim’s burning body in the city’s Busserine district, beside the words DZ Mafia.



They quickly became notorious for “score settling” gangland killings fuelled by an intense rivalry with Yoda gang.

Local cops counted 68 shootings in the first eight months of that year, 30 of which were fatal. In August 2023, there were six deaths in six days.

December 2025 saw one of the most chilling killings take place.

Children spotted the charred corpse of Adel, aged just 15, as they walked to school by a beach in Marseille.

A single bullet was lodged in his head and his killers had doused his lifeless body in petrol and set him on fire as a warning to rivals.

The bloodbath spread across the northern districts as drug peddlers exerted control of “lucrative” locations.

But a “turning point” came later that year, according to Fabrice, when 20-year-old Mehdi Kessaci was shot dead while parking his car in Marseille.

Investigators fear his killing was ordered as a brutal warning to his brother, Amine, an outspoken anti-drugs activist.



Fabrice said: “For the first time authorities became afraid – their violence was no longer contained within gangs.”

Fabrice founded French organisation Crim’HALT a decade ago to encourage authorities to work alongside victims of organised crime.

He said: “It is not just drug dealers and criminals being killed, there are so many innocent victims.”

At the same time DZ Mafia was diversifying, from drugs into extortion and protection rackets.

But it is the cartel’s presence on social media that surprises and concerns Fabrice.

He said: “They are recruiting child killers on TikTok and Telegram by sending out announcements offering money for a hit on someone.

“It’s a new generation of organised crime, taking the code of the Mexican cartels.”

Other TikTok posts show masked, black-clad men standing behind a makeshift altar covered with a white sheet inscribed with the words DZ Mafia.



These clips have been used by the gang to deny killings they have been blamed for.

Fabrice said: “They are like press conferences – but a terrorist group speaking to the state.

“‘We are DZ Mafia but it wasn’t us’. It’s incredible, we have not seen this before.”

In response to escalating violence France has intensified its crackdown on the group.

In early March, police launched Operation “Octopus” – which led to the arrest of 43 suspected high-ranking members.

During the raids, authorities seized assets valued at more than £3.4million (about $4.6million).

Despite resources deployed by the State, police, and justice system, DZ Mafia is extending its grip far beyond Marseille.

A recent cross-border money laundering probe seized over £34.81 million ($46.3 million) along a route across France and into Italy.



Fabrice said: “They are already expanding throughout France, taking control of territory. It is incredibly ambitious.”

Now a violent turf war in Brussels has been linked to the gang.

Last year it was revealed that two inmates were playing a leading role in the raging gang war blighting Belgium’s capital from behind prison walls using clandestine phones.

One of the men is said to lead a gang of at least 30 members in the Peterbos neighbourhood, which allegedly has links to DZ.

Through this alliance DZ Mafia allegedly aims to have the Peterbos gang take over the entire Brussels drug trade, local media reports.

While authorities in France clamp down on the gang, Fabrice says “judicial time is not on our side.”

The trial of six men accused of being key figures in DZ Mafia began in March.

The defendants face charges from a 2019 double murder that authorities say was a calculated underworld hit.

Farid Tir, 29, and Mohamed Bendjaghlouli, were found with fatal gunshot wounds in a hotel room on August 30, 2019.

Among the six men currently standing trial are Amine Oualane and Gabriel Ory, who prosecutors claim to be the leading kingpins of DZ Mafia.



But the gang does not have one single boss, instead operating within a coalition of factions making it far more difficult for authorities to dismantle.

Fabrice said: “Trials are unacceptably long, sometimes taking years to hold these criminals to account.

“And in the meantime there is a catastrophic demand for cocaine that will continue feeding the gangs growth.”

News.title: Trump cancels Iran strikes at final moments after vowing to unleash WW2-level blitz on Tehran alongside Israel
News.content:
‘TERROR, STRENGTH & POWER’ Trump cancels Iran strikes at final moments after vowing to unleash WW2-level blitz on Tehran alongside Israel

DONALD Trump has cancelled strikes on Iran at the final moment after vowing he was “locked and loaded” to unleash a massive blitz.

In a Truth Social post the US President said he decided to cancel the attack after being able to “rapidly make a DEAL”.



The fresh agreement includes the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to “Iran’s nuclear threat”, he added.

It comes just hours after the US warned it citizens to flee the Middle East in the wake of intense strikes on Tehran.



In the post, Trump said the US was “locked and loaded and ready to go” at “levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II”.

But Iran “asked” the US to “hold off” on the attack as the rogue nation begged for a deal, Trump said.

News.title: Six arrested after man stabbed & rushed to hospital with ‘serious injuries to head and hand’
News.content:
STABBING PROBE Six arrested after man stabbed & rushed to hospital with ‘serious injuries to head and hand’

COPS have arrested six men after a man was reportedly stabbed in the street.

A 19-year-old man was found by police on London Road in Portsmouth just after 8pm on July 30.

He suffered “serious, but not life-threatening” injuries to his head and hand, according to officers.



The teenager was taken to hospital for treatment.



An investigation was launched which resulted in six people being arrested.

A 20-year-old man from Croydon was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent; an 18-year-old man from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent, and a 24-year-old man from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place.

A police spokesperson said: “They remain in police custody at this time and enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances.”

As the investigation progressed, three more men were arrested.

A 23-year-old man from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place; a 17-year-old boy from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent and a 17-year-old boy from Wolverhampton was arrested on suspicion of assault, wounding with intent and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place.

They have now been released from custody and will face no further action in relation to these arrests.

News.title: At least three dead & 5 injured after ‘gunman opens fire’ outside In-N-Out as cops hunt for ‘shooter still at large’
News.content:
THREE people have been killed after at least one gunman opened fire at an In-N-Out burger chain in Idaho – sparking a major manhunt.

A rifle-wielding suspect began shooting at victims in the drive-thru area of the restaurant.



Terrified bystanders were seen running for their lives across the car park as the suspect fired a large AR-style assault weapon.

Another possible shooter was seen firing a handgun, but it was not clear if they were a secondary gunman or a responding witness.



Idaho Falls city spokesperson Josh Palmer told NBC News that at least three people had lost their lives and five others were injured.

He could not confirm whether the shooter was among the deceased.



Bullets began ringing out at around 3pm local time, with shocking footage showing dozens of people fleeing for their lives.

The suspect drove up to the chain’s drive-thru before exiting a white vehicle and retrieving a rifle from his trunk.



The man, wearing a black T-shirt and blue trousers, was seen walking through the car park before shooting through a Tesla‘s windscreen.

Twin Falls police confirmed they are responding to an active shooter situation near the In-N-Out.

Officers have been scouring a hotel that overlooks the complex where the shooting broke out.

They said that they would be enforcing a lockdown and closing multiple roads and bridges while they search for the suspect, urging people to avoid the area.

Idaho Governor Brad Little wrote on X: “Idahoans, join me in keeping the Twin Falls community in your prayers as law enforcement and first responders respond to an active shooter situation near In-N-Out.



“Please avoid the area and follow directions from law enforcement as they work to keep everyone safe.”

Attorney General Raul Labrador confirmed that cops were still searching for the suspect.

He said: “Praying for everyone in Twin Falls as first responders continue searching for the suspect near In-N-Out.

“Twin Falls Police, Idaho State Police, and fire and paramedic crews remain on scene working to secure the area.

“If you’re in the area, please listen to local authorities and stay away from In-N-Out and the surrounding streets so first responders can do their jobs.”



The FBI confirmed it would be assisting in the investigation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Authorities are yet to publicly identify the shooter or shooters, as well as a possible motive.

The investigation remains ongoing.

News.title: Two bikers rushed to hospital with serious injuries after horrific crash as air ambulance called to scene
News.content:
MOTORBIKE HORROR Two bikers rushed to hospital with serious injuries after horrific crash as air ambulance called to scene

TWO bikers were rushed to hospital after a major collision, with the air ambulance called to the scene.

The incident took place near Glossop on the A57 Snake Pass – one of the highest roads in the Peak District – on 4pm on Saturday.



Emergency services were called to the site and part of the road was cordoned off.

One rider in his 20s sustained severe injuries, which were not believed to be life-threatening.



The other rider was a man in his 70s, who escaped the crash without suffering serious injuries.

A spokesperson for Derbyshire Police said: “We were called to a report of a collision between two motorbikes on the A57 Snakes Pass close to Glossop just after 4pm today.



“Both riders were taken to hospital for treatment.

“A man in his 20s is understood to have sustained serious, but not life-threatening injuries, and a man in his 70s is not believed to be seriously hurt.”

News.title: Mother ‘scrolled on porn sites and watched TikToks’ as her six-month-old son was dying, cops say
News.content:
SICK 'NEGLECT' Mother ‘scrolled on porn sites and watched TikToks’ as her six-month-old son was dying, cops say

A MOTHER allegedly scrolled through TikTok and visited pornographic websites more than 30 times as her six-month-old son was dying, police say.

Tatiana Norman is accused of deliberately throwing little Jeremiah Peters into a playpen before failing to get him medical help as his condition deteriorated.



The tragic baby was eventually found unresponsive at Norman’s home on West Chestnut Drive in Lakeland, Florida, shortly before midnight on June 29.

Jeremiah was rushed to Lakeland Regional Hospital but was pronounced dead at 12.32am on June 30.



Police Chief Sammy Taylor Jr said the child may already have been dead for hours before his mum finally called 911.

Taylor said: “I think the child was probably deceased hours before she called us, just based on the evidence and the temperature of the body and the temperature a child should be.



“I think the child’s temperature when he got to the emergency room was 94, so I feel like he’d been dead for several hours by the time she decided to call us.”

Norman initially told cops she had put Jeremiah to bed while she prepared a bottle, only to return and find him lying on the tiled floor after falling from the bed.

But detectives say she later changed her story, claiming she had been sleeping beside Jeremiah and her one-year-old when they may have rolled onto the baby.

An autopsy allegedly tore apart her accounts, finding injuries that did not match her explanations.



The examination also found an unexplained mark on Jeremiah’s thigh was not caused by hot bathwater, as Norman had claimed, but by “a more significant thermal event.”

Police say Norman eventually confessed to a series of shocking incidents on the day her son died.

According to an arrest affidavit, she told detectives that at around 9am she accidentally dropped Jeremiah face-first while reaching for a remote.

Rather than seeking urgent medical help, she allegedly searched online for concussion symptoms and monitored him at home.

Jeremiah then allegedly suffered another brutal fall when Norman’s one-year-old climbed into his rocking bassinet, causing it to topple over.



Police say the infant again landed face-first.

Norman also allegedly gave detectives a string of conflicting explanations for the burn on Jeremiah’s leg.

She initially blamed laundry detergent used by the baby’s father before admitting she had spilled microwave noodle broth onto his leg, according to the affidavit.

The document stated: “Norman advised she contacted Jeremiah’s pediatrician via telephone regarding that injury.

“It should be noted that the injury to Jeremiah’s leg is not consistent with any of the statements provided to law enforcement.”



Then, at around 1pm, police say Norman became overwhelmed by her crying children.

Detectives allege she “intentionally ‘tossed’ or ‘threw’ Jeremiah into a playpen from a standing position” from several feet away.

During her explanation, Norman reportedly demonstrated both an underhand and an overhand throw.

Police say Jeremiah slammed his back and head into the playpen, which had no cushion on its base.

Norman allegedly told detectives that her son did not cry after the impact.



Taylor said: “When she threw the infant into the playpen, a visceral and obvious reaction of curling his hands and pulling his hands up, I think that’s probably when the significant injury occurred.”

Jeremiah then allegedly became increasingly lethargic and drank less formula, but police say Norman still did not seek medical attention.

Her phone activity has now emerged as a chilling part of the investigation.

At 2.10pm, Norman allegedly searched Google for “baby feels cold”, followed minutes later by “what happens when baby had concussion in Florida”.

Yet police say she then switched to TikTok, watching two videos including a cooking clip at 3.34pm.



The affidavit states she returned to the cooking video repeatedly until 4.23pm.

Even more disturbingly, detectives say Norman accessed pornographic websites more than 30 times while Jeremiah’s condition continued to worsen.

The baby’s father later texted Norman at around 10pm asking for a photograph of his son, but allegedly received no response before discovering Jeremiah was no longer breathing.

The Polk County Medical Examiner’s Office said Jeremiah might have survived if he had received medical attention immediately, according to the affidavit.

The affidavit states she described feeling depressed and having suicidal thoughts, as well as a history of PTSD and borderline personality disorder.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Norman has been charged with one count of aggravated child abuse.

The charges could be upgraded as prosecutors continue their investigation.

News.title: Britain must kick out overseas criminals or slash foreign aid until their countries take them back
News.content:
Kick out overseas crims, or slash aid

LAW-ABIDING Brits are sick of seeing vicious crooks walk away from prison less than halfway through their sentences.

It is a disgrace that prison overcrowding has led to Labour’s open door policy for thousands of villains who will never serve their terms in full.



Andy Burnham has slammed the brakes on the scheme after the outrage over the potential early release of the two killers of PC Andrew Harper.

But it is a scramble against the clock. Around 6,000 lags were due to go free from September 2 under the plan.



Without that, prison bosses warn jails will start running out of space in November.

So since every cell place counts, why are we still hosting more than 10,000 foreign prisoners?

It is insane that thousands who should be serving time in their own country’s jails are taking up scarce places in our own.

Successive governments have failed to cut numbers of overseas inmates.

The row over deporting grooming gang leader Shabir Ahmed to Pakistan shows how unsuccessful we have been. But there is a bargaining chip we could use.

Two countries with large groups of their nationals in our prisons are India and Albania.



The former receives nearly £25million in foreign aid and the latter got £4million in 2025.

Neither should receive a penny in aid again until they take back their citizens from our crisis-hit jails.

Regulate funerals

ONE thing is clear from the trial of funeral home monster Robert Bush.

The Wild West culture surrounding this business must end for good.

Hundreds of mourning relatives had their lives ruined by the evil of one man.



But the freedom he enjoyed to hoodwink victims under a cloak of secrecy while siphoning off their cash can and should be stopped immediately.

The Government must step in and regulate the funeral business without delay.

Bush had a parlour and chapel under the same roof. Such madness can’t go on.

It gives twisted individuals a licence to act with impunity.

It’s full-time, Gianni

“A SHABBY, backroom, opaque deal.’’



We couldn’t agree more with Uefa’s assessment of Gianni Infantino’s shameful collapsed plan to sell the World Cup.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

With every day that passes the Fifa chief’s position gets weaker.

It’s time to blow the final whistle… with no extra-time.

News.title: Fugitive accused over Athens firebomb deaths worked at Gatwick duty free for six years
News.content:
GATWICK FUGITIVE Fugitive accused over Athens firebomb deaths worked at Gatwick duty free for six years

A FUGITIVE accused of being part of a fatal firebombing has been working at a Gatwick airport duty free shop for years.

Eleni Argyriou, 46, was arrested last month in connection with the attack on a bank in Athens in 2010 in which three people died.



She was held by officers from the National Extradition Unit at Gatwick as she was about to board a flight to her native Greece.

Argyriou is thought to have been living in Sussex for seven years.



According to her LinkedIn page, she has worked as a sales assistant at the World Duty Free Shop at Gatwick since April 2019.

Avolta, which operates the duty free business, and the airport declined to comment.



The day after her arrest she appeared at Westminster magistrates’ court and consented to her deportation.

Argyriou is now in custody and is due to be flown back by August 14.

She faces trial in Athens for three murders and domestic extremism.

Masked anarchists threw petrol bombs into the Marfin Bank, setting it ablaze, as tens of thousands protested during the Greek financial crisis in May 2010.



Around 30 workers were inside.

Most managed to flee but three clerks, including a pregnant lady, were trapped and died from asphyxia.

Greek prosecutors believe Argyriou was part of an anarchy group responsible.

Two 42-year-old men were arrested in Athens last month and are in custody awaiting trial.

Police are still trying to identify other suspects.



According to reports in Greece, the arrests followed the publication of a 117-page forensic report that provided evidence, including ­photos and videos, that helped to identify suspects.

It is also claimed that an anonymous email was sent to Greece’s organised crime squad naming Argyriou and the two men arrested.

She has previously said she would voluntarily return to prove her innocence.

The Crown Prosecution Service said Argyriou was accused by Greek authorities of “operational planning, joint action, and with a shared homicidal intent — thereby killing three individuals”.

News.title: 'I flogged my old Lego toys on eBay - now I rake in £300,000 a year while at college'
News.content:
'I flogged my old Lego toys on eBay - now I rake in £300,000 a year while at college'

EXCLUSIVE: Jamie says his JTB Collectables business raked in £300,000 across the last tax year, and after buying and accounting costs he was left with around £50,000 profit

View 6 Images Jamie Bell sold toys he'd 'grown out of' at age 13 (Image: Kennedy News/JTB Collectables)

A teenage college student claims he's flogged £300,000 worth of Lego figures on eBay in the last year.

‌



Jamie Bell sold toys he'd 'grown out of' at age 13 and quickly realised he could earn money from Lego pieces in particular. Now 18 years old, the teen buys kilos of the plastic toys online and from his contacts, in order to flog them to collectors or people selling them individually.

‌



On May 2, he sold a 95kg pile of Lego Star Wars figurines and claimed it to be the 'largest mini-figure lot ever listed on eBay worldwide'. The listing, which includes images of the bundle stacked on his parents' bedroom floor, began at £1 and was bought for an eye-watering £22,428 after 65 bids.

‌



View 6 Images Now 18 years old, the teen buys kilos of the plastic toys online (Image: Kennedy News/JTB Collectables)

Couple paid £37.5m by eBay after they were sent cockroaches and bloody pig mask READ MORE :

Jamie says his JTB Collectables business raked in £300,000 across the last tax year, and after buying and accounting costs he was left with around £50,000 profit.

The college student says he and his dad decided they needed to hire an accountant at age just 16 because his earnings were skyrocketing. He says he's now selling about 100kg of Lego per month using bulk sales and individual figure auctions online.

‌



View 6 Images He's made £300,000 in a single year (Image: Kennedy News/JTB Collectables)

Despite his side-hustle's success he doesn't want to make it his full-time job and plans to commit his time to studying History at university next year.

Jamie, from Wandsworth, South London, said: "It's exciting watching the auctions because sometimes someone will pop in right at the end and increase the price by a few thousand pounds. I'd say 40% of people are huge collectors with a lot of disposable income and 60% would be resellers who could take months selling them individually.

‌



View 6 Images Despite his success, Jamie doesn't want his side-hustle to become a full-time job (Image: Kennedy News/JTB Collectables)

"I keep them [the figures] on the floor in big cardboard boxes at my parents' house. I had to get an accountant at 16 but I probably needed one at 15.

"By age 15 my huge bundles were selling well because nobody else was doing it and I realised people would buy them to sell each one individually and I could be their supplier. The profit margins are never certain and the cost was quite high so it's not the listing I've made the most profit on but I think the benchmark of the size was more important than the profit.

‌



View 6 Images Jamie sold two Lego Batman figures for £751 (Image: Kennedy News/JTB Collectables)

"My dad helps with the packing and admin and [my parents will be supportive] but it's up to me because they'll only do so much. It's my side-hustle or business. My mum was shocked because she thought it was a little resale thing and didn't know it had grown into a proper business.

"I could make it my full-time job but for career stability I'd like to have a profession as well. These big sales have become normal now and I save most of the money for my first home and put it in an ISA."

‌



View 6 Images Jamie's 95kg pile of Lego Star Wars figurines sold for an eye-watering amount

Jamie says he earned a few hundred pounds from selling his own toys then bought a bundle to sell on individually for double the money at aged 14. The teen says he earned £100,000 in revenue in the 24/25 tax year before tripling it for the 25/26 tax year.

He says he's still a collector himself but will buy some high-value figures instead of picking any from the bundles he plans to sell. His £22,000 bundle was bought by a UK eBay user who he believes to be a reseller aiming to profit from selling the items individually.

Article continues below

Other listings on his eBay account show other large bundles sold for £4,458 and two Lego Batman figures sold for £751.

News.title: Everything to watch for when hiring a car abroad so you don’t get hit with massive bill
News.content:
Everything to watch for when hiring a car abroad so you don’t get hit with massive bill

Consumer rights expert Martyn James explains everything you need to know about the horrors of hiring a car

View Image Hiring a car gives you freedom on holiday - but it can go wrong (Image: Getty Images)

There are certain types of businesses that have very, very bad reputations. You know the ones!

‌



You mention a problem to a friend or a relative and they say: “Yes! That happened to me too!” I’m looking at you, package delivery companies, social media shops… and car hire companies.

‌



Every year, as tired travellers head off on their holidays, I’m flooded with complaints from readers about the horrors of hiring a car.

‌



From ‘upgrades’ that end up costing a fortune, disputes of full or empty fuel tanks on return, extortionate insurance policies and – the biggie – thousands of pounds vanishing from credit cards for non-existent damage claims, the sector’s reputation is pretty poor.

I must add that in all fairness, not all companies are bad. But because of the reputation of the worst offenders, it makes sense to be prepared for the cons, so you can be pleasantly surprised if everything goes like a dream!

Here’s my guide on everything you need to watch for.

‌



Do your research before you travel

Always research car hire prices at home before committing to a specific business. When you look on the comparison websites, you see that there’s a huge competitiveness among the hire firms to give the lowest quote. But this is often achieved by raising excess fees and adding on additional costs in other areas. So remember that the cheapest policies might actually be more expensive when you factor in all the catches.

Speak to friends and family about the good experiences they’ve had with specific brands. Bear in mind though that car hire companies often operate in different ways in different countries. So a good experience in Milton Keynes might not result in the same service in Malaga with the same firm.

Beware airport fatigue

Wherever possible, don’t book a car on arrival at an airport, station or ferry terminal. You’ll be tired, possibly a bit fed up, the kids might be playing up, and you all just want to get to your destination. Car hire firms know this and are aware that you might not scrutinise the contract too closely. Even when you’ve pre booked, you might suddenly find that you’re being charged extra for things that weren’t mentioned when you booked. Understanding all the costs associated with car hire contracts is essential, so take your time and don’t be rushed.

‌



Avoid upgrades and confirm the booking the day before

A common complaint in the last few years relates to upgrades and unavailable vehicles. While getting a nicer vehicle for the same price might be a good thing, you may be expected to buy a new insurance policy to cover damage and repairs, which could set you back £200 to £300. You may also find that your excess fees have increased as the vehicle is worth more money.

At the other end of the scale is the downgrade due to a lack of available vehicles. When my good friends Aki and Tsukasa visited France last year, they had booked an automatic vehicle, but on arrival were given a manual car with a gearstick – which they’d never driven. This is not only a breach of contract but it’s fundamentally dangerous. So check 48 to 24 hours beforehand that the vehicle you have booked is available and will be retained for you. Make it clear that you will not accept an alternative and get it in writing.

Make sure you question the credit card payment

Countless people get caught out by the car hire credit card rule. In order to hire a vehicle the majority of firms will insist the driver must pay the fee and deposit on a credit card in their name .

‌



But why do you have to have a credit card to book a hire car? Or why does it have to be in the driver’s name? It’s all down to liability if something goes wrong. The credit card you use will need to have a set amount of credit on it before the car hire company will even let you leave with the vehicle – and they’ll check you’ve got it too. Frustratingly, many firms ‘ring fence’ a deposit for excess fees for damage too, which will mean you can’t use that credit for the duration of your trip.

This is because the company will automatically debit your account for any damage or contract dispute costs as soon as it concludes you’re liable. The money comes off your credit card without you having the right to argue – though you should receive written notification of the debit – and then you’ll be forced to make a complaint to get your cash back.

Damage excess fees

When you are conducting your research, always look for the damage or collision ‘excess’ fee. This is what you have to pay if there’s a crash or minor damage to the vehicle that needs to be repaired. It’s not unusual for this to be £1,000 or over – despite the fact that the firm will have its own insurance.

‌



Leaving aside the sheer size of these excess fees, the main source of frustration when it comes to car hire disputes is over allegations of damage. If the car hire firm decides that repairs are necessary to the vehicle as a result of your actions, they can conclude you are liable for the repairs and debit your credit card. It’s not unheard of for people to be charged £1,000 or more for a minor scratch on a bumper. Astoundingly, a representative for the industry once admitted during a radio interview I was taking part in that the repairs might not even be made!

So if you remember one thing from this article, make it this: Before you drive off you need to photograph and/or video the car from all sides , check the boot and glove compartment along with the interior. The hire firm will mark up existing damage on the car on a diagram and give you a copy (photo that too). Make them mark down everything that you’ve spotted too.

Insurance overcharging

Car hire firms will tell you that you will need to take out an insurance policy to cover the excess fee. This is vital, so don’t drive off without a policy covering you for the excess. Many firms are insisting that you have to take out their own policies. Yet an excess fee policy bought from the car hire firm can cost £300 or more! However, you can buy cheaper better policies in the UK for just £30 to £40. You will need to make sure that the policy covers the make and model of the vehicle you are hiring.

‌



I’ve heard from many readers who have told me that the car hire firm stated they had to take out the car hire firm’s own policy. This is absolutely not the case. In the UK and EU, selling insurance is a regulated activity, which means you can go to the Financial Ombudsman if you feel you have been misled by the business in to taking out their policy. Laws vary around the world though.

Petrol, mileage and endless extras

Some car hire firms have ludicrously complicated rules about petrol and returning the car. Some will insist on a full tank, others on a half-filled tank, which doesn’t make much sense. Failure to follow the requirements can result in extra charges.

Many of the contracts I’ve reviewed bill you for mileage over a certain amount. So if you’re driving around a foreign country talking in the sites as you go, then you could find it’s more expensive than you expected.

‌



Finally, there are a bewildering range of additional ‘add-on’ charges levied by some car hire firms. These can include an ‘out of hours’ pick up of the car, late arrival fees if your plane is late and extra administration charges. You will also usually have to pay more for everything from roof racks to child seats.

Making a complaint

If you’ve got a complaint about a car hire company, make a complaint to the business first in the country it’s based. This can be frustrating if you booked a car abroad because all the big brand names have branches in the UK too. Put your complaint in writing (email it if you can) explaining what went wrong and what you want them to do to sort it out.

If that doesn’t work the European Car Rental Conciliation Service (ECRCS) can help with cross border car hire complaints – but only in the EU. The European Consumer Centres Network (ECRCS) can help you for free if you’re struggling.

‌



In the UK, The British Vehicle Rental and Leasing Association (BVRLA) can help with complaints.

If the complaint is about an insurance policy sold by the car hire firm, there are ombudsman schemes for banking and insurance abroad and you can find a list at FIN-NET.

You may be able to ‘charge back’ or claim for any money back that’s been taken in breach of the contract. This can be a problem because car hire contracts are written to allow the firms to debit you straight away for any ‘damage’ or ‘costs’ you’ve incurred even if you dispute this. It’s definitely worth attempting this though. Payments taken on a credit card could also be disputed through making a section 75 claim under the Consumer Credit Act to your card provider too.

Article continues below

Your car hire checklist to avoid being ripped off when hiring a car abroad

Book in advance, compare prices and read all the documents before you travel.

Check the excess fees – the higher they are, the more you’ll pay if the firm claims there is damage.

Take out a damage/collision insurance policy (sometimes called ‘zero excess’). Don’t buy the car hire policy – online options are much cheaper.

Ask about the deposit. If the firm ‘ring-fences’ a deposit, you can’t spend that money. If they debit your card and refund you on returning the vehicle, find out how long it takes for the credit to come back and if you can pay in the local currency, so you don’t lose out on exchange rates.

Video the car from all angles. A representative from the firm will sign the car out with you. Make sure they write down every mark or scuff on their documents and photo the car from all angles too (check the boot). Do the same when you return the car.

Keep all the paperwork and receipts for things like petrol.

If you are in an accident, call the police and get copies of all documentation. Make sure you’ve checked with the hire firm what their procedures are too.

News.title: 'I bought a coat I'd wanted all winter for £11.99 - it taught me a money lesson I'll never forget'
News.content:
'I bought a coat I'd wanted all winter for £11.99 - it taught me a money lesson I'll never forget'

'I buy coats, boots and cold weather essentials months before I need them and it has transformed both my wardrobe and my budget'

View Image Vicky Parry had her eye on a particular Zara coat (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

There are some purchases that stay with you. Not because they were expensive, but because you simply can't believe what you paid. Mine happened last week.

‌



I'd wandered into Zara without any real intention of shopping when I spotted a waxed cape I'd admired all last winter. I'd picked it up several times over the colder months but never quite managed to justify buying it. It was £59.99.

‌



This time, it was sitting on the sale rail. The price? £11.99. Needless to say, it came home with me.

‌



It wasn't my only bargain either. A few days earlier I'd picked up a pair of quality men's leather boots in the John Lewis sale. They had originally been priced at well over £100 , but I paid less than £40 .

Get the best deals and tips from Mirror Money WHATSAPP GROUP: Get money news and top deals straight to your phone by joining our Money WhatsApp group here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

This isn’t anything new either, shopping out of season isn’t a new concept for frugal people. It is however good to remember that now is a good time to get that winter coat: Because with the energy prices due to rise – we will thank ourselves later on.

‌



So here is the reminder: The best time to buy winter clothes isn't when the weather turns cold.

It's when everyone else is buying sandals.

We all shop at exactly the wrong time

Most of us don't think about buying a coat until we're cold. We don't replace our boots until they leak. We don't look for knitwear until the first chilly morning reminds us we haven't got enough.

‌



It's perfectly understandable. The trouble is, millions of other shoppers are doing exactly the same thing. Retailers know this too.

Once demand returns in autumn, discounts become harder to find. New season collections arrive, full prices return and the best sizes disappear quickly.

By buying before you actually need something, you completely change the balance of power. Instead of shopping because you have to, you're shopping because the price is too good to ignore.

‌



The savings can be remarkable

The Zara cape wasn't an old design that had seen better days. It was simply last season's stock making way for the next collection.

Exactly the same was true of the John Lewis boots. There was nothing wrong with them. They weren't seconds. They weren't damaged. The store simply needed the shelf space.

Come October, boots of that quality are much more likely to be selling close to their original price because people suddenly need them.

‌



That's why shopping ahead often lets you buy better quality for less money.

I'd much rather own a pair of boots that originally retailed for more than £100 but cost me under £40 than spend the same amount on a cheaper pair that might not survive the winter.

The retailers worth checking now

If you're tempted to start thinking a season ahead, these are some of the places I'd be looking over the next few weeks.

‌



Zara

The sale rails can be a goldmine for coats, jackets, boots and statement pieces that were full price only a few months ago. My £11.99 waxed cape is proof that it's worth taking a look.

John Lewis

‌



Don't assume premium means expensive. Seasonal sales can dramatically reduce the price of quality leather boots, winter coats and accessories, making investment pieces much more affordable.

Mango

Ideal for stylish coats, knitwear and leather boots, particularly once summer sales are in full swing.

‌



Marks & Spencer

If you're looking for classic winter staples that won't date, it's well worth browsing the clearance section.

Mountain Warehouse

‌



One of the best places to find bargains on waterproof jackets, walking boots, fleeces and insulated coats while demand is low.

Sports Direct

Branded puffer jackets, walking boots and winter footwear are often heavily reduced before autumn arrives.

‌



Next Clearance

Particularly useful for families looking to spread the cost of children's winter wardrobes.

Schuh

‌



Worth keeping an eye on if you're after premium footwear, with seasonal reductions often making quality brands far more affordable.

TK Maxx

Stock changes constantly, but that's exactly why it's worth popping in regularly. You never know what winter bargains might appear.

‌



Vinted

Summer can be one of the best times to buy nearly new winter clothing, as many people clear out wardrobes to make room for lighter clothes.

The biggest saving isn't always the discount

What I've realised is that the biggest benefit isn't necessarily saving 50% or 60%. It's avoiding what I call the panic purchase.

‌



Every year, the same thing happens. The first cold snap arrives. You discover your coat zip has broken. The children have outgrown last year's coats.

Your boots suddenly let in water. Now you need replacements immediately. You haven't got time to compare prices or wait for another sale. You buy whatever fits and whatever's available.

Planning ahead removes that pressure completely.

‌



Your budget starts to catch up

One of the biggest changes I've noticed is that my spending now feels much more manageable.

Instead of buying school uniforms, winter coats, Christmas presents and everything else within a few hectic months, I spread those costs across the year.

If I see something I'll genuinely need in a few months' time and it's an exceptional price, I buy it. Little by little, my budget has caught up.

‌



Rather than constantly replacing things at the last minute, I'm quietly ticking them off the list long before I actually need them.

It feels organised at first. Before long, it simply becomes a habit.

Think one season ahead

This approach works for almost everything.

‌



Right now I'm keeping an eye out for:

Winter coats

Leather and walking boots

Waterproof jackets

Children's winter clothing

Hats, scarves and gloves

Thermal base layers

Electric blankets

Hot water bottles

And the same trick works the other way too. When summer comes to an end, I'll be looking for bargains on barbecues, garden furniture and outdoor entertaining.

Article continues below

Thinking just one season ahead has probably saved me hundreds of pounds over the years. It isn't about filling your wardrobe with things you don't need.

It's about buying things you were always going to buy anyway, just at the moment when retailers are most keen to sell them.

That £11.99 Zara cape reminded me of something I'll never forget. Sometimes the easiest way to save money isn't cutting back. It's simply changing when you shop.

News.title: 'I stay hydrated, reduce bloating and ease digestion with health-boosting drink'
News.content:
'I stay hydrated, reduce bloating and ease digestion with health-boosting drink'

Many people are struggling to stay properly hydrated with all the hot weather we're having in the UK. If that's you, Social News Assistant Editor Samantha Bartlett recommends one drink with other health-boosting benefits too

I stay hydrated, reduce bloating and get better digestion by consuming 1 drink

With the UK baking in hot weather all summer with it recently experiencing its fourth heatwave, many people are struggling to stay properly hydrated. If you find yourself feeling thirsty, have dark-coloured urine, are confused or dizzy and have a rapid heart rate, these are all signs that your may be dehydrated and need to drink more.

‌



Because water is essential for your body to function properly, a lack of fluids impacts multiple systems at once. The indicators vary depending on the severity of the fluid loss and the age of the individual. Of course, you can just stick to normal water, however if you're looking for a tasty drink that will keep you hydrated as well as bring other health benefits, then I have just the thing for you - mint water.

‌



Mint water is an excellent, low-calorie beverage that boosts hydration, supports digestion, and naturally freshens breath. While it is not a concentrated medicine, the natural oils like menthol found in peppermint and spearmint leaves seep into the water to provide subtle, science-backed wellness advantages.

‌



View Image I fill up my £4 B&M water dispenser to have throughout the day (Image: Samantha Bartlett)

Menthol relaxes the muscles of your digestive tract. This helps reduce mild bloating, gas, and stomach heaviness after meals.

Mint leaves also possess natural antibacterial properties. Drinking the water helps inhibit odour-causing bacteria in the mouth.

‌



It's great for those watching their weight too as it serves as a zero-sugar, calorie-free alternative to juices or sodas. This helps reduce overall daily calorie intake.

Mint contains phytonutrients and antioxidants like rosmarinic acid also These compounds assist your body in combating oxidative stress.

The natural, uplifting aroma of mint can further focus and help lower feelings of stress and mental fatigue too.

‌



Ever since the heatwaves have started, I've begun filling up a small water dispenser with mint and putting it on my desk daily to drink from while I work.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

I got my jug for £4 in B&M and it's so easy to take around with you. We also use it for picnics, however you could take it to the office with you, to the beach, park or wherever.

Article continues below

It's definitely an easy way of getting in the fluid while it's hot, even if you're busy, as it feels like a nice treat thanks to its minty flavour.

With the hot weather currently continuing like it is in the UK, I can't see myself putting my water dispenser away for a while, that's for sure.

News.title: Tragic end for man, 21, after house party descends into 'all-out brawl'
News.content:
Tragic end for man, 21, after house party descends into 'all-out brawl'

Local residents reported seeing chaotic and violent scenes spilling out onto the street - police were called out to a 'disturbance' in the early hours of the morning

View 2 Images Police and forensic teams at the scene after the 'brawl'

A 21-year-old man has succumbed to his injuries after a house party descended into an 'all-out brawl' on the street.

‌



The youngster died nearly one week after being seriously injured during the incident at a short-term rental house on Orchard Avenue in the Logan suburb of Bahrs Scrub in Australia on Sunday, July 26.

‌



According to reports, the party was gatecrashed and this led to Queensland Police being called out to a 'disturbance' near the property. The force said they found “significant damage” throughout the street, including to several cars and a home.

‌



The 21-year-old man from Redbank Plains died in hospital on Saturday, August 1 from serious wounds. He was catastrophically injured after he was allegedly bashed in the fight that spilled onto the street. By the time officers arrived, the aftermath of the disturbance stretched across the street.

Police said they found “significant damage” throughout the street, including to several cars and a home. The young man was taken to the Princess Alexandra Hospital in Brisbane where he died on Saturday.

View 2 Images Some cars on the street were also targeted (Image: 7News)

‌



Residents say fighting and disorder spilled through the estate, with reports suggesting two groups had been involved.

Footage from CCTV appears to show a man running away from the scene down the street at about 2.47am.

Logan Crime Group Detective Inspector Ian Galpin last week said an “all-out brawl” broke out between two rival groups - aged between 18 and 21 years old - after one crashed a party.

‌



“This was a targeted attack and there is no ongoing threat to the wider community,” Inspector Galpin said.

“It appears to be a short-term accommodation rental property where some sort of party was occurring, and then at some stage in the night a second group arrived.

“Our inquiries suggest the second group was known to the occupants of the rental, and a conflict has begun, which kicked off quite a violent disturbance.”

Article continues below

Several vehicles were left with smashed windows and dents, while a nearby home also suffered shattered windows.

Police have said investigations remain ongoing and are urging anyone with information to come forward and assist with their investigation.

News.content:
North London festival issues statement after several people injured due to 'major incident'

Ghana Party in the Park orgnaisers have spoken out following a "major incident" at the event yesterday.

‌



Police have been called to a festival in London on Saturday evening as several people have been left injured.

‌



Met Police in Barnet said: "Officers are at Copthall Playing Fields where Ghana Party in the Park has been cancelled after an overcrowding issue at the entrance saw several people sustain non-life threatening injuries. Speculation about a stabbing is inaccurate. Please help us by avoiding the area."

‌



View 2 Images Copthall Playing Fields (Image: google maps)

The festival organisers have now issued a lengthy statement shortly before midnight last night in which they clarify the speculation surrounding a stabbing and deaths.

In a statement shared on Facebook the event organisers said: "Following the unfortunate incident at today's event, we wish to provide an update regarding the abrupt closure of Ghana in the Park. The decision to close the festival was made solely on the grounds of health and safety.

The police and council officers are on site, please help us by avoiding the area."

News.title: I asked legal experts what to do about neighbours' pets pooing in my garden — I was dead wrong
News.content:
I asked legal experts what to do about neighbours' pets pooing in my garden — I was dead wrong

From keeping a journal to taking legal action, experts have revealed exactly what your rights are - and the steps you should take - if a neighbour's dog or cat keeps fouling in your garden

View 4 Images No matter how cute your neighbour's pets are, you don't want them using your garden as a toilet (Image: Lesia Kapinosova via Getty Images)

If you take pride in your garden, there are few things more frustrating than stepping outside to find a neighbour's pet has been using it as a toilet. Whether it's a cat treating your flowerbeds as its own personal litter tray or a dog leaving unwanted deposits on your lawn, the problem can quickly become a source of real tension between neighbours - which is never pleasant.

‌



But what can you actually do about it - and does the law offer you any protection? I asked a panel of legal experts to spell out your rights and the steps you should take. There was one thing that came as such a surprise to me, but the majority of the experts all agreed that there's one thing you should try to do in basically every situation.

‌



View 4 Images It can be so irritating when a neighbour's pet messes up your garden (Image: Getty)

‌



The rules are different for cats and dogs

I had assumed that there would be a one-size-fits-all when it comes to pets, but this isn't the case at all.

Manjinder Kaur Atwal, Director of Housing and Property Litigation at Duncan Lewis Solicitors, explained: "Under UK law, cats enjoy a legal 'right to roam.' Because of this, owners are not generally held legally liable if their cat wanders into private gardens or fouls outdoors. Homeowners cannot trap, harm, or relocate a neighbour's cat, as doing so could constitute animal cruelty or criminal damage under the Animal Welfare Act 2006.

"Dogs are a different matter entirely. Dog owners have a statutory duty to clean up after their pets in public spaces, often backed by Public Spaces Protection Orders (PSPOs) enforced by local councils, which can carry fixed penalty notices. Furthermore, if the fouling occurs in communal areas—such as shared residential corridors, courtyards, or gardens—it likely breaches the terms of the neighbour's tenancy agreement or leasehold rules prohibiting nuisance behaviour."

‌



In short, if a cat is the problem, your legal options are more limited - but that does not mean you are entirely without recourse.

Start by talking to your neighbour

Regardless of whether it is a cat or a dog causing the problem, every expert we spoke to gave the same first piece of advice: keep it civil and speak to your neighbour before doing anything else.

David Gammill, trial attorney and the Founder of Gammill Law Accident & Injury Lawyers, urged people not to go in all guns blazing. He said: "From my experience as a lawyer, I would not begin with legal threats. Start with a polite and honest conversation. The owner may not know what their animal is doing. Explain what has happened and ask them to help prevent it from happening again."

‌



It sounds straightforward, but it is the step that most people either skip or handle badly - and that can make things far worse down the line.

View 4 Images Most people are reasonable and will be happy to help (Image: Getty)

Keep a record of every incident

Before you approach your neighbour - or certainly before you go any further - make sure you are documenting everything. Benson Varghese, a Board Certified Criminal Lawyer, stressed the importance of building a clear paper trail.

‌



He said: "The first thing that homeowners suffering from a long-lasting problem should do is to keep a journal of the situation with pictures or video evidence. Having a clear example of the ongoing problem will be much more effective compared to a one-off case. Usually, before any legal action is taken, mediation is the preferable way to settle a dispute, as it often proves to be quicker and cheaper."

Put it in writing if talking does not work

If a conversation with your neighbour fails to resolve the situation, the next step is to follow up in writing. Sending a formal letter serves two purposes: it makes clear to the owner that the problem has been raised, and it creates a record that could prove valuable if matters escalate further.

According to Everett Lupton from Slaughter and Lupton, this paper trail is crucial. He said: "If speaking to the owner does not work, the homeowner can send a short and polite written request. This also creates a record showing that the owner was told about the problem."

‌



View 4 Images The rules differ slightly for dogs and cats (Image: Getty)

Legal action should always be a last resort

All of the specialists I consulted agreed that taking a neighbour to court should be an absolute last resort. Not only is litigation costly and time-consuming, but it can permanently damage what might otherwise be a repairable relationship.

Mediation services are available in most areas and can help both parties reach an agreement without the need for formal legal proceedings.

Article continues below

Don't harm the animals

Some of the experts suggested safe and humane ways you can try to deter animals from entering your garden, but they must not hurt them in any way.

These included pet-safe barriers, citrus peels, a low fence, motion-activated sprinklers, or adding gravel or pebbels to flowerbeds.

You can also try to keep any soil around your garden as damp as possible, which some cats are said to dislike.

News.title: Three killed after bomb detonated at Moscow restaurant, state media say
News.content:
At least three people have been killed and 21 injured after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russian state media reports, quoting security officials.

The blast happened at about 20:00 local time (17:00 GMT) on Kudrinskaya square near the city centre.

The National Anti-Terrorist Committee said a woman carrying the explosives tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard.

The device detonated, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor to the Balzi Rossi restaurant, which had been holding a private function.

Authorities have not said who they believe was the target, but many Muscovites will suspect a link to the war in Ukraine.

In recent years, several senior Russian military figures have been assassinated in and around the Russian capital. Moscow has blamed Kyiv for those attacks.

Initial reports said the blast happened in the establishment's kitchen but the restaurant later issued a statement saying "there was a problem outside".

The restaurant is located in one of Moscow's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers, with roads around the square briefly closed.

Dozens of cyclists had been gathering nearby for an evening ride through the city but the event was cancelled.

Video released by Russia's RIA news agency showed heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene, which had been closed off to members of the public.

News.title: A bruising 24 hours - what next for Fifa and under-pressure Infantino?
News.content:
The quickest route for Infantino's exit would be for the Swiss to resign, like his predecessor Sepp Blatter did in 2015.

But Infantino still retains support and he could try to hold out until March, when he is up for re-election for a fourth and final term as president.

What other avenues are open?

The Fifa Council could try to force Infantino's hand through an emergency meeting.

Such a gathering would be triggered if 19 of the 37 Fifa Council members call for one.

Uefa has nine members, AFC has seven, Concacaf five, Africa has six, Conmebol five and Oceania three. It is completed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.

BBC Sport understands there are some doubts that the 19 votes could be achieved.

If they do get to 19, the meeting must take place within two weeks and the Fifa Council could call on Infantino to tender his resignation. But he could simply refuse to do so.

It would, however, add further pressure.

The next step would be an extraordinary congress of the 211 Fifa member associations, which would be held if one-fifth, or 43 associations, "make such a request in writing".

So Uefa, which has 55 nations, can trigger the extraordinary congress whenever it wishes.

That would take a minimum of two months from the point it is triggered, but more likely three months, and there is no guarantee of success.

In effect, it would be a de facto election without there being another candidate as 106 votes would be needed to pass the vote of no confidence.

Uefa has 55, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10.

Africa, Conmebol and Oceania have not criticised Infantino's plan.

So could Uefa get to 106? In total, 136 countries officially rejected the investment plan, but voting to reject an idea is not the same as voting to kick Infantino out.

Of the 136, Qatar have already publicly backed him and Mexico have distanced themselves from the joint Concacaf statement.

Which leaves finding a suitable candidate to fight the election in March.

Infantino stood unopposed when he was re-elected in 2019 and 2023 and if someone wants to battle him for the position, the deadline to announce their candidacy is 18 November.

News.title: Emotional Kerr delivers moment Glasgow 2026 has waited for with men's mile gold
News.content:
There were no pacers. No wave lights. No declarations about what time he would run or what record he would beat. This was a Saturday night scrap - Glasgow rules - and Josh Kerr wasn't going to let anyone beat him in that fight.

Not his childhood pal and Scotland team-mate Jake Wightman. Not the Australian prodigy Cam Myers. Not the former Olympic silver medallist Timothy Cheruiyot.

This Commonwealth Games men's mile was his race, in his country, in front of his people. This gold medal really meant something.

Kerr's explosion of joy after he crossed the line and swaddled himself in a Saltire - having conducted the crowd during his final few strides - made that clear.

And so did his halting attempts to sing along with Flower of Scotland, the 28-year-old repeatedly stopping to bite his lip before wiping away tears from each eye.

"We rush through these moments so quickly," Kerr told BBC Sport Scotland, having spent the best part of 45 minutes doing selfies and signatures. "So I was just telling myself to slow down.

"In my head, I was flashing through all the hard moments and realising that I've come a long way. And to have Flower of Scotland playing versus the GB national anthem, it's just different. Not many times in my career I'll ever have that."
