Sports.title: Xabi Alonso welcomes Mykhailo Mudryk back to Chelsea after 4-year doping ban cut short but admits Blues future unclear
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO is ready to welcome Mykhailo Mudryk with open arms after the end of his doping ban.

The Chelsea winger, 25, saw his four-year ban cut short this week after the FA and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved their disciplinary process against him following an appeal.



Mudryk tested positive for a of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, in 2024 and was slapped with a four year ban which he appealed with the Court of Arbitration for Sport this year.

The £62million forward has always maintained he never intentionally took the substance and changes to testing processes mean that, had the sample been taken today he would not have been reported as failing a drugs test.



Alonso, who had not expected to be working with Mudryk at Chelsea, confirmed the winger will join his squad for the next leg of their pre-season tour, in Hong Kong – despite the fact they have not spoken yet.

He said: “We are happy for him, especially for him, because probably we are not able to understand what he has been through in this time and how does he feel at the moment with the things that he had to cope with.

“We want that he feels part of a team, because he has been training on his own for a long time, and that we have the support from everyone, from the club, from the team-mates, from the staff, and for sure it will take time.

“Once he is with us, we will see how things develop.

“He is coming to Hong Kong, but I haven’t spoken to him yet.”

While many at Chelsea are excited to have Mudryk back, there is yet to be any clarity on his future at the club. He has a contract which runs for another five years, to 2031, but no decision has been made regarding his place in the squad for this season so far.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Alonso added: “We need to see, it’s too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it’s still early to tell.

“We were not expecting to have this great news at this moment, so we are very happy. We feel that he will be working with us.”

Chelsea ended the Australian leg of their tour with a late 2-1 defeat to London rivals Tottenham, who had ten men for almost the entire second half.

The Blues were without goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, who suffered a small knock.



Meanwhile, striker Joao Pedro is in talks over a new contract with the club, who are confident he will agree terms.

Pedro was a target for Barcelona at the start of the summer window, but Chelsea dubbed the Brazilian striker “untouchable” this summer and are pushing to tie him down further.

The forward only joined from Brighton last summer and the 24-year-old’s deal currently runs until 2033.

Sports.title: It’s a nice surprise to discover deep down football has a backbone.. but where’s this show of strength been hiding?
Sports.content:
WHAT a pleasant surprise to discover that­, buried deep, football actually does have a backbone.

It has been a delight to watch the sordid plan of suit-and-trainer wearing — creepy uncle at a wedding style — Gianni Infantino ­collapse around his own not-insignificant ears.



Uefa’s threat to boycott all but started the snowball.

Others attempted to look brave as they scrambled aboard the bandwagon which had been impressively assembled by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin.



But, sorry to complain at what is undoubtedly a triumph in the face of attempts to ­further b*****dise football, where has this sudden show of strength been when we needed it before?

Football has needed this newly-discovered might of its leaders and governing bodies time and time again.



Yet they have often been too cowardly or self-interested to stand up for supporters or those they represent.

Where were you when we needed to stop hydration breaks, half-time shows, Sunday night kick-offs or the omnipresence of that ‘Here we go’ touting wally on social media? It is true they are trivial points but all of them have got under the skin of fans at one point or another in recent years.

They are also a window to the serious problems which occur across the game, and all too often involve Fifa.

Belgium, Germany and Norway all publicly expressed their dismay over Fifa’s bowing to Donald Trump over Folarin Balogun’s one-match suspension for the United States’ round of 16 tie at the World Cup.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The decision to allow the striker to face Belgium was as dodgy as they come and they did not even try to hide that fact from us all.

As soon as the world learned that Infantino had taken calls from the US President — who just happened to have been the recipient of the first Fifa Peace Prize — a boycott would have been fitting.

It may seem extreme but Infantino’s spineless approach to Trump tainted his precious tournament.

What was the point of everyone else ­putting all that effort in if the hosts could fix any problems with a phone call to the man who is supposed to uphold and champion the rules?



Even though Belgium dismantled a Balogun-led USA 4-1 in the last-16, a united front at that moment — in the middle of a major tournament — would have made quite the statement, one Infantino and Fifa could not have stood up to.

Ticket prices, the barring of Sudanese referee Omar Artan from officiating at the tournament and the treatment of Iran were all largely greeted with a shrug from around the world.

Uefa quickly sailed in to appoint Artan to their Super Cup match between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa this month.

But that appeared to stem from a dislike of Infantino and a shot at a quick PR win rather than anything more moral.



A firm stance in Qatar at the World Cup four years ago would have been welcomed.

Instead the European nations’ show of support for human rights and the LGBTQ+ community fell down under the ­terrifying threat of a yellow card.

Those Fifa-approved armbands Harry Kane and his fellow captains ended up sporting in 2022 must have really warmed the hearts of the oppressed in the Middle East.

None of this is to say that Ceferin has not done well to gather the whole of Europe into what is undoubtedly a noble stand.



It would have been easy to swing the powerful nations behind a boycott but smaller federations tempted by Infantino’s promise of riches would have taken persuading.

This must set the tone for what Uefa has to stand for going forwards if it is to mean anything.

Let’s not forget this is a body which bowed to the Super League plotters by needlessly expanding the Champions League, dulling the experience for fans and piling more minutes into the legs of shattered stars.

Wake-up calls for those at the top are always helpful but did the collapse of the Super League really prevent Europe’s powerhouses from running the game? No.

Governing bodies must fight for football more often, otherwise their standing up to Fifa merely looks to be a move laced in self-interest by Uefa’s top man.



ED’S TOON’S BEST BET

A PAL in the pub recently lumped a few quid on Newcastle to get relegated at 40-1.

The fact he is a Sunderland fan may have tipped the scales but it is looking like a spot of superb foresight.

Just over a week on and that price has collapsed and may shorten further after the Toon effectively forced out their greatest asset in recent years.

Up against the expectations of a club the size of Newcastle, let alone their Saudi benefactors, Eddie Howe overdelivered given what he had to work with.

Chronic mismanagement and snail-paced decision-making made it an impossible task and, for his sake, it was wise to jump now.



Should his next club offer proper support, they will be very lucky indeed — as I would be if I listened to my mate’s tips more often.

RISEN FROM THE ASHES

THE drumbeat for Ben Stokes’ Ashes return appears to have started a little over a month after he retired.

All England fans want to see him in one last dust-up with the Aussies.

And given the narcissistic way he left the international stage, they may well get their wish — albeit not as captain.



Stokes will not be able to resist the storyline of riding back into the Test side next year to beat Australia.

FANS IN A MUD-DLE

CONFIRMATION that he is allowed to start playing football again will have been a delight to Mykhailo Mudryk after his doping ban.

The news was celebrated by some Chelsea supporters as if the Ukrainian would return like a new mega-money signing, a fresh star for Xabi Alonso to work with.

Have they forgotten just how hopeless the winger was at times?

Ten goals in 73 appearances does not scream superstar.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

I watched him play ten minutes of a charity match at Stamford Bridge — and he even struggled in that.

Those fans may soon recall why they were not too bothered by his suspension in the first place.

Sports.title: Arsenal in classy gesture after fans left fuming by £7 PPV for Girona pre-season friendly suffering technical glitch
Sports.content:
ARSENAL made their pre-season friendly against Girona FREE to watch after a technical issue stopped fans from streaming the scheduled pay-per-view offering.

The Gunners had advertised the fixture to buy for £6.99 prior to kick-off.



Supporters could also purchase a £14.99 bundle which gives them access to stream four pre-season fixtures.

However, many viewers missed the first half of the Girona match after being unable to log on to the club app or website.



Several fans took to social media to complain.

And at half-time, Arsenal responded by making the match free to view on YouTube.



A statement from the club read: “Arsenal supporters, apologies for the inconvenience. We’re working through some issues on Arsenal.com and The Arsenal App.

“Tonight’s game is now being streamed for free on our YouTube channel.”

The Gunners went on to win the match 4-1 against Girona.

Kai Havertz opened the scoring after latching onto a brilliant through ball from Max Dowman and slotting his shot into the bottom corner.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

New signing Christos Tzolis then scored a debut goal from the edge of the box to make it two.

Arnau Martinez got one back for the hosts just after the break, but Dowman restored the two-goal advantage moments later.

And Gabriel Jesus came off the bench to make it four.

Marli Salmon, Andre Harriman-Annous and Ceadach O’Neill were among the academy stars to appear on the night.

The Gunners next face Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday.

Sports.title: England wag Megan Pickford sparks fury with ‘offensive’ Princess Diana post as fans caught ‘off guard’ by comments
Sports.content:
ENGLAND World Cup Wag Megan Pickford has referenced Princess Diana in a TikTok about seatbelt safety.

Megan, 33, married to 32-year-old Three Lions and Everton goalie Jordan, was posting during her trip to Ibiza via private jet.



She captioned the video: “I love wearing my seatbelt in every environment.

If it can go wrong for Princess D it can go wrong for any of us.”



A comment said: “The Princess Diana bit caught me off guard.”

Diana died on August 31, 1997, after suffering fatal injuries in a car crash in the Pont de l’Alma road tunnel in Paris, France.



She was not wearing a seatbelt when she was travelling in the back seat of a chauffeur-driven Mercedes car with then boyfriend Dodi Fayed.

Mum-of-three Megan also said she had a crystal for “protection”.

She said: “I was not messing around for this trip, protection first.”

Megan’s holiday comes after England were defeated in the World Cup semi-finals in the US last month against Argentina.



She has been dubbed the ‘Queen of the Wags’.

She was seen promoting her designer outfits on social media during the tournament.

The Magpies shelled out £23million to sign teenage star Steur from Ajax in the wake of Sandro Tonali‘s £100m departure for Tottenham.



In a TikTok video posted by a Dutch performance centre just two days before Steur’s move was announced, the 18-year-old could be seen performing drills dressed head-to-toe in Man Utd training gear.

And a second joked: “Boy doesnt like Zebra FC”.

Newcastle fans defended their new boy.

Others posted a snap of a young Michael Carrick wearing a replica Newcastle kit.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo set to marry Georgina Rodriguez in fairytale wedding on island where he grew up
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL star Cristiano Ronaldo is set to marry fiancée Georgina Rodriguez on the island where he was born and raised.

The pair appear to have decided to get hitched in Madeira.



The cathedral in the island’s capital Funchal is booked for a big wedding next Saturday, according to local reports.

Appropriately, weddings there kick off at 3pm.



Portugal star Ronaldo, 41 — who grew up in Funchal — and model Georgina, 32, are said to have reserved the nearby five-star Savoy Palace hotel for the reception.

He met Georgina, who is Spanish-Argentinian, in 2016 and proposed to her last August.

Last week the couple were snapped wearing diamond rings as they boarded a yacht in Majorca.

Ronaldo said previously that he and Georgina planned to marry after the World Cup, from which Portugal were ousted by eventual winners Spain last month.



The striker told Piers Morgan: “I hope to arrive at my wedding with the champion’s trophy.”

He said Georgina was the only woman he had dated that he had wanted to settle down with.

Sports.title: Music legend Phil Collins’ son Mathew, 21, joins former Bundesliga champions in shock transfer
Sports.content:
PHIL COLLINS’ son Mathew is looking to make his mark on the football world after completing a surprise transfer to former Bundesliga champions 1860 Munich.

The 21-year-old midfielder has signed a one-year contract with the German outfit after impressing during a trial spell.



Collins joins the club after spending last season with Austrian second-tier side Austria Salzburg.

The Switzerland-born youngster – whose half-sister is Lily Collins, of Emily In Paris fame – has spent the majority of his senior career in Austria after previously coming through youth systems in Germany.



And 1860 Munich confirmed the signing on Friday as they prepare for life in Germany’s fourth tier.

The historic club now compete in the Regionalliga after suffering relegation from the 3. Liga when they failed to secure the licence required to remain in the division.



Despite their current struggles, 1860 boast one of the richest histories in German football.

They were founder members of the Bundesliga in 1963 and famously won the German title during the 1965/66 campaign.

The club have also lifted the German Cup twice and reached the 1965 European Cup Winners’ Cup final, where they were beaten by West Ham at Wembley.

Collins began his career in the academies of Astoria Walldorf and Hannover 96 before moving to Austrian side WSG Tirol in 2023.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

During his time there, he even faced Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly, coming up against England captain Harry Kane in the summer of 2024.

Last season he made four league appearances for Austria Salzburg and also featured once in the Austrian Cup.

He linked up with his new team-mates ahead of their opening league match, a 2-2 draw away to FC Schweinfurt.

While Mathew is chasing his football dream, his famous father became one of the biggest names in music history.



Collins rose to fame as drummer and later lead singer of Genesis before launching a hugely successful solo career with hits including In the Air Tonight and You Can’t Hurry Love.

The music icon, who was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame both with Genesis and as a solo artist, has five children, including actress Lily, musician Simon Collins, actress and producer Joely Collins, and Mathew’s brother Nic.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Tzolis a livewire on Gunners debut as Dowman sparkles but Nwaneri off the pace in Girona win
Sports.content:
ARSENAL got their pre-season underway with a thumping win over Girona in the Catalan sunshine.

Mikel Arteta‘s side eased past their hosts, who were relegated from LaLiga last term.



The Gunners spent all week in Spain training ahead of this match.

And they looked sharp from the off, Kai Havertz firing them into the lead on 16 minutes and new boy Christos Tzolis doubling their advantage on the half hour.



Arnau Martinez pulled one back for the hosts, only for further efforts by Max Dowman and Gabriel Jesus to add gloss to the scoreline.

Here’s how SunSport’s Joshua Hall rated each Arsenal performer on a sweltering evening in Girona.

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 5

Had very little to do, but still couldn’t keep out Arnau Martinez’s second-half bullet header from a corner.

BEN WHITE – 6

Back from the injury that ruled him out of the Champions League final and the World Cup, and with the captain’s armband on.

A mixed performance that saw some sloppy touches, but also some great pressure to earn Arsenal their fourth goal with a tackle-cum-pass to Gabriel Jesus.

CRISTHIAN MOSQUERA – 6

Arsenal were not put under too much pressure by Girona, but Mosquera’s calm presence is always a comfort blanket when there is a wave of attack.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

PIERO HINCAPIE – 6

One of three World Cup stars to be given just over 30 minutes of action. Some nice link up play on the left flank when he was on the pitch.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 6

The Italian looked a threat when he was combining with Hincapie and Tzolis down the left side.

The game being played at a usual laid-back pre-season pace meant his usual marauding runs were out of the question.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Mikel Arteta looks like he views Lewis-Skelly as a midfielder now, starting him in that position from the off for this game.



A solid performance from the Englishman, but shifting into the middle of the park could still mean limited minutes if Bruno Guimaraes arrives.

KAI HAVERTZ – 8

A brilliantly taken opener from the German who still seems sharp from his time with Germany at the World Cup.

Whether or not the second goal was his is up for debate, the ball deflected off his ankle en route to the bottom corner from Christos Tzolis’ shot.



ETHAN NWANERI – 5

Arteta will be watching Nwaneri closely during pre-season, with his future at Arsenal still very much up in the air after his failed loan move to Marseille last term.

This was a solid enough performance with some nice close control, but the 19-year-old needs to have a more direct impact on the game.

MAX DOWMAN – 8

Not that anyone was doubting it, but Dowman’s raw talent is evident every time he gets the ball.

His through ball to find Havertz for the opener was sublime, and there were some moments of silky ball control scattered throughout his cameo too.

A brilliant solo goal topped off his performance, cutting in from the right flank and drilling the ball into the back of the net with his left peg.



CHRISTOS TZOLIS – 8

Some really promising stuff from the summer signing.

Tzolis was always looking to cut in on his right foot and get a shot off or find a man in the box, while he also offered a bit of set piece threat.

He will be claiming the second goal as his own after it was his goalward effort that deflected off Havertz and into the back of the net.



VIKTOR GYOKERES – 6

The Swede was given just 32 minutes after his World Cup exploits, but showed for the ball in his usual passionate manner for each and every one of them.

The final pass never really came.

SUBSTITUTES

This performance didn’t do much to make Arteta desperate to convince him to stay, in fact he was subbed off just over half an hour after coming on.

GABRIEL JESUS – 7

Did very well to tuck away the loose ball that fell into his path when Ben White forced an error at the back for Girona.

MARLI SALMON – 7

So assured on the ball for a centre-back of his age and comfortable under pressure too.

Arsenal fans will be hoping they will see more of the rising star this season, especially with William Saliba’s back injury.

ILLAN MESLIER – 7

Some really tidy saves from the new arrival, who joined on a free transfer after his Leeds contract expires this summer.



With so many youth players on the pitch alongside him, Meslier stepped in to clean up their mistakes.

Another player who seems destined for the exit doors this summer. The winger had little impact during his cameo.

An exciting talent who loves to break up play and sit at the base of midfield. Like most of the youth talents brought on, it would have been nice to see him play alongside more first-team players.

Son of former Premier League and Championship midfielder Nigel Quashie, Clarke was one of many youth players who held their own to maintain Arsenal’s cushion in the last 30 minutes.

ANDRE HARRIMAN-ANNOUS – 6

Always trying to make something happen, but didn’t quite get the opportunity to grab a goal given the gamestate when he was brought on.

Sports.title: Liverpool have been given green light for 'dream' Bradley Barcola alternative
Sports.content:
Liverpool have been given green light for 'dream' Bradley Barcola alternative

Liverpool are in the market for a Mohamed Salah replacement for the new Premier League season

View 2 Images Liverpool want to sign Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty)

Liverpool are stepping up their efforts to sign Bradley Barcola from PSG. But there are other potential options out there if a move fails to materialise, notably AFC Bournemouth's Brazilian sensation, Rayan.

‌



The Reds are preparing an opening bid for Barcola, who is understood to be keen on a move to Anfield. However, the Frenchman's price tag could prove a sticking point.

‌



Barcola is valued by the Ligue 1 champions at £145million. Not only would that represent a Premier League record transfer, it is also some way above the £100m mark that Liverpool chiefs would prefer to do business at.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Should the winger's price prove insurmountable in negotiations, the Reds could turn their attention to Rayan instead. The 19-year-old has been linked with a host of clubs, including the Liverpool, after impressing for Bournemouth following his January move to the south coast.

‌



Indeed, talkSPORT reports that the Bournemouth star is considered a 'dream' target for the Reds. However, the teenager's release clause of £85m will not kick in until 2027, meaning that Andoni Iraola may need to fork out more for his signature in the short term.

One person who is very aware of Rayan's abilities is Cherries midfielder, Marcus Tavernier. The 27-year-old showered his team-mate with praise following Bournemouth's 3-0 win over Crystal Palace in May, even going so far as to predict that his stay at the Vitality Stadium would be short lived given his exceptional talents.

View 2 Images Rayan could prove a good alternative to Barcola (Image: Getty)

‌



He told Sky Sports: "Rayan and Kroupi? It’s been unbelievable, they are two world-class talents. I don’t think they will be at Bournemouth for a long period of time give the quality they have got.

"It’s brilliant to have them on the pitch. As a team we give the young players the confidence to go out and play with freedom."

Barcola is evidently still Liverpool's main target, with the Reds expected to submit an offer imminently. But with the sums involved in securing a deal, there's no guarantee a move will happen - and that could lead Iraola to look elsewhere.

Article continues below

PSG argue that the France international is now a back-to-back Champions League winner and should be priced above the likes of Morgan Rogers - who went to Chelsea for £117m - and City's £116m move for Elliot Anderson.

It is understood that Barcola is not planning to sign a new deal in France and has just two years remaining on his current contract.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola’s three new Liverpool starting XIs with blockbuster Bradley Barcola transfer
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola’s three new Liverpool starting XIs with blockbuster Bradley Barcola transfer

Liverpool could line up in a number of interesting ways under Andoni Iraola

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola is a major target for Liverpool (Image: Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool have been relatively quiet in the transfer market compared to 12 months ago – so far. The Reds dropped a whopping £446million on the likes of Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike, Florian Wirtz and Milos Kerkez ahead of the 2024-25 Premier League season.

‌



But that outlay didn't result in the retention of the title as Arne Slot's side ended up trophyless and the Dutchman out of a job. Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate followed the Dutchman out the door following the expiry of their respective contracts.

‌



Now, a new era is set to begin under Andoni Iraola. The former Bournemouth boss has signed Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz so far, but fans would argue that they will need more reinforcements before the season begins.

‌



One major target Iraola is focusing on is Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola. The winger is not an out-and-out replacement for Salah, but he can slot into multiple areas if Liverpool does complete his signing.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The Reds face Newcastle in just three weeks' time and also have a number of players sidelined for this curtain raiser. Conor Bradley, Joe Gomez, Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni are all unavailable, meaning Iraola will need to adapt.

Should Barcola be brought in before the Premier League opener, and Munoz also available, the Reds could set up totally differently going forward. Here, Mirror Football details three ways Liverpool could line up if the PSG star does join.

4-2-3-1

View 4 Images This is Iraola's trusted system (Image: Supplied)

‌



Iraola will probably opt to implement his trusted system from his Bournemouth tenure with Alisson Becker anticipated to stay as No. 1 this season.

This setup would allow the Reds to operate a flat back four with active wing-backs in Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, alongside Virgil van Dijk and Jacquet at centre-back.

It's in midfield where a double pivot of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch could anchor the side, while a lethal attacking trio of Rio Ngumoha, Wirtz and Barcola would operate behind Isak leading the line.

‌



In this setup, Barcola would occupy his preferred left-sided position, where he has netted 32 goals and provided 32 assists for PSG and Lyon. Ngumoha would play on the right, a switch Iraola deployed in the recent pre-season victory over Wrexham, while Wirtz would orchestrate play in his natural No. 10 role.

4-3-3

View 4 Images This formation could be played around with by the boss (Image: Supplied)

With the same goalkeeper and defensive quartet, the alteration here arrives in midfield. Szoboszlai, Gravenberch and Wirtz would create a more conventional engine room, with the German playmaker granted licence to drift while the Dutchman operates in a deeper position.

‌



It's in attack where Iraola could tinker, too. Barcola could operate on the right, a flank the Frenchman isn't completely accustomed to, but does possess experience in.

The PSG man has just seven goals from the right but has contributed 15 assists. New signing Munoz would slot into his preferred position on the left flank with both wide men delivering balls into Isak, who would operate as a lone striker.

This could even shift into a compact 4-5-1 without possession, should the Reds need to protect a lead.

‌



4-4-1-1

View 4 Images This formation could bring some chaos for the Reds (Image: Supplied)

This setup places Wirtz on the left and Ngumoha on the right of a four-man midfield, with Szoboszlai and Gravenberch forming a two-man defensive shield. However, this would represent Iraola's wildcard option, potentially shifting Barcola into the hole behind Isak.

Barcola has featured as a centre-forward on more than 20 occasions, contributing a respectable nine goals. It's not an extensive sample, but the winger is known for cutting inside and frequently taking on opponents in central areas.

Article continues below

With a dependable midfield quartet behind him, and Wirtz and Ngumoha controlling the supply lines down either flank, Barcola could be handed the opportunity to forge a lethal partnership with Isak, operating just behind him in an unfamiliar yet potentially devastating No. 10 role.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Arsenal fan to snub Gunners for Man Utd in transfer U-turn
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Arsenal fan to snub Gunners for Man Utd in transfer U-turn

Manchester United have battled with plenty of Premier League sides for transfers over the years

View 2 Images Chris Smalling joined Manchester United after speaking with Sir Alex Ferguson (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Sir Alex Ferguson convinced Chris Smalling to abandon his dream to play for Arsenal and join Manchester United instead. The defender grew up a fan of the Gunners and was sure he would join his beloved club from Fulham.

‌



The north London outfit were in talks with the Cottagers as Arsene Wenger's reputation for developing rising stars interested Smalling. However, Sir Alex jumped in with a pitch that the centre-half just couldn't turn down.

‌



He told The Athletic: "In my head, I was going to Arsenal. Then Manchester United got in touch. I was leaving the team bus at Blackburn away and [Fulham boss] Roy Hodgson said, 'We’ve accepted a bid from Man United.' That threw me.

‌



"I felt there were more opportunities to play at Arsenal, but I spoke to Fergie and he said, 'I wouldn’t sign you if I didn’t think you could play games.' Maybe his aura felt right, but I made the right decision because I was soon playing alongside great players and winning the league."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies READ MORE :

Fergie's words stuck with Smalling and he joined United for an initial fee of around £8million, which rose to £12m due to appearance and performance bonuses. This was a major success story for a defender who had been playing non-league football just two years before his move to Old Trafford.

‌



Smalling had been at Maidstone in 2008 and ended up at Fulham, who were paying him just £5,000-a-week. He quadrupled his salary by joining United but his former non-league side didn't receive a penny, as he was a non-contract player when he departed the Stones.

Arsenal had met Fulham's clause of £10m before United swooped in, but Sir Alex's words alone convinced Smalling to ignore the allure of Wenger and head to Manchester instead. The Arsenal snub proved a wise decision for Smalling, as he would go on to win two Premier League titles and the Europa League with United.

View 2 Images Sir Alex Ferguson's 'aura' had Smalling convinced (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



The defender also won numerous domestic cups and came runner-up in the Champions League final in his first year at Old Trafford. Smalling made 323 appearances for United over a decade, scoring 18 goals and assisting three times.

He joined Roma on loan for the 2019/20 season and became the first English player to score at least two goals in the same Serie A campaign since fellow United alumni David Beckham.

The centre-half joined the Italian outfit permanently for a fee of £17m and spent four years there before moving on to Al-Fayha. Smalling is now 36 years old and without a club, though he hasn't announced plans of retirement yet.

Sports.title: Man Utd’s dream final month of transfer window: £85m midfielder joins and three deals done
Sports.content:
Man Utd’s dream final month of transfer window: £85m midfielder joins and three deals done

Manchester United could make multiple dream signings before transfer deadline day on September 1

View 3 Images Michael Carrick will likely be busy in August (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have secured several new signings but Michael Carrick's team remain busy in the transfer market. As August arrives, the club have one month remaining to restructure their squad.

‌



The middle of the park remains a priority, despite signing Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. United have been linked with numerous possibilities but the manager may seek to deliver a marquee name in midfield to underline the club's aspirations to challenge for major honours next season.

‌



In attack, Benjamin Sesko requires competition, with striker Joshua Zirkzee among several players who could depart Old Trafford this summer. Meanwhile, United could begin long-term planning by testing Newcastle's determination over left-back Lewis Hall. Here, Mirror Football examines what a dream end to the transfer window might look like for the club.

‌



£85m midfielder signs

Aurelien Tchouameni arriving from Real Madrid would mark a statement signing for United in the final weeks of the window. The Red Devils refused to pay astronomical sums for the likes of Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes earlier in the summer but splashing out on Tchouameni would emphasise the club's ambitions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The 26-year-old would represent an ideal signing for Carrick's revamped midfield as the United manager reshapes his squad following Casemiro's departure. Spanish publication AS previously reported that Real Madrid would seek around £85m for Tchouameni after the France international recently penned a contract extension with Los Blancos.

‌



Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe READ MORE :

However, the Spanish heavyweights are keen on Manchester City's Rodri, which could prompt Tchouameni to weigh up his options elsewhere. It would provide Carrick with an impressive selection of midfielders, with Tielemans, Santos and Kobbie Mainoo all competing for spots in the United starting XI.

Lewis Hall deal

United are interested in Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall and, in an ideal scenario, would secure Luke Shaw's long-term replacement this summer. The 21-year-old has caught the eye during his spell with the Magpies, who have already demonstrated a readiness to offload key assets through the departures of Anthony Gordon and Tonali.

The England international is reportedly open to joining Carrick's side. Yet Newcastle are believed to be hesitant about selling another prized asset, meaning United may need to fork out a substantial fee for the defender, who left Chelsea for £35m in 2023.

‌



View 3 Images Lewis Hall is reportedly open to joining Manchester United (Image: Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

United depended heavily on Shaw throughout last season but will have worries about the seasoned full-back staying injury-free, while Patrick Dorgu appeared more effective when deployed on the left wing. Completing a move for Hall would enable United to begin their left-back succession planning early, even if the young defender commands a substantial transfer fee.

New striker joins

Benjamin Sesko's unavailability for United's early pre-season fixtures has underlined the club's need to add a striker before the summer window closes. Joshua Zirkzee has spearheaded the attack for Carrick's team but has struggled to establish himself since his arrival from Bologna in 2024, prompting reports of a possible £30m return to Serie A.

‌



While Sesko flourished after Carrick arrived at United, it took time for the Slovenian forward to cement his place in the starting lineup. The 23-year-old is still developing and shouldn't be the club's sole senior striker as United prepare for a Champions League campaign and seek to improve upon their third-place Premier League finish.

View 3 Images Dusan Vlahovic is a free agent after leaving Juventus (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Dusan Vlahovic is among several forwards to be linked with a move to Old Trafford and could offer the perfect answer to United's dilemma. The 26-year-old is a free agent after leaving Juventus this summer, where he netted 68 goals across 168 matches.

Article continues below

An expensive, high-profile signing could potentially hinder Sesko's development under Carrick and stop him from fulfilling his true potential. However, the former RB Leipzig star would benefit from competing alongside Vlahovic, who would equally be afforded the chance to impress as a rotation option at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star

Liverpool round-up as Bradley Barcola negotiations take a turn in the Reds' favour

View 3 Images Liverpool's interest in Bradley Barcola remains strong (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's transfer window has been quieter than many fans had hoped so far. But it may be about to stir into life as negotiations with Paris Saint-Germain over long-running target Bradley Barcola continue.

‌



Pre-season has been promising with wins over Sunderland and Wrexham. Next up on the tour of the United States is a meeting with Leeds United at Chicago's Soldier Field.

‌



New signings Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz are yet to figure. The former is getting closer to his Reds debut following a shoulder injury, while Spain World Cup winner Munoz is coming to the end of his post-tournament break.

‌



It's the interest in Barcola that continues to take centre stage, with movement elsewhere in the transfer market strengthening the Reds' hand. Here's a round-up of the latest Liverpool transfer news.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Barcola replacements found

PSG are close to landing two wingers in a clear sign they are preparing for life after Barcola. They have reportedly opened talks with Ajax about signing Mika Godts for £51million.

‌



Yan Diomande transfer twist as surprise update emerges on Real Madrid target READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Green light given for huge transfer offer as talks for new signing begin READ MORE :

Meanwhile, the Champions League holders are on the verge of signing Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco for around £43m. With Desire Doue, Ibrahim Maye and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia already at the club, the position is set to become even more crowded.

Something needs to give, and that 'something' is Barcola. Liverpool have no intention of meeting PSG's £145m asking price but negotiations are continuing and the impending arrival of Godts and Akliouche should strengthen their hand.

The French champions still stand to make an enormous profit on a player who arrived from Lyon for less than £40m three years ago.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Barcola's PSG exit has moved closer (Image: Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP via Getty Images)

New Jones offer

Inter Milan are willing to increase their offer for midfielder Curtis Jones. The Serie A champions have already brought John Stones to the club this summer and are keen to add another England international, having already had one bid of around £21m rejected.

As reported by the Liverpool Echo, Inter are preparing a bid of £30m, although that is still short of the Reds' £35m valuation for the 25-year-old, who has a year left on his contract.

‌



View 3 Images Curtis Jones is attracting interest (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Intermediaries working on behalf of Inter have now contacted Liverpool once more and have informed them of the Serie A side's willingness to up their offer. Jones has made 228 appearances since his debut in January 2019 but has struggled for regular first-team football.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Transfer 'approved' as £70m target 'open' to Old Trafford switch
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Transfer 'approved' as £70m target 'open' to Old Trafford switch

It's been a busy summer for Manchester United - and their transfer business looks far from over, with a number of targets still on their radar

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is looking to make a few more signings this summer (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have wasted little time getting to work this summer - but their rebuild is far from complete. With the 2026/27 campaign fast approaching, the priority is to maintain the momentum generated at the end of last season and ensure Michael Carrick's side are equipped to hit the ground running.

‌



Having spent the previous two summer windows addressing issues in attack and defence, the focus has now shifted towards strengthening the midfield. United have already made significant moves in that department, with Andrey Santos arriving from Chelsea in a £50million deal and Youri Tielemans joining from Aston Villa for £35m.

‌



However, the business is not expected to stop there. The club remain active in the market and continue to monitor a number of high-profile targets, including reinforcements beyond midfield as they look to complete a much-needed squad overhaul.

‌



With plenty still to unfold before the window closes, here are the latest Manchester United transfer headlines.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

Man Utd 'internally approve' Hall transfer

Lewis Hall has emerged as a top target for United this summer, with reports claiming an official approach for the Newcastle defender has been approved internally. The England international has been linked with a move away from St James' Park for some time, with United among a number of Premier League heavyweights keeping a close eye on his situation.

‌



The Red Devils see Hall as a potential long-term replacement for Luke Shaw and are reportedly considering an opening bid worth around £60m for the 21-year-old. Although Hall remains tied down to Newcastle until 2029, the significant upheaval at the club could potentially open the door to an exit.

View 3 Images Lewis Hall is high on Man United's wish list (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

The Magpies have already seen Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe all leave in recent weeks, while Bruno Guimaraes is expected to follow suit in the coming days. Hall could yet follow them through the exit door, although Newcastle's impressive summer sales could actually strengthen their negotiating position.

‌



Having already generated around £170m through player departures - a figure that could rise towards £250m if Guimaraes completes his proposed switch to Arsenal - Newcastle are under no financial pressure to cash in on Hall.

Scott 'open to Man Utd move'

Manchester United could be set to make their third major midfield signing of the summer, with Bournemouth star Alex Scott reportedly open to the possibility of joining Carrick's side. The 22-year-old is attracting significant interest from across the Premier League, with Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal also keeping tabs on his situation.

View 3 Images Bournemouth's Alex Scott is reportedly open to a move to Manchester United (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



Scott is believed to be considering all options at this stage, with no clear frontrunner emerging in the race for his signature. Reports claim Chelsea recently saw a £64m offer rejected by Bournemouth, although that does not necessarily put them ahead of their rivals in what remains a fiercely contested transfer battle.

The Cherries are thought to value Scott at around £70m, but given the level of competition for his services, that asking price could climb closer to £80m. United would then need to weigh up whether such a sizeable outlay represents good value.

The Red Devils remain keen to add another central midfielder after their pursuit of Atalanta star Ederson collapsed, but their recent recruitment strategy has typically focused on more measured, cost-effective deals rather than marquee spending.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr transfer trick set to be repeated as next three signings lined up
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr transfer trick set to be repeated as next three signings lined up

Mikel Arteta and Arsenal are eyeing three more first-team additions

View 3 Images Arsenal are hoping to land Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty )

Arsenal have seemingly kicked into life as we enter the final month of the summer transfer window. Mikel Arteta’s men faced Girona in a pre-season friendly on Saturday evening - but the focus was mainly on the club's activity off the field.

‌



That’s because the Gunners have been closely linked with several big-name targets in recent days, including Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid. The Los Blancos superstar would represent the first genuinely marquee addition of the window for sporting director Andrea Berta, having been given the green light financially to bring in the forward.

‌



Until now, Berta has only signed Piero Hincapie on a permanent basis for £34.5million, third-choice goalkeeper Illan Meslier and £34m Leandro Trossard replacement Christos Tzolis. Ahead of the transfer window’s closure on September 1, Mirror Football brings you the latest news from the Emirates Stadium.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Three signings lined up

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is reportedly close to being signed (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are reportedly eyeing three more signings this summer. The Athletic reported on Saturday that Vinicius is Arteta’s top transfer target to strengthen the attack.

‌



An agreement between the Brazilian and Arsenal is expected to be found on personal terms if Real Madrid don’t match his demands and the forward opts not to renew at the Bernabeu. The report adds that, whether Vinicius signs or not, the north Londoners will bring in a new winger before the window shuts.

Arsenal will also seek a new midfielder, understood to be Bruno Guimaraes, after reportedly agreeing a £77m deal with Newcastle. Finally, The Athletic states a central defender is being pursued in an effort to cover the injured William Saliba in the coming months.

Vinicius transfer trick repeat

View 3 Images Ferran Torres is on Arsenal's radar (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The transfer links with Vinicius seemingly came out of nowhere last weekend. Yet, Berta is understood to have kept an eye on the 26-year-old winger’s contract situation for some time before making his approach, having seen Vinicius enter the final year of his deal.

Now, Arsenal are reportedly considering employing a similar method in their pursuit of another forward - Barcelona’s Ferran Torres - who is also due to become a free agent next summer, as it stands.

Spanish outlet Estadio Deportivo claims the Gunners have enquired about the Spain striker, who scored the decisive goal in the World Cup final last month. Barcelona want to extend Torres' contract, which is due to expire in June next year.

Article continues below

But negotiations are yet to produce an agreement, increasing pressure on Barcelona to cash in rather than risk losing the 26-year-old for nothing next summer. That, similarly to the Vinicius situation, plays directly into Arsenal’s hands as they can offer a lower transfer fee. Torres can play on either wing or through the middle, with his versatility making this potential signing an alluring one.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta directly pressed on Vinicius Jr before ending Arsenal press conference suddenly
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta directly pressed on Vinicius Jr before ending Arsenal press conference suddenly

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was asked about Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr during his post-match press conference on Saturday evening in Girona

View 2 Images Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr. continues to be linked with Arsenal (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has refused to be drawn on whether the Gunners will secure the signing of Vinicius Junior this summer — abruptly bringing his post-match press conference to a close after being quizzed about the Brazilian star.

‌



Arteta's side are understood to be weighing up a move for the Real Madrid winger, with the 26-year-old seen as a prime candidate to bolster Arsenal's left flank — widely regarded as a vulnerability in their attack — as they look to cement their position as Premier League champions.

‌



Vinicius Jr. netted 22 goals and provided 14 assists in 53 appearances for Los Blancos last season — despite the Spanish giants enduring a disappointing campaign. With negotiations over a contract extension at the Santiago Bernabeu having reportedly hit a wall, it could represent a golden opportunity for the Gunners to land one of football's most electrifying attacking talents.

‌



Max Dowman oozes class as new Arsenal partnership unlocked in Girona win – 5 talking points READ MORE :

Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes READ MORE :

Arteta was asked about a potential deal for the very first time following Arsenal's 4-1 pre-season friendly victory over Girona on Saturday.

When pressed on whether supporters could expect further additions to the squad before the new season gets underway, he said: "Well, we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it.

"The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr is being linked with a big-money move to Arsenal (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



The Spaniard was subsequently asked, in the final question, whether Vinicius Jr. would be arriving.

"Thank you so much," the 44-year-old responded with a smirk before departing.

Recent reports from Spanish outlet Marca suggest that Jose Mourinho's outfit have tabled a final offer to the Brazil international.

‌



It is understood that no further salary enhancements or additional rounds of talks are expected, and should he turn down the proposal, Madrid will seek to cash in this summer.

Sports.title: Staveley-led consortium agrees deal for minority stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
Vanessa Gold has confirmed she has agreed to sell her stake in the club to a consortium led by former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley.

Gold, who succeeded her father David as joint-chair of the Hammers following his death in 2023, has a deal in place with a group headed by Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners for her family's 25.1 per cent holding.

However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.

Image: Former Newcastle co-owner Staveley's consortium is set to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the club

"Amanda Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, PCP Capital Partners along with Ashland Forest Capital Partners can confirm they have agreed the purchase of the Gold family's 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham United," the Staveley-led consortium said in a statement.

"A legal binding agreement has been signed.

"This sale agreement, though, remains subject to a pre-emption process under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"No further comment will be made whilst the ongoing legal process takes its course."

Sky Sports News further understands Staveley, Ghodoussi and their consortium have brought together considerable funds.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of West Ham's pre-season friendly against Stevenage

Gold said in a statement: "As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint-chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023.

"Whether as a youth-team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father's priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.

"On June 12, Daniel Kretinsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

"In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.

"My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

Image: The consortium is led by Staveley and her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, alongside PCP Capital Partners

"Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham.

"While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club's best interests, as my father did and would expect of me."

Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club's rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.

The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on August 16.

West Ham said in a statement: "West Ham United can confirm it is aware of the announcement from joint-chair Vanessa Gold that she has reached a provisional agreement to sell her shares to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

"The proposed transaction will now be subject to a pre-emption rights process. This provides all existing shareholders with the opportunity to acquire their proportional percentage of shares in round one, and any remaining shares in round two. This process will take approximately two months and, until it is completed, nothing will change regarding the ownership structure of the club.

"West Ham United would like to assure supporters that the day-to-day running of the football club is in no way affected by this situation. Preparations for the new season continue to take shape with diligence and focus, and we thank all fans for their continued loyal backing at this time.

"The club will be making no further comment while the pre-emption process runs its course."

Sports.title: Evening Saigon wins Stewards' Cup at Goodwood
Sports.content:
James Doyle picked the right one from three choices as his bosses at Wathnan Racing topped an amazing week at Glorious Goodwood with victory in the Coral Stewards' Cup with Evening Saigon.

The win was a feather in the cap for the owners, who target this fixture with a vengeance, but perhaps more telling it was a second major handicap of the week for Qatari-born trainer Hamad Al Jehani.

Having also won the Golden Mile with Archivist when Doyle picked the wrong one, Al Jehani was able to celebrate a famous victory with the whole team on this occasion.

Despite higher numbers being preferred at Thursday's draw, the finish was dominated by the eventual winner drawn in 10 beating Stratusnine in five. Jamie Spencer flew from the back on Mitbaahy for third but he was beaten a head and a short head. Completely Random was fourth.

"It's been a great week. Obviously I was very deflated last year with just one and we were really frustrated by that so the memo was we need to do better and that's everyone, including me as well," said Doyle.

"We've done a lot of work this week looking at different tactics and things like that, track position and stuff. All the guys back home in the office, these guys, Hamad has done an unbelievable job with this horse as well.

"He's not an easy conveyance, setting off he was that well in himself he tried to get rid of me the first few strides but that was great.

"We just had the perfect set-up. Dark Thirty was near me, I was able to draft in behind him and we didn't go that mad I didn't think for a Stewards' Cup so I was happy to pull him out before the two and set sail for home.

"I knew the second horse, I won on him the other day at York, he's a pretty decent horse too so it was a good tussle up to the line.

"Hamad and his team, it's nice that they have won the two big handicaps this week."

Al Jehani said: "I am very happy for Evening Saigon and very happy for the team. He performed very well at Royal Ascot and it was the right decision from the management to keep him for the Stewards' Cup.

"It's really important for us and it's a really important race for the season. I'm very happy and thanks to James for giving the horse a great ride.

"It's not easy to be competitive with the best trainers in the world but we try our best and I think we are building in a very good way, with great help from the management. Hopefully, we will improve year by year and we can make Wathnan be in the winner's enclosure more and more."

Wathnan's racing advisor Richard Brown added: "James had a bit of a hard choice but he was pretty firm on riding this lad in the end. Hamad has turned up and won two of the hardest handicaps to win all year. We plot these and work as a team - when these results come off, it's just fantastic for Wathnan and what Wathnan is all about.

"If you look at Hamad's statistics since he started training, they match up with the best trainers in the country. He's a phenomenal horseman and was a very good rider himself. He's very modest about it but he showjumped to a good level. He's a great horseman and he's formed a great team. We all work very closely together and to pull this off is huge for everybody involved."

Goodie Two Shoes sticks her neck out to edge Lillie Langtry battle

Goodie Two Shoes needed to be very brave as she added to Joseph O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle's fantastic week at Goodwood in the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes.

With three winners already in the bag, the JP McManus-owned Goodie Two Shoes was sent off an 8/1 chance to bag a first victory of the season but looked to face a tough ask as Santorini Star kicked for home.

She still had ground to make up with 100 yards to the line but the seven-year-old stuck her neck out right where it mattered to get the verdict by a nose.

Image: Goodie Two Shoes (centre), ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle, on the way to winning the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes at Goodwood

Goodie Two Shoes was second in the Melbourne Cup in November and a return to Australia will surely now be on the cards following this Group Two triumph.

The winning rider said: "She's a lovely filly, she's improving all the time since she started coming back this year, she's got better with each run.

"I was quietly confident she would get a lot closer to these fillies, she ran well last year [third] when the ground turned up soft but she would gallop down the road for you, she handles quick ground. I got a lovely split through them and she wanted to win.

"To be honest I didn't think I'd won but I looked back at the camera and she had her head stuck down for me at the right time; I did think Tom (Marquand) had won but we came out the right side of it.

"These are very, very special silks to put on. A big thanks to JP for putting me up and she's going to have a nice campaign through to the end of the season.

"I'm sure the Melbourne Cup is probably the main target, the boys will know that and Joseph and JP will discuss it but I'd probably guess that's the obvious target."

Sir Anthony McCoy, representing McManus, said: "I didn't think she had won but Jason Weaver said right on the nod, not before the line or after the line but right on the line, she put her head in the right place.

"She got a good ride - he was going to ride her for that bit of luck, down the inside, and he got a lot of luck. When you are as good as Dylan Browne McMonagle and you are riding for Joseph O'Brien, you seem to get a lot of luck.

"Dylan was over at mine a few times when he was 11 or 12. He is very mechanically correct, like Ryan Moore, and he's got that chip - that little thing where he could go the wrong way. I mean it in a good way. As Frankie found out one day at Ascot, he has that little edge to him.

"She was second in a Melbourne Cup and I thought she had been quite well handicapped for the Galway Plate if she ran there off 123. It's nice when you win races like this and hopefully she will be able to go back to the Melbourne Cup."

Sports.title: Warrington go fourth as Wakefield move second, Saints beaten by York
Sports.content:
Super League: Warrington move into fourth with comprehensive win over Castleford, St Helens beaten by York in thriller, and Wakefield regain second

Warrington got back to winning way on their visit to Castleford

Warrington Wolves moved up to fourth in the Betfred Super League table after recovering from a lacklustre start to claim a comprehensive 48-18 win at Castleford Tigers .

Having lost four of their last six matches, including three in a row on the road, Warrington were made to pay for an error-strewn first 20 minutes as the Tigers went 16-6 ahead at the OneBore Stadium.

But Matty Ashton, Toby King and Toafofoa Sipley touched down to turn the tide and put Warrington 24-18 in front at half-time, and James Harrison and Leon Hayes extended the Wolves' lead after the break.

Ashton scored again, taking his tally to five tries in two matches against Castleford this year having bagged a hat-trick when Warrington claimed a 72-6 victory in March, before Ben Currie scored.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Teenage scrum-half Ewan Irwin was excellent with the boot, splitting the posts with all eight conversions, to make it back-to-back defeats for Castleford.

While Castleford were stuffed by rivals Wakefield last weekend, they claimed a shock win over Leeds in their last home match and Warrington head coach Sam Burgess had warned they would be no pushovers.

On this occasion, they could not find the defensive intent required to stop Warrington on their push for a spot at the top end of the top six.

Sailor misses late kick as York edge thriller

Oli Field's double further dented St Helens' play-off hopes despite Jack Welsby's try-of-the-season contender as York edged to a thrilling 34-32 victory at the LNER Community Stadium.

Saints got off to the perfect start when Welsby kicked through to allow Jake Davies to touch down, with Jackson Hastings adding the conversion.

York Knights inflicted a damning loss on St Helens

York hit back almost immediately when Toa Mata'Afa put Jon Bennison over in the corner, and although he was unable to convert his own score, he was successful after Field capitalised on Cody Hunter's well-timed pass with a neat step to make it 10-6.

The lead proved short-lived when Hunter was unable to claim Hastings' up and under and Shane Wright pounced to score a converted try, and the visitors surged further head when Welsby burst through Denive Balmforth's tackle after the fleet-footed Harry Robertson had raced down the right wing.

However, Balmforth swiftly made amends with a sniping finish and Bennison levelled it up at 16-16 at the break.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The Knights were temporarily reduced to 12 when Ata Hingana was sent to the bin for a high tackle on Davies, but it was they who regained the lead with 53 minutes gone when prop Paul Vaughan barged his way over and Bennison added the extra points.

They went 12 points ahead after Saints failed to deal with Hunter's lofted kick, Nikau Williams touching down and Bennison making it 28-16, but Robertson's brilliance allowed Tristan Sailor to feed Welsby to complete a length-of-the-field move which was converted by Hastings.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Field's second try and a fifth successful Bennison conversion gave the Knights breathing space, but late scores from Robertson and Jacob Douglas gave Saints a chance.

Regular goal kicker Hastings remained on the field but was holding his glute so Sailor had to deputise and missed the crucial kick to level the game.

Wakefield move back second with win over Catalans

A crucial double from Isaiah Vagana helped Wakefield Trinity to a 32-12 win over Catalans Dragons to move back into second place in the Super League table.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The match was close at the break, Trinity leading by just four points, but a five-minute spell changed the game thanks to Vagana's quick efforts.

Jake Trueman and Cameron Scott had gone over early to give the visitors the lead before Catalans responded through Toby Sexton.

After Caleb Hamline-Uele and Matthieu Laguerre then put more points on the scoreboard for both outfits, Vagana's moment arrived with just 15 minutes remaining before Scott sealed the deal with his second.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The night was dampened further for Catalans with one minute remaining when Ugo Tison was sent to the sin bin for his hit on Jack Sinfield.

If Wakefield manage to hold onto second until the end of the season, it will be their best ever Super League finish.

Sports.title: Welbeck completes move to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Chelsea have completed the signing of Danny Welbeck from Brighton for an undisclosed fee.

Chelsea have turned to Welbeck as they look to add experience to manager Xabi Alonso's squad.

The last time the west London club paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 was four years ago, when they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona.

Image: Welbeck is set for a medical ahead of a move to Chelsea

It has been two years since Chelsea selected a player over the age of 30 in any game.

Welbeck has continued to be a reliable goalscorer in the Premier League at 35. He scored 13 last season, and 10 during the campaign before that.

His arrival is another example of Chelsea prioritising physically-imposing players with Premier League experience this summer.

They have already signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m - a record fee for a British player - and have brought in Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix.

It would also place further doubt on the futures of strikers Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu.

Chelsea have signed several players from Brighton in recent seasons, including their main striker Joao Pedro, plus Moises Caicedo, Marc Cucurella and Robert Sanchez.

Several Brighton staff members have also moved to Stamford Bridge over the past four years, including sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell.

Welbeck reveals 'immense pride' at move

Welbeck says he already feels at home following "fantastic conversations" with Alonso and his relationships with some of the current Blues squad.

"When you hear of the interest from Chelsea, it's something that fills you with such immense pride," said Welbeck.

"Knowing the history of Chelsea, it's a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season.

"I'm really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time.

"I know a few of the boys already, and I've had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection.

"I've got that fire in my belly, and I'm ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.'

Neville backs Chelsea decision to sign PL experience

Gary Neville has said signing players like Welbeck and Jordan Henderson is exactly what Chelsea's young players need in order to gain more guidance.

The former Premier League-winning captain insists the decision to bring the veterans in is not a "magical" one, but rather an example of what all top teams need to compete.

"If you watched Chelsea for the last three, four or five years you'd say there's inexperience right throughout the football club," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Gary Neville says Chelsea have been crying out for Premier League experience in their squad, backing any decision to sign the likes of Welbeck and Henderson

"I think putting a spine in of good, senior professionals who act as guardians of good behaviour, responsibility and discipline in the dressing room is something that's not magic. It's something all top teams have had for many decades.

"Putting in Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck who know how to win Premier League titles, their jobs will be as much off the pitch as it will be on it. They're still good players who can contribute 25-35 games a season, but they will make sure the young players turn up every single day and give their all.

"I didn't think the young players at Chelsea have any real leadership or guidance on and off the pitch. They've now got people who can do that."

BlueCo's drastic change in transfer policy

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains why Chelsea's transfer policy U-turn - including potential signings Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson - makes sense.

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

The BlueCo era at Chelsea has been defined by hoarding some of the best young talent on the planet and developing them in-house. That method has had some successes, but overall, it has not panned out.

Image: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was the last player over the age of 26 who Chelsea paid a transfer fee for

There is clearly some recognition and accountability from the top brass about that. In bringing in Alonso as manager, they know they have lucked out in getting one of the most sought-after tacticians in the game. The Spaniard has clearly identified the need for experience and the club are following his lead.

The interest in Granit Xhaka earlier in the summer was among the first signs of the shift. Even making a move for Lacroix is evidence of a change in approach.

The Welbeck move is surprising, but there is some logic that can be applied to it. Is he going to start every week? No. However, Chelsea's other four senior strikers have an average age of just 23. Combined, they have made 269 Premier League appearances and scored 74 goals.

Image: Thiago Silva was the last player over the age of 30 to play for Chelsea

The Brighton veteran has 400 appearances and 90 goals on his own. To have that as your back-up to the young guns you want to develop makes sense.

Henderson? That's a complete 180-degree turn. Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez are two of the more experienced players Alonso has. If you had to pick anywhere Chelsea needed a wise head, you would not say midfield.

Yet, they wanted Xhaka. They will soon have Henderson. Alonso may have been the man to oversee the blossoming of players like Florian Wirtz at Bayer Leverkusen. However, he clearly sees the values of opposite characters and knows Chelsea, and perhaps more importantly, he needs people ready now.

Sports.title: There can be no letup. Humiliated Infantino must stand down at Fifa or be removed | Nick Ames
Sports.content:
There is no time to dance around the subject. Gianni Infantino must stand down as Fifa president or otherwise be legally removed. No fresh chances can be made available for an official who has demolished trust in football’s integrity and governance, trashing all remaining credibility of the body that oversees the world’s most-cherished sport.

Infantino was forced into a humiliating climbdown on Saturday morning when he accepted the failure of his plan to sell off portions of the World Cup to private investment. He resolved to resume dialogue about football’s growth “in the spirit of shared interest in our game”. But such a naked attempt to save his own skin cannot hold. Every day Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor.

The overreach involved in unilaterally launching the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme – with its vision to place huge influence on football’s future in the palms of venture capitalists – would be enough to bring down most leaders. But Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond that. He has routinely made a mockery of Fifa’s own statutes and governance regulations, so nobody should be surprised that patience has finally snapped in corridors of power globally. Fifa’s “football unites the world” slogan has never looked more empty.

Article 10.3 of those regulations, which specifically pertains to the presidency, requires the incumbent to ensure “Fifa’s objectives, mission, strategic direction, policies and values are sustainably pursued, protected and implemented, and that a positive image of Fifa is fostered”. It stipulates “promoting friendly and peaceful relations within Fifa”, which is a nonsense given the degree to which federations and senior personnel have distanced themselves from Infantino in recent days.

The rules give no green light to the pursuit of multiple private projects that, most recently in lockstep with the current US administration or its tributaries, have been tabled with scant appetite for oversight or explanation.

Where to begin? The Folarin Balogun saga tipped many leading figures in football, particularly in Europe, towards the edge. There had already been widespread bafflement and disgust at Infantino’s presentation of the new Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump in December, with little background given about the process and highly contestable information provided about the US president’s qualifying achievements. Stakeholders were frustrated by a lack of consultation about the introduction of “hydration breaks”, which fundamentally toyed with the fabric of matches at this summer’s World Cup.

View image in fullscreen The saga involving Folarin Balogun after his ban for a red card was suspended tipped many leading figures in football towards the edge. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

The bizarre expedited bidding process for the 2034 tournament, which resulted in Saudi Arabia’s candidature being waved through in December 2024, also brought widespread criticism. This list only covers the past 20 months of controversies inflicted by Infantino, capped on Friday by revelations that plans for a 64-team World Cup are in full swing.

When a scathing statement from Uefa on Saturday called for an end to “secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game”, it was not only referring to the FFE project and its casual sidelining of other decision makers within Fifa.

A critical mass has been reached. Uefa took a decisive lead in following more than a year of harsh words with strong, united action in pledging to boycott future Fifa tournaments if Infantino did not withdraw his plan. It undoubtedly influenced the outcome and the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, secured an achievement that may define his own reign. But it will mean nothing if Infantino, who is understood to have deployed a major consultancy to smooth relations with federations in recent days, is given the oxygen to dangle fresh promises and turn heads back towards the status quo.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond attempting to launch the Fifa Forward Enterprise unilaterally. Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPA

There is an acknowledgment within Uefa and beyond that the pace must not let up. Senior figures are adamant Infantino must not survive the current scandal. Some insiders feel a crucial next step will be for member associations, the overwhelming majority of whom had formally pledged their support for Infantino’s re-election next March, to recall those letters.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Doing so requires a request to Fifa but could, in sufficient numbers, be a de facto vote of no confidence in Infantino. Fifa had lobbied aggressively for those submissions but many FAs would now be red faced if their expression of fealty towards Infantino was more widely publicised.

Member associations have a duty not to shrink in staving off existential threats to their sport otherwise they, like Infantino, are doing it an egregious disservice. Backing away now would mean leaving the job half done at best.

Uefa have pledged to devise a new method for distributing Fifa’s wealth, delving into its multibillion cash reserves without “selling the family silver”. Behind the scenes it continues to work with other confederations in an effort to find credible candidates for Infantino’s replacement, with a view to running in the election should the Swiss hold on until then. The present crisis can be used to reshape football for the better but only if Infantino is not in situ to impose the final say.

The alternative is that Fifa, and by extension the game, continue lurching from one disaster to the next. It is no laughing matter when the public conversation around football centres on one man, his ego and brazen ventures.

In December Zvonimir Boban, a former sidekick to Infantino as Fifa’s deputy secretary general, told the Guardian that “the way is lost” after the peace prize award to Trump. Fifa will not find a route back until Infantino plays no further part in its operation.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m. Welbeck has agreed a two-year contract and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad on their pre-season tour.

The 35-year-old’s move to Stamford Bridge is a break from Chelsea’s policy of signing younger players with the potential to be developed. It is the first time they have paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 since they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona in 2022 when the striker was 33.
