“When you hear of interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride. Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season,” Welbeck said.

“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”

Alonso was keen to add experience to his squad after last season’s disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League. He opted for Welbeck after the former Manchester United and Arsenal forward enjoyed a memorable campaign with Brighton.

Welbeck, who has 42 caps for England, scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League games last term after netting 10 times in 2024-25.

Welbeck’s arrival in west London will raise questions about the future of Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who signed from Ipswich last season, as well as fellow forwards Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

Welbeck is the latest player to move from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years after João Pedro, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and Marc Cucurella, who joined Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Chelsea spent a British record £117m to sign the England forward Morgan Rogers, 24, from Aston Villa in July. They also secured the France defender Maxence Lacroix, 26, from Crystal Palace for £52m earlier this week and signed Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, 21, for £43m.

Brentford seal record Sangaré deal

Brentford have signed the Mali international Mamadou Sangaré from ⁠Lens for a club-record fee, reported to be £39m. Sangaré, 24, joins Brentford on a five-year contract, with ⁠the option to extend for another year.

“Mamadou ​is someone ‌that we’ve tracked ‌for quite some time. He’s been on ‌our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in,” the Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said. “He’s a humble young man, but he’s equally as ⁠determined to succeed in his career. He ​fits ​everything we want from ​a Brentford player, on and ​off the ‌pitch.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sangaré left Austria’s Rapid Vienna to ‌join Lens last year, and featured prominently as they won the ​French Cup for the first time and finished second in Ligue 1.

View image in fullscreen Mamadou Sangaré has swapped RC Lens for Brentford in a £39m move. Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters

Bournemouth have announced the signing of António Silva from Benfica for a fee believed to be in the region of £25m. The 22-year-old defender becomes new manager Marco Rose’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Álvaro Rodríguez earlier this week.

Silva made 235 senior appearances for Benfica and collected six major honours during his time in Portugal. He told the club website: “I am very happy to be here. It’s a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League.

“The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans. We have everything here that helps us perform on the pitch, and I can’t wait to get started.”

Sports.title: Faster, faster: Iraola in a rush to plug Liverpool gaps before Premier League starts
Sports.content:
“Faster, faster,” bellowed Andoni Iraola throughout the open training session Liverpool held in Chicago on Friday. His first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach ends at the city’s famous Soldier Field Stadium on Sunday, with a friendly against Leeds, and “faster, faster” could apply to all aspects of the club’s preparations for a new Premier League campaign that begins in three weeks’ time.

Iraola was in his element as he immersed himself at the centre of every training drill that Liverpool performed at Chicago Fire’s Endeavor Health Performance Center, their base for the past two weeks in the US. “Faster, faster” was the new head coach’s instruction to his players as three teams of seven worked on their pressing games. He also shouted it when they walked over to a different pitch, recently vacated by Robert Lewandowski and his new Chicago Fire teammates, to work on offensive and defensive set-piece routines. Sprints were demanded following every rondo.

There is an urgency to Iraola’s situation at Liverpool as he works towards his first season in charge, not only to his style of football. Post World-Cup holidays have deprived him of eight first-team players so far, injuries of a further six.

It was telling that, after Liverpool’s open training session had ended, many of the fans invited headed to the gym for a look through its glass windows. Jérémy Jacquet, Liverpool’s £60m recruit from Rennes, was inside working on his recovery from a shoulder problem.

He was joined by Giovanni Leoni, who is rehabilitating from an anterior cruciate ligament rupture and appears to have doubled in chest size since sustaining the injury on his Liverpool debut last September. Nearby was Joe Gomez, who pulled up with a muscle injury eight minutes into the first friendly of the tour. All central defenders, all out.

The concentration of problems in one particular area was a recurring theme under Arne Slot last season and has not eased yet. Two 18-year-olds, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, have impressed in their absence but Liverpool are looking to loan out the latter next season having been unable to secure a work permit.

Among the observers on Friday was Mike Gordon, the president of Liverpool’s owners, Fenway Sports Group, who has returned to a more hands-on role at the club after the departure of Michael Edwards as FSG’s chief executive of football.

View image in fullscreen Teenage defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is likely to be loaned out by Liverppool. Photograph: Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

Gordon is expected to be in attendance at Soldier Field on Sunday when Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak should feature for the first time in pre-season. FSG will not be the only ones at Liverpool looking for a return on their combined £241m investment in the pair.

“We need a very good version of Florian,” Iraola said this week, when confirming he intends to play the Germany international “in that position behind the striker” rather than on the left, where he operated without reward at the World Cup, or in the variety of roles that Slot tried without success.

Wirtz supplying Isak and/or Hugo Ekitiké was always the intended plan of attack for Liverpool last season. The trio ultimately played only 119 minutes together as injuries struck. That stat was never lost on Slot as he was ushered to the exit after a turbulent and toxic campaign.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool need a very good version of Isak, too. The excuse of playing catch-up having missed pre-season, or almost four months of the season due to a fractured ankle and fibula, no longer washes for a striker who featured in all four games of Sweden’s World Cup. Isak has looked sharp in pre-season training. He not only has to sustain that sharpness next season but convince he is a suitable fit for this Liverpool team.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz will be used behind the striker this season under Andoni Iraola for Liverpool. Photograph: Becky Oliver/LFC/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Iraola’s options and vision for Liverpool will improve as senior names return but he undoubtedly requires more help through the transfer market. Work is under way on a move for Bradley Barcola, who is open to leaving Paris Saint-Germain for Anfield, but a deal for a winger who the European champions value at £145m is yet to be struck.

A lack of defensive cover cost Liverpool last season and remains a glaring issue, and there are doubts over the futures of Curtis Jones, Federico Chiesa and Harvey Elliott, among others.

Liverpool’s head coach has admitted he “hates this month of August” because of the uncertainty that surrounds players while the season starts. “It’s difficult to build a proper team with a lot of question marks,” he added. Between Soldier Field on Sunday and St James’ Park on 23 August, the building work must accelerate.

Sports.title: De Zerbi wants ‘lovely guy’ Richarlison to stay at Tottenham after winner sinks Chelsea
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi wants Richarlison to stay at Tottenham, but says the striker, who has been linked with a move away, is still unsure about his future.

The Brazilian scored a last-gasp winner as 10-man Tottenham defeated Chelsea 2-1 in a pre-season friendly in Sydney, with Kevin Danso sent off just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute.

Speaking after the game, De Zerbi said Richarlison had not clarified if he was going to depart this summer. “I don’t know, I didn’t understand well, because sometimes he said to stay, sometimes he leaves, we have to speak. Anyway, there is not any problem, he’s a lovely guy. All of us love him, the teammates, the club, the staff, because he works hard every day.”

Richarlison has less than a year left on his contract after joining Tottenham from Everton in 2022. He has struggled to find consistent form during his time in north London but De Zerbi said it would be difficult to replace his goals.

“For me he’s still an important player because it’s not so easy to find another striker as Richarlison, because Richarlison scored goals and he knows the way. The new striker, we don’t know, the other striker, we don’t know. He [Richarlison] scored 12 goals last season, not for luck, because he feels the way to score.”

Richarlison bagged a 92nd-minute winner for Tottenham against Chelsea in front of more than 80,000 fans at Sydney’s Accor Stadium. The Brazilian was the first player to react after Jamie Donley’s shot came back off a post, prodding the ball into an empty net to avert the need for a penalty shootout.

It was the first time that the two sides have met outside the UK and the match started in the spirit of a true London derby. Conor Gallagher flew into a challenge on Dário Essugo after 10 minutes, picking up a yellow card and a fair few heckles from the largely Chelsea-supporting crowd. Jan Paul van Hecke clattered into João Pedro, while Dominic Solanke and Levi Colwill tussled off the ball.

This fixture has had its fair share of red cards over the years and there was another one to add to the list, after Danso was sent off three minutes after coming off the bench. A poor surface got the better of the Spurs defender as he failed to control a backpass, allowing João Pedro to run on to the ball and through on goal. Danso lunged headfirst into the Chelsea forward, with the referee reaching straight for his pocket.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Danso is shown a red card three minutes after coming on as a substitute. Photograph: David Neilson/EPA

De Zerbi said the sending off made the game harder for both sides. “It was worse for us and for Chelsea, because if you consider the condition of the pitch, very bad. And if you consider we are starting from two weeks, maybe less than three weeks, the second half you start the fatigue and playing, attacking against 10 players behind the line of the ball is tough for every team.”

De Zerbi’s side were on top in the early stages and took a deserved lead on 17 minutes when the new signing Sandro Tonali scored his first goal for Tottenham. The midfielder’s side-footed effort from outside the area took a deflection, wrong-footing the Chelsea goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe before nestling into the bottom corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Spurs were only ahead for four minutes, as Estêvão Willian got the better of Andy Robertson to head home at the back post after some good work from Jamie Gittens down the left.

The game lost its competitive edge in the second half with both sides making a flurry of substitutions, before Richarlison settled it at the death.

Chelsea will now head to Hong Kong where they will be joined by Mykhailo Mudryk, who has been cleared to play again after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved his appeal against a ban for failing a doping test. The Ukrainian winger was suspended for four years after failing a drug test in 2024. De Zerbi, who managed Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk, said he viewed the player as one of his “sons”.

“I’m very happy – he deserves to play, he’s a good guy, top player. Hopefully he can show what he suffered in the last two years, in the next season, maybe not against Tottenham, but he’s a lovely guy and he’s a very, very good player.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Mayo and Nisbet strike late to help Aberdeen stun Hearts
Sports.content:
Hearts’ miserable summer continued as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1 to Aberdeen in their Premiership opener at Pittodrie.

Wouter Vrancken and Hearts looked on course for a much-needed victory after a turbulent few months as they led through Oisin McEntee’s first-half goal. But just as they looked to be closing out a first win at Pittodrie for more than a decade, Lewis Mayo equalised in the 90th minute before Kevin Nisbet won it for Aberdeen with a stoppage-time penalty after Stuart Findlay was sent off for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.

It was a third consecutive defeat for Vrancken, who has endured a chastening start since replacing Derek McInnes in June.

The Aberdeen manager, Stephen Robinson, whose side had built up some momentum by winning each of their four Premier Sports Cup group-stage matches, pitched Chris Cadden straight into his starting lineup a day after he joined from Hibernian.

There were five changes to the Hearts side that lost Wednesday’s Champions League qualifier at home to Sturm Graz, with the goalkeeper Beau Reus and Laurent Mendy handed their debuts and Sabah Kerjota – more than a year after joining – and Amadou Ba-Sy given their first competitive starts.

In what was their first league match since being pipped to the title by Celtic in May, the 1,600-strong travelling support could be regularly heard singing anti-Scottish Football Association songs in protest at the contentious calls from officials in the closing matches of last season that they felt cost them dear in their quest for glory.

Following a summer of transition and a 6-0 aggregate defeat by Sturm Graz that had done little to improve the mood of the fans since that agonising end to the past campaign, there was a sense of trepidation in some quarters about the prospect of kicking off the new season at Pittodrie, where they had not won in their previous 14 visits.

Hearts’ makeshift defence – with the midfielder McEntee playing at centre-half following an injury to Malachi Fagan-Walcott – looked to have allowed the Aberdeen captain Nisbet to get clean through in the third minute but McEntee recovered well to scramble the ball behind for a corner.

Nisbet then glanced a header just wide from Connor Ronan’s corner in the 27th minute, although clear chances were generally at a premium.

Hearts made the breakthrough in the 35th minute after some pinball in the penalty area. Ba-Sy’s cutback from the left broke to Blair Spittal, whose shot was blocked by Nesta Guinness-Walker on the edge of the six-yard box and the fellow defender Dan Happe’s attempt to clear ran into the path of McEntee, who shot low into the net from seven yards.

The visitors generally looked comfortable for most of the second period, with Cláudio Braga spurning a good chance to double their lead.

Aberdeen had offered little as an attacking force but they levelled in the 90th minute when Mayo bundled in from close range after Happe headed Ronan’s free-kick back into the danger area.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Toyosi Olusanya was hauled down by Findlay, who saw red, and Nisbet despatched the spot-kick.

The St Mirren manager, Craig McLeish, believes his team’s 2-0 win at Falkirk augurs well for a successful campaign.

McLeish is convinced his squad will improve on last season’s struggles before he steered Saints to safety when the interim head coach.

He has set a high bar of the top six and a European qualification bid this term, and a double from Killian Phillips helped St Mirren get off to a fine start at Falkirk Stadium.

“I thought the performance was excellent and if we can build on that we can go and achieve something as a group,” McLeish said. “I’m delighted for the group. We got the result our performance deserved. I thought we were excellent.”

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley consortium set to buy Gold family’s 25.1% stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has reached an agreement to buy a ‌25.1% stake in West ⁠Ham after Vanessa Gold, daughter of the former chair David Gold, ⁠agreed to sell ⁠her ​family’s shares in the Championship club.

The move by the businesswoman who helped lead the Saudi consortium takeover of Newcastle comes after a previously agreed sale to fellow shareholder and Czech businessman ⁠Daniel Kretinsky fell through.

The Gold family ​trust owns the 25.1% stake in West Ham, ‌who were relegated from the Premier League last season just two seasons after winning the Europa Conference League in 2023. However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.

Gold said in a statement: “As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023. Whether as a youth team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father’s priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.

“On June 12, Daniel Kretínsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

View image in fullscreen West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/Reuters

“In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family’s shareholding to a consortium led by Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

“While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions. My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham. While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club’s best interests, as my father did and would expect of me.”



Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy-out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club’s rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.

The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on 16 August.

Sports.title: Marketing stunt or ‘extraordinary’ transfer? Ravenna fans ride wave of the Ronaldinho Effect
Sports.content:
On a scorching summer afternoon in Ravenna, a city far better known for its fifth-century Byzantine mosaics and Dante’s tomb than for footballing glory, eyes are peeled in the historic centre for one of world football’s most recognisable figures – a man who featured in the World Cup final half-time show alongside Madonna and Ronaldo: Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, better known as Ronaldinho.

“We haven’t seen him yet,” four Ravenna supporters sitting at a cafe say with dry irony as they flip through La Gazzetta dello Sport, Italy’s famous pink sports daily. They are undeniably sceptical, viewing the signing as a purely commercial operation, yet deep down they still harbour the dream of seeing the 2005 Ballon d’Or and 2002 World Cup winner wear their yellow and red shirt.

It is a small, surreal glimpse into the whirlwind that has engulfed this quiet corner of Emilia-Romagna, thanks to the business instinct of Ignazio Cipriani. Heir to the Venetian hospitality dynasty behind the renowned Harry’s Bar, Cipriani took over the club in 2024 when they were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football. A native of Ravenna, he is the grandson of Raul Gardini, the Italian chemicals tycoon and sailor who steered Il Moro di Venezia to the 1992 America’s Cup final.

In his first year as president, Cipriani oversaw victory in the Serie D Cup and promotion to the professional ranks of Serie C. But that is merely the first step in a long ascent, he says: “It’s not a provocation. Serie A is the goal I declared from day one because I intend to reach it. And the Champions League remains the ultimate horizon we want to walk towards, step by step. I made this statement because I like working with my back against the wall: when you have no way out, you are forced to find solutions instead of excuses. I prefer to remove every alibi from the beginning.”

And this summer, Cipriani pulled off a surprise move – so surprising that anyone reading the headlines assumed it was a prank: bringing the 46-year-old Ronaldinho back as a player.

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho holds up a Ravenna top with Ignazio Cipriani, the club president, after the surprise move was announced in Miami in June. Photograph: Rebecca Blackwell/AP

“We met through Lorenzo Tonetti and Ariedo Braida,” Cipriani says, “two people who worked for over 20 years at AC Milan and had Ronaldinho as a player. The idea of involving him was a dream I cultivated as soon as I bought the club. Thanks to Lorenzo and Ariedo, we met, started talking, and a genuine friendship grew. From that relationship came many ideas for the club’s growth. And to the question everyone is asking, I am happy to answer: Ronaldinho will wear the Ravenna shirt as a player, and he will try – maybe scoring the last goal of his career with us!”

Meanwhile, a dedicated website has already put a special-edition shirt on sale featuring the “R10” logo – the Brazilian’s personal brand – which sold out within a few hours. It represents a striking collision of high-end global branding, small-town football, and brilliantly executed marketing stunt.

“If someone had told me three years ago that Ronaldinho was coming to Ravenna, I would have sent them straight to the psychiatric ward,” says Fabio laughing, a lifelong supporter. “The night the news broke, international headlines everywhere read ‘Ronaldinho to Ravenna’. It was an extraordinary operation.”

Ravenna is no footballing giant. Plagued by bankruptcies in 2001 and 2012, the club has spent decades bouncing around the lower tiers, with seven seasons in Serie B the highest point. Historically a volleyball stronghold, the football scene was accustomed to modest budgets and regional rivalries.

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho will be aiming to wow the crowds at Ravenna’s Stadio Bruno Benelli this season. Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The Guardian

“Ronaldinho is a unique icon,” Cipriani says. “His way of playing made my generation fall in love with the game. We want him today to make the next generation of fans, in Italy and around the world, fall in love with Ravenna . It’s not just a visibility stunt; it’s about building a bridge between different eras of football and growing a truly global fanbase around it.”

To support this ambitious sporting and industrial project, the club is working with the municipality to renovate the Stadio Bruno Benelli, increasing its capacity beyond 6,300. But the president’s ultimate dream is a new multi-purpose venue open seven days a week, featuring retail spaces, concert facilities, and an integrated Hotel Cipriani linked to the city’s international tourism expansion.

For Ravenna’s mayor, Alessandro Barattoni, the arrival of a world-famous figure fits neatly into a broader strategy to promote the city globally. In recent years, Ravenna has been expanding its international reach beyond traditional beach tourism and commercial ports. The city is enjoying renewed ties with the Anglo-Saxon world, highlighted by a recent visit from the British royal family and the opening of the Lord Byron Museum.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Ronaldinho brings a whole new level of global fame,” Barattoni says. “When the news broke, my phone exploded with messages from former schoolmates. For younger kids today, he might be someone to discover on YouTube, but the fascination remains intact.” With a smile, the mayor adds that, schedule permitting, he would be delighted to personally guide Ronaldinho on a tour of the city’s cultural heritage.

However, Barattoni is quick to clarify the institution’s role: “Our common ground with the club is internationalisation: bringing Ravenna’s image to the world. Ronaldinho has been a global ambassador for countless brands. There is an overarching project that can bring great visibility to the team and allow the city to showcase its initiatives beyond standard routes.” He adds: “Even before Ronaldinho’s arrival, the club did a fantastic job engaging younger generations. The average age in the stands is lower, more vibrant, and more engaged than ever before. A genuine sense of community is forming.”

View image in fullscreen Alessandro Barattoni, the mayor of Ravenna, is confident the Ronaldinho transfer will be positive for the Italian city. Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The Guardian

Yet, fears of a hyper-commercialised image linger among traditional supporters. In the Curva Mero, such marketing moves are approached with caution. “There is a certain reluctance among some factions,” Fabio admits. “Modern football pushes values that many don’t share: rising ticket prices, losing accessibility for lower-income families. As a result, visibility and marketing stunts risk being viewed sideways.”

Cipriani demonstrates an acute awareness of these dynamics: “Without roots, no global project makes sense,” the president says. “Ravenna is not a brand we are building from scratch; it’s a history and an identity that existed before us. Tradition isn’t a brake on ambition: it’s the foundation. A club without its people is worth nothing.”

“I’m 50 years old and I’ve been coming to the stadium since my school days,” says Giovanni, another fan. “I’m rediscovering the enthusiasm of the past. If it takes an icon like Ronaldinho and a local entrepreneur to make us dream of Serie A, then so be it. The important thing is never to forget the people in the stands.”

Riding the wave of the “Ronaldinho Effect”, the season-ticket campaign has just launched with a target of selling 2,800. Ticket prices have risen by an average of about 12%, with variations across different stadium sections.

For now, Ravenna is soaking up a dizzying, galvanising atmosphere. On the pitch, the club is assembling a squad to win the league; off it, the city awaits 20 August, when Ronaldinho is expected to appear during a three-day summer festival in nearby Marina di Ravenna, organised in signature Cipriani style.

Sports.title: Women’s football continues to be used as a pawn in Gianni Infantino’s Fifa tenure | Suzanne Wrack
Sports.content:
Despite not having been deemed worthy of more than a single mention in Fifa’s 25-page sales deck to its 211 member associations on its doomed proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, now very expensive waste paper, it was women’s football that had found itself on the frontline in the fight for the “soul of football”.

Uefa’s statement that European national teams would not “participate in any Fifa competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that Fifa will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership”, was a bold, necessary and effective declaration of war against the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino.

However, with the Under-20 Women’s World Cup being held in Poland next month; the Under-17 Women’s World Cup and Uefa’s qualifying playoffs for the senior tournament both beginning in October; and the big one, the Women’s World Cup itself, taking place in Brazil next summer, women’s tournaments would have been the first test cases had a boycott gone ahead.

There was no further detail on the FA’s plans for England’s two-legged World Cup playoff against Greece, but Uefa’s call for a boycott would have had an impact on the women’s game in September.

A boycott of the Women’s World Cup would have been catastrophic and yet that was the likely consequence of Infantino’s deadline. The 2023 Women’s World Cup was the first to break even after generating more than $570m (£424m) in revenue and Fifa said in May 2025 it is targeting $1bn in revenue from the 2027 edition.

The women’s game is so desperately reliant on international competition for accelerating its growth that the knock-on impact of having no World Cup would have set progress back far more than four years.

However, Uefa was not wrong in its stance and the subsequent collapse of Infantino’s masterplan after the almighty fallout from demonstrates as much. It was not European football’s governing body that engineered the timeframe that put women’s football on the frontline and it was correct not to exclude women’s football, or youth football, from its arsenal in the fight back against Infantino’s attempt to steamroller through his plans.

View image in fullscreen England’s dream of avenging their World Cup final defeat in 2023 was thrown into doubt by Gianni Infantino’s proposals. Photograph: Zac Goodwin/PA

The blame for the threat posed by a boycott on women’s football lay squarely at the feet of Gianni “I have four daughters” Infantino, who was praised in February by Jill Ellis, Fifa’s chief football officer and twice a World Cup-winning coach, for his “commitment to accelerating the women’s game and increasing women’s influence in shaping its future” and under whose leadership “investment has moved from rhetoric to action”.

To an extent Ellis is right – Infantino is the Fifa president who has done the most for the women’s game. But when his predecessor is Sepp Blatter, a man who said in 2004 that “tighter shorts” was the way to get more people watching the women’s game, the bar is staggeringly low.

Yes, under Infantino Fifa has invested more in the women’s game than ever before, but it has been a pawn in his tenure: initially useful for showing just how progressive and in tune with modern society he and Fifa are, and now useful because it presents an opportunity for medium- to long-term financial gain as one of the fastest growing and least‑tapped areas of the game.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Step behind the rhetoric and handouts and Infantino’s real attitude to the women’s game is evident. In 2023 Sky News reported the Fifa president had left the Women’s World Cup for Tahiti after less than a week, before returning later in the tournament. By contrast, he went to at least some part of every one of the 64 games of the 2022 men’s World Cup and at times appeared at two a day during the latest men’s edition despite the huge environmental impact of using a private jet.

View image in fullscreen The 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil starts in less than 11 months. Photograph: Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters

Perhaps Infantino waited until the beginning of a new four-year men’s World Cup cycle to try to limit the impact of any backlash on the showpiece event, but in doing so he added to the pile of evidence demonstrative of real attitude towards women’s football, with women’s edition of the tournament on the imminent horizon.

It would have been oddly fitting, then, if the women’s game had become the sun that melted his Icarus wings. Luckily, women’s football didn’t have to pay that costly price. However, this episode must act as a warning, both to those who care about the development of the women’s game and its future and those who care about the future of the men’s game.

The reality is that the European Super League debacle and this latest and most blatant of attempts to hand the wealth of football to private finance vultures show that private finance will keep coming back as they search for ways to get a piece of the pie.

Sports.title: Why Rob Key picked Stephen Fleming over England's up-and-coming coaches: The coaching 'shift' that has swept cricket, why foreigners are judged through a different prism and the county coach who has been harshly overlooked
Sports.content:
There are many reasons that few Englishmen go on to coach England these days: the results of those that have gone before hang heavy, a mistrust of the country’s embedded coaching system has developed and so has an infatuation with star names.

This century only Peter Moores (twice) and Chris Silverwood have been given the privilege of calling themselves Test coach and between them they lost more matches than they won - the numbers being 24 and 23 respectively.

That might appear to be a tough yardstick to be judged by, but such statistics will have influenced Rob Key in his decision to appoint New Zealander Stephen Fleming despite a lack of first-class coaching experience, ahead of Richard Dawson, perhaps the brightest coaching talent in the country and one with silverware on his CV.

Some will argue, perhaps with justification that Dawson’s achievements with two unfashionable counties have not been given commensurate weighting in this selection process. Gloucestershire supporters look back on their Lord’s one-day cup final win in 2015 as one of the club’s finest achievements while he has Glamorgan as high as fourth in the County Championship after his first season in charge concluded with promotion last September.

In between those two jobs, there was the small matter of overseeing an eight-match England Lions tour of Australia in early 2020, returning home undefeated having won the four-day ‘Test’ against Australia A.

On Friday, Key spoke of ‘working on’ homegrown coaches to ‘upskill’ them, saying more experiences needed to be created for them overseas. That such development would not be a quick fix. Yet Dawson’s very positive experience of winning in Australia was six years ago. He has knowledge of lots of conditions around the world garnered from various England tours.

With the appointment of Stephen Fleming, there is the suggestion that England have overlooked attracting one of their own - such as Richard Dawson

Fleming (left, with ex-team-mate and former England coach Brendon McCullum in 2008) is a much starrier name

It feels like a case of disregard for the coaching path from which Dawson - whose standoffish demeanour should not detract from the fact he is an excellent coach well respected by the country’s leading players - has emerged.

Key has shown little regard for the traditional level four coaching qualification that the ECB has asked the country’s best coaches to complete for the past quarter of a century, instead appointing those with limited or no coaching backgrounds in the form of former playing greats Brendon McCullum and Andrew Flintoff to high position.

Investment has been in inspiration not perspiration. Overall, McCullum has proved to be a success across four years and three England teams, but said early on: ‘Don’t expect me to be on the tools.’ But Flintoff has proved more of a mentor than coach since taking over the Lions two years ago, and will skip some of next winter’s programme in South Africa to coach Sydney Thunder in the Big Bash League.

It is part of a wider culture of ‘image’ taking precedent over results. When the Hundred launched in 2021, not a single coach was English. The late Shane Warne was chosen by London Spirit; experienced international coaches like Andy Flower, Darren Lehmann and Gary Kirsten were signed; the two emerging coaches were New Zealander Daniel Vettori and Australian Simon Katich.

Key is part of a shifting cricket culture that places names over deeds and achievements abroad over ones here.

The last six County Championship titles have been claimed by teams with English coaches: Moores (Nottinghamshire), Gareth Batty (Surrey), Mark Robinson (Warwickshire) and Anthony McGrath (Yorkshire).

If we do not have confidence in our own production line, why should we expect others to? Work abroad has been limited: Silverwood and Paul Farbrace (both Sri Lanka), Bob Woolmer (Pakistan) and Jonathan Trott (Afghanistan) rare examples of those to have taken head coach jobs of Test-playing nations this century.

Vikram Solanki is the only Englishman to move from a county position to one at the Indian Premier League, as director of cricket at Gujarat Titans. Moores was the only English coach at the Big Bash League last winter.

However, there is evidence of a shift. Ian Bell has been on coaching staffs at both tournaments. Others have ventured to the BBL to gain experience through observational or backroom roles. Andrew Gale, formerly of Yorkshire, is making big waves as a coach with Tasmania and was promoted to work with Australia A last winter.

Peter Moores is one of few English coaches able to have the privilege of calling themselves England Test coach this century

But like his compatriot Chris Silverwood, Moores lost more Test matches than he won

Foreigners appear to be judged through a different prism. For all of Fleming’s widely acknowledged man-management skills, tactical acumen and calm, calculated persona, he has never won a trophy without MS Dhoni as his captain.

Marcus Trescothick, meanwhile, failed to make the shortlist this time despite four years of experience under McCullum in which his one major failing was insisting there had been no talk of the dangers of driving on the up after first Test defeat in Perth, in keeping with the regime’s off-the-cuff policy.

Trescothick did a sound job as McCullum’s stand-in on the limited-overs tour of the Caribbean two years ago, coming home with a rare series win over West Indies, and will step up again against Pakistan.

He has been produced by a country with a revered coaching system that has launched several individuals on the road to international head coach jobs around the world.

Australia coach Andrew McDonald completed his coaching badges by the age of 27, cutting his teeth here seven years later, starting at the bottom of the pile with a Leicestershire side that had gone winless for two seasons while continue to play back in his homeland.

In improving the midlands club’s finishing positions in both the 2015 and 2016 seasons, he established a reputation as one of the brightest young coaches on the global circuit, something he gave further credence to when in his first senior coaching position in Australia he marked his debut campaign of 2016-17 by taking Victoria to the Sheffield Shield title.

At Grace Road, McDonald could put into play his belief in a hands-off approach, making players take greater responsibility and use his own previous struggles with the mental side of the sport to liberate the thinking of a team previously suffocated by struggle.

The fierce loyalty he has developed towards players was arguably forged through witnessing a group of low achievers rise above their stations with the right backing.

The art of managing people, he says, is what he invested in most as a coach. A six-month season that barely pauses for breath allows the time to get to know the individuals concerned. It gave him a steep learning curve.

Ottis Gibson won the Twenty20 World Cup with West Indies, defeated both Australia and India in Test series while in charge of South Africa and was England’s bowling coach on two occasions, having gone through the ECB coaching programme in the first decade of this century.

Gibson was mentored by an Australian Troy Cooley, but both were very much part of the English system.

Another Australian Jason Gillespie was exposed to the pressure of ending Yorkshire’s trophy drought as a young coach fresh from a maiden stint in Zimbabwe, and responded by delivering back-to-back Championships in 2014-15. Like Gibson, he moved onto the international scene, albeit briefly, with Pakistan.

Others are grateful for what the county system offers. Perhaps it’s time for us to be so too.

Sports.title: Club at centre of 'Clicky Ponting' scandal hit by fresh 'cheating' claims as umpire releases footage of ANOTHER player seemingly clicking fingers
Sports.content:
A fresh controversy has engulfed the amateur cricket club at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal after an umpire released footage appearing to show another player deploying the same tactic.

Saltburn Cricket Club has been at the centre of a storm after fielder Brian Devine allegedly cheated during a Second XI Division Two match against Norton. Video footage of Devine appearing to be clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of a bat edge, tricking the umpire into giving the batsman out, went viral on social media.

On Monday, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League launched an investigation into Devine, 38, who has since been suspended by the club for the 'foreseeable future'.

Now, fresh footage has emerged appearing to show another Saltburn player successfully using the same tactic during a Third XI match against Marton.

The fielder appears to click his fingers as the ball flies past the bat and into the wicketkeeper's gloves, prompting the on-field umpire to give the batsman out. The footage was posted on social media by Berkshire-based umpire Andy Smy.

The captain of another team in the same league earlier this week claimed the alleged tactic had not been confined to Saltburn's victory over Norton.

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

He said: 'It was not confined to just one game. I was at the other end when one of our players was dismissed and I heard a big sound as the ball went through and immediately thought: "He's out."

'The umpire didn't hesitate either, but our batsman was adamant he was nowhere near the ball and couldn't understand the loud click.

'In all we had three batsmen given out caught behind, but all of them said they hadn't touched the ball. One protested so much the umpire had to speak to him and threaten him with a warning.

'I know of at least three other teams who now have suspicions and it should be noted that in one match against Shildon their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

'You hear of all kinds of things going on in cricket but this is something I haven't heard of before. I hope the league takes appropriate action.'

Earlier this week, Saltburn's Second XI forfeited their match against Marton, dumping themselves out of a cup competition, with a source close to the league saying 'none of the players will have wanted anything to do with this game while they're under such focus'.

They did, however, return to the field on Saturday for a league match against Marton, where table-toppers Saltburn crashed to a nine-wicket defeat. With Devine no longer fielding at slip, Marton chased down their target of 101 in just 20 overs.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his alleged actions on the cricket field

Saltburn player has been caught on camera seeming to be clicking his fingers

And Devine, a father and auction mart worker from Guisborough, North Yorkshire, is planning to 'lie low' until the scandal dies down.

A friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world - in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK, of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction from around the world has knocked him sideways.'

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League said it was treating the allegations of cheating 'with the utmost seriousness' and called for the 'rights of all parties' to be respected amid intense scrutiny on social media.

'We would want to place on record our genuine concern for the welfare of those at Saltburn Cricket Club and ask for all to take that into account. There are many people at the club and one of our aims will be to provide them with any wellbeing support we can,' the league said.

'Whilst we understand, to some degree, the interest this issue has generated in the press and media, it is imperative that, now this process is under way, the rights of all parties are observed, including the overriding principles of natural justice and the right to a fair hearing for any individual or entity concerned.

'Anything less risks prejudicing any formal action which may follow.'

Saltburn, in a statement on Wednesday, said: 'This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club run entirely by volunteers.'

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal will be 'very ambitious' in the transfer market with club refusing to give up on sensational Vinicius Jr deal
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta would not be drawn on questions about Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior, but he did insist the champions were ‘very ambitious’ and ‘won’t sit still’ in the summer market.

The 26-year-old winger has been heavily linked with a move to north London as Arteta looks to bolster his frontline.

Vinicius’ contract at Real Madrid expires next summer and the Gunners are interested in signing the player.

Just days after Arteta said that new signings are needed to take Arsenal to a ‘different dimension’, he doubled down on his assertions.

When asked about whether more signings are expected in light of the Vinicius reports, Arteta said following Arsenal’s 4-1 pre-season victory over Girona: ‘Well we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else.

Vinicius’ contract at Real Madrid expires next summer and the Gunners are interested in signing the 26-year-old Brazilian winger

‘And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing - we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do.

‘The margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that's the way we have to think.’

Max Dowman shone with a goal and an assist in the match, issuing a reminder ahead of what could be an important season for the 16-year-old.

‘That's what we want,’ added Arteta. 'When you play for Arsenal, the expectations should be high and should be expecting really good things.

'We know what he's (Dowman) capable of doing. We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver.

‘But I think today he had a really good game.’

Sports.title: Dominant Josh Kerr powers to gold in the mile race at Commonwealth Games - two weeks after shattering world record
Sports.content:
Dominant Josh Kerr powers to gold in the mile race at Commonwealth Games - two weeks after shattering world record

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It felt like the ghosts of 1954 were chasing Josh Kerr down the home straight of the Scotstoun track. Stories from the famous battle between Sir Roger Bannister and John Landy pumped nostalgia into every step of this Miracle Mile.

Queen Elizabeth II was just two years into her reign for that epic clash in Vancouver. Her great grandchildren were in the crowd for this one, braving the Glaswegian chill to watch Kerr push and shove his way to gold.

More than seven decades have passed since Bannister's victory but Kerr's spirit when he made his move in the final lap would survive the test of time. The Scotsman was boxed in with 400 metres to go, before he shoved Kenya's Brian Komen out of the way and charged from the middle of the pack.

This is the place where Kerr set personal bests in the shot put and high jump as a schoolboy. He watched his brother play rugby here for Edinburgh and, at times, this race had the physicality of a Scottish scrum.

'Welcome the world champion and the world record holder,' blasted the stadium announcer. As if this race did not have enough storylines to it, the stadium announcer was the father of fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished sixth.

Like Kerr, Wightman knows this place well. Both raced here for Edinburgh Athletics Club as juniors. Wightman is renowned for his sprint finish but he could not catch Kerr, who turned his bedroom into an altitude chamber to increase his lung capacity for moments like this.

Scotland's Josh Kerr surged clear of the field to claim a dominant gold medal in the mile event

There was even more anticipation for this race than when Usain Bolt stepped onto the Glasgow track for the relay in 2014. Hometown heroes, champions, record holders, Olympians were all in the mix. This was a world-class field.

Two weeks ago, Kerr broke the mile record at London Stadium. Bannister and Landy did the same before Vancouver, famously breaching the four-minute barrier for the first time.

They did not have the same footwear as the Scotsman, whose running spikes were engineered in a laboratory in Seattle.

'It definitely felt a little bit overkill - like driving a formula one car along the street for a cup of coffee,' said Kerr after his heat on Thursday.

To the untrained eye, they look like trainers that are missing the heel. Their 'rocking' midsole is designed to maximise the energy return on every stride. They were formulated to break the world record at London Stadium, where Kerr had smooth pacemakers and the shelter of ginormous stands.

Championship racing is different. The racers constantly changed pace as they jostled for position - with Botswana's Thesipo Masalela setting the pace in the opening lap.

Gusts of wind rip through Scotstoun, whipping up the 74 Commonwealth flags behind the finish line. The heatwave in the south of England, it is safe to say, did not make its way to Glasgow.

Kerr's face has greeted every commuter arriving into Glasgow, his image looming large on the billboards outside Central Station. He slicked back his hair before the starting gun, having had a fresh trim a few hours before the race. He knew this was his moment to shine.

'This is absolutely incredible,' he said. 'Doing it in front of the Scottish crowd where I learned how to race. I came here week after week as a kid. I didn't waste any energy. I knew the opportunity would open up and I had enough energy to put a gap on them in the last few hundred. I went early to save everyone some stress.

'With the World Indoors and going after the record in London, this was the one we had circled on the calendar before any of that.

'I didn't put together my performance I wanted in Birmingham 2022. I think a British crowd deserved more from me – I owed them that for sure.

No Scotsman has been named BBC Sports Personality of the Year since Andy Murray in 2016. The bookies had Kerr as joint favourite with Jude Bellingham to be named sports personality of the year before this race. This victory may well nudge the odds in his favour.

Interest in middle distance racing has waned over the years. Seb Coe, Steve Ovett, and Steve Cram enjoyed a golden era in the 1980s. This race felt like a resurrection.

Sports.title: Former Man City captain, 56, gives positive health update after being diagnosed with devastating neurological condition as he returns to co-commentary work
Sports.content:
Former Man City captain, 56, gives positive health update after being diagnosed with devastating neurological condition as he returns to co-commentary work

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Manchester City captain Andy Morrison has given an encouraging update on his health following his battle with devastating neurological condition Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

Morrison, 56, revealed in a heartbreaking video online earlier this year that he was battling the condition as he vowed to fight the disorder.

In May, he appeared in good spirits as he explained his symptoms and detailed how his recovery was going to take 'a long, long time'.

Now, however, in a new video, Morrison appeared to be much further down his road to recovery as he revealed he has returned to commentary work.

'Evening everyone,' he began after work covering City's pre-season defeat by Inter Milan. 'Just a quick update after the first day back working at City with the matchday live team, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

'It was fantastic to be back. Felt the voice was strong enough to go back and do co-commentary today. That's my first time back in five-and-a-half months. I really appreciate all the support and working with Ali Mann, who makes it very easy.

Great to be back 🩵⚽️🙏 pic.twitter.com/VW1nUplE0N — Andy Morrison (@AndyMorri5on) August 1, 2026

Former Manchester City captain Andy Morrison has given fans an update on his battle with a devastating neurological condition. Left: pictured this week, right: pictured in May

The former defender previously revealed that it will take him a year to fully recover

'An enjoyable game. I struggled with a few words, a few names, but nothing too bad. I did struggle with (Ryan) McAidoo. Could have a player there by the way, watch this space. There was enough there to think he could be the next one on the conveyor belt, hugely impressive in the second-half.

'Birthday yesterday, that was a great day with grandkids and family. I had a specialist on Wednesday and it was really positive, he was really delighted and amazed at the progress I had made, from House-Brackmann (nerve grading scale) six to a four and he is really positive that within a year I'll get my eye back and be able to blink, so I won't have to tape it down at night.

'I still have to take juice to swallow and I have no taste in the side of my mouth and the whole side of the face is numb, so I have to drink through a straw still. He wasn't sure just how much that would progress because it's still really weak. But if sucking through a straw is worst case scenario then so be it. I won't be posting now because I won't see a specialist for another three months.

'A really good day and it just felt great to be back doing something when that seemed a million miles away. I didn't get out of bed for four weeks and couldn't speak for a month. I had some really dark days in this conservatory but I stayed positive and this too shall pass, everything passes, good or bad, everything comes and goes and sometimes you just have to dig in and get through it. But thanks for listening and see you all soon.'

Morrison made 47 appearances for Manchester City after joining from Huddersfield Town in 1998.

He helped guide the club to the old Division One via the play-offs in 1998-99 before winning promotion to the Premiership the following season.

Voted as Man City's third best captain ever in their official magazine, the Scot was named as a club ambassador in 2013.

Ramsay Hunt Syndrome is caused by a virus in the facial nerve and can lead to ipsilateral face paralysis, blistering rashes near the ear, severe earache and hearing loss.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham continues his homecoming tour as he watches the cricket after investing in The Hundred franchise Birmingham Phoenix - hours after hero's welcome at his former football club
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham continued his homecoming tour on Saturday by visiting Edgbaston, just a day after receiving a hero's welcome at his former football club Birmingham City.

The Real Madrid midfielder, who grew up in nearby Stourbridge, purchased a 1.2 per cent stake in The Hundred franchise Birmingham Phoenix earlier this year and has previously spoken about his love for cricket, saying he and his brother Jobe used to 'scrap' when playing it growing up and that it's now his 'favourite thing to watch outside football'.

On Saturday at the famous cricket ground, Bellingham was there to enjoy plenty of action, particularly in the first women's game. He watched on as Phoenix won their opening match of the women's competition in dramatic fashion, defeating Welsh Fire with just one ball remaining.

The England star was also on hand to present captain Donovan Ferreira with the coin for the toss in the subsequent men's match, although the 23-year-old wasn't able to inspire victory as the hosts slumped to defeat by Welsh Fire. England's newly confirmed Test captain Joe Root guided the visitors to victory with four balls remaining.

Hundreds of millions of pounds in private investment cash has been injected in The Hundred with all eight teams having been either partially or fully taken over by new owners as part of significant financial investment into the competition since last year. Upon announcing his own involvement with the franchise, Bellingham said: 'I feel like I owe the city something. And this feels like a good way.'

The Real Madrid midfielder, who grew up in nearby Stourbridge, purchased a 1.2 per cent stake in The Hundred franchise Birmingham Phoenix earlier this year

Bellingham was in attendance as Phoenix won their first match in the women's competition in dramatic fashion, defeating Welsh Fire with just one ball remaining

He as previously spoken about how he and his brother Jobe used to 'scrap' when playing it growing up and that it's now his 'favourite thing to watch outside football'

Upon announcing his own involvement with the franchise, Bellingham said: 'I feel like I owe the city something. And this feels like a good way'

The previous evening, Bellingham was welcomed back to his former club Birmingham City like a hero as he watched them triumph on penalties against Barcelona.

Barcelona had travelled to St Andrew's for a pre-season friendly against the Championship club, giving Blues fans plenty to cheer about as they were given a rare opportunity to see the LaLiga champions in action.

The occasion was made even more special for those inside St Andrew's when England superstar Bellingham, who began his glittering career at Birmingham before leaving to join Borussia Dortmund in 2020 and later Real Madrid in 2023, was unveiled at the start of the game.

Before kick-off, Birmingham City's official social media account showed Bellingham taking his seat and waving to fans in a touching video captioned: 'Jude. He's home.'

As he raised his arms aloft to greet the adoring fans, Blues supporters loudly bellowed 'Jude' to honour their former starlet and fervently chanted 'he's one of our own' in a special moment for the England midfielder at St Andrew's.

Bellingham is still enjoying some richly deserved time off after playing an integral role for England at the World Cup this summer and thus has not yet returned to the Spanish capital to begin the new season under Jose Mourinho.

The £113million midfielder cheered jubilantly as he watched his boyhood club triumph over Real Madrid's bitter rivals, winning on penalties after drawing 2-2 in normal time.

Bellingham was given a warm reception as he watched Birmingham defeat Barcelona

Bellingham posed for selfies with Birmingham fans who once cheered him on as a teenager

August Priske Flyger and John Solis were both on the scoresheet for the Blues, while Hamza Abdelkarim netted a brace for the Catalans.

Goalkeeper James Beadle was the hero in the shootout as he saved spot-kicks from Roony Bardghji and Brian Farinas, while Jordi Pesquer crashed his effort against the crossbar to hand Birmingham a 3-2 win on penalties.

Few clubs have a fonder view of an academy player than Birmingham City have of Bellingham, who at 23 has already become one of the best midfielders in world football.

Bellingham burst through the ranks at Birmingham as a youngster, starring for the U18s as a 14-year-old before making his debut for the U23s at the age of just 15.

The midfielder was then promoted to the Blues' senior squad for the 2019-20 season, becoming the youngest first-team player in the club's history at 16 years and 36 days old.

After making 41 appearances that campaign, Bellingham joined Borussia Dortmund for a £25m fee and became the youngest player ever to have his shirt retired by a professional club, with Birmingham permanently keeping his No 22 jersey out of action.

Despite arriving at St Andrew's in a white T-shirt, Bellingham finished the match wearing his retired No 22 Birmingham jersey, which appeared to bring the hosts luck as they pulled off a comeback to force the decisive penalty shootout.

Sports.title: Spain's 'down to earth' World Cup hero Marc Cucurella praised for wholesome interaction with postman as he lets him wear his winner's medal
Sports.content:
Spain star Marc Cucurella thrilled his local postman after the World Cup winner offered him the medal he won Stateside last month to wear after dropping off his deliveries.

The former Chelsea defender has been a Horsham resident for some years, moving there after a previous home was targeted by burglars shortly after his 2023 transfer to the west London club.

The West Sussex enclave provided a peaceful sanctuary for Cucurella and his young family, with locals frequently sharing their positive experiences on social media if they crossed the defender's path.

But few can claim the experience his postman Gary enjoyed during one of his last rounds for the departing Real Madrid star.

Sharing his story with Horsham's social media account, the postman said: 'Had the pleasure of chatting to local World Cup winner Marc Cucurella while delivering his post today.

'Very nice, down-to-earth guy. Let me hold his winners' medal.

Marc Cucurella was praised for his thoughtful interaction with his local postman in Horsham

Gary the postman was allowed to try on Cucurella's gold World Cup winners' medal

'I reckon I am the first Englishman to hold a World Cup winners' medal in 60 years.'

Fans were quick to show their support for Cucurella's once-in-a-lifetime gesture, with one commenting: 'The biggest and greatest accolade for any football player. And he was kind enough to share that.'

Another added: 'Amazing stuff. He sounds like a really nice guy.'

One chronicler of life in Horsham wrote: 'Amazing. We keep hearing great things and sorry to be losing him. Wishing him the best of luck in his new adventures'.

In the photograph, Cucurella showed off his new braided hairstyle, a notable departure from his iconic curls.

Switching up his look has been just one piece of the 28-year-old's post-World Cup celebrations, with the player also making good on his promise to ink the face of his manager Luis de la Fuente on his body.

Horsham's social media account has previously shared snapshots of Cucurella's life in the south of England, and cheered on their 'local boy' in Spain's World Cup final against Argentina.

Since becoming a resident in the market town, Cucurella and his family have slotted in seamlessly to local life, interacting with other parents at their children's schools and even becoming regular visitors to Indian restaurant Hen & Chicken.

Life in Horsham is likely one of the reasons that Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez admitted that she was feeling mixed emotions about his move back to Spain to join Real Madrid.

Posting on Instagram after the £47.4m deal was announced, she wrote: 'I don't know how to say goodbye to my home.'

'Thank you to everyone who has been a part of this experience; I feel so lucky for everything we've shared these past years. I arrived with two babies and I'm leaving with two little boys and a British girl, and I don't know how I'm going to explain to them that Chelsea is no longer part of our lives.

'Everything we've experienced these past years has been a pure learning experience; we've lived through it all, but above all, we've enjoyed this journey. Thank you to everyone who has been a part of this chapter of our lives, thank you to my girls, whom I'm going to miss a lot, and thank you to every Blue I've met. I wish you all the best; London will always be Blue.'

Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez spoke last month about her sadness at leaving England

Rodriguez's comments come in stark contrast to how she felt before the family moved into their latest house in England.

In the wake of the traumatising burglary, the influencer told Daily Mail Sport that she had been afraid to go to sleep.

'The security is one of things I'm more worried about,' Rodriguez admitted. 'It's very hard when you are not comfortable at your home.

'I'm scared to sleep alone with my kids, for example. So for today, the most important thing for me, I think, is the security of me and my family.'

Sports.title: Man United star becomes target for Spanish club, Jordan Henderson inches closer to Chelsea move and Everton in talks with Arsenal midfielder: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Cherries chase defender

Bournemouth have stepped up talks over a £25million deal for versatile Sevilla defender Juanlu Sanchez.

The Spain U23 international can play as a right-back or winger and has attracted interest from a number of Premier League sides over the past 18 months including Everton.

However, Bournemouth are pushing to sign the 22-year-old now after offloading Alex Jimenez to Fiorentina on loan earlier this month.

Everton discuss £7m Norgaard move

Everton are in talks with Arsenal over a £7million deal for midfielder Christian Norgaard.

The 32-year-old has been on Everton’s radar for some time as agreement over a new contract for veteran Idrissa Gana Gueye looked increasingly unlikely. They also have James Garner sidelined for the start of the season after groin surgery.

Norgaard would become Everton's fourth summer recruit after the £24m arrival of Hayden Hackney, while Tyrique George and Merlin Rohl joined permanently.

Norgaard made seven league appearances for Arsenal last season and 20 overall.

He joined last summer from Brentford in a £15m deal but wanted more game time. He also had offers from Turkey and Saudi Arabia but was keen to stay in the Premier League.

Norgaard, 32, has been on Everton’s radar for some time as agreement over a new contract for veteran Idrissa Gana Gueye looked increasingly unlikely

Arsenal want to upgrade their midfield with Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

The Toffees are also in talks over a move for Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley.

The deal is viewed as one for the club’s academy. Everton technical director Nick Coc worked with Wheatley while with United’s academy.

The 20-year-old Wheatley was on loan at Bradford City last season and has been considering offers from abroad.

Dutch side Cambuur were keen to take him on loan.

Hull want £20m Socceroos teen Herrington

Hull City are closing on a £20million agreement with Colorado Rapids for defender Lucas Herrington.

The 18-year-old was part of Australia’s World Cup squad. He became the Socceroos' youngest-ever World Cup starter in their final group game against Paraguay.

Watson to make Leicester debut in Carabao Cup

Leicester City have signed Brighton winger Tommy Watson on a season loan.

The winger was at the King Power Stadium for Saturday night's friendly against Genoa, but he is not in the squad. He is set to make his debut for City in the Carabao Cup first round against Northampton Town next Saturday.

The 20-year-old, who spent time on loan at Millwall last season, had attracted interest from a number of Championship clubs but Leicester, who were relegated to League One last season, have won the race for his signature.

A scratch Leicester side lost 1-0 to Coventry City in a behind-closed-door friendly at the club's Seagrave training complex on Saturday afternoon.

Joel Latibeaudiere headed home from a corner in the 80th minute to give Coventry victory.

Altay BYE-indir?

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is a target for Spanish side Celta Vigo.

The Turkey international was on the bench on Saturday for United's friendly against Atletico Madrid.

Bayindir had interest from Besiktas early in the window but they have since signed Alexander Nubel from Bayern Munich.

The 28-year-old Bayindir has other offers but Vigo are hopeful of reaching an agreement.

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is a target for Spanish club Celta Vigo

Cherries land Benfica defender

Bournemouth have completed the signing of Portugal international defender Antonio Silva from Benfica.

The transfer is worth £21.4m plus a potential £4.3m in add-ons.

'The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans,' said Silva.

'It's a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League. I can't wait to start the season with my team-mates and I'm excited to be here.'

Toffees looking to strengthen wide areas

Everton are exploring a deal for Turkey international winger Baris Yilmaz.

The 26-year-old from Galatasaray, who was in Turkey's World Cup squad, is one of a number of options Everton are looking at.

Manager David Moyes, who oversaw a 2-1 win over Hamburg on Saturday, is desperately short on players as the new season approaches and in need of support from the club's owners.

Despite an improvement last season, Moyes was disappointed with how their campaign ended with the lack of squad depth evident in a tail off in results.

They are working to add midfielder Christian Norgaard from Arsenal and have spoken to Manchester United about striker Ethan Wheatley. They are also discussing a deal for Celtic right-back Alistair Johnston.

Hammers youngster heading to Belgium

West Ham midfielder Freddie Potts is poised to join Club Brugge in a £10.5million deal.

The 22-year-old is due to travel to undergo a medical.

The Hammers have been trying to find agreement with Celtic for midfielder Arne Engels but had their latest offer rejected.

West Ham midfielder Freddie Potts is poised to join Club Brugge in a £10.5million deal

England U21 star swapping French clubs

England U21 defender Charlie Cresswell is joining Rennes on an initial loan from Toulouse.

The 23-year-old centre-back has had tentative interest from West Ham, Fulham and Crystal Palace but will undergo a medical tomorrow before joining the French side.

Rennes have an obligation to buy for £19m and a 10percent sell-on had been included.

Tigers target Nice winger

Hull City are in talks over a £17million deal for Nice winger Mohamed Ali-Cho.

The 22-year-old who can play across the frontline has also attracted interest from Monaco.

The France U21 international had spells with Paris St Germain and Everton as a teenager before signing for Angers.

Born in France, raised in England, and of Ivorian and Moroccan descent, Cho is eligible for all four national teams. He was a youth international for England U16s.

Tottenham academy graduate courts interest

Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott is attracting interest from Como, Ajax, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis.

The former Tottenham academy graduate is in demand after scoring 31 goals last season.

Alkmaar are reluctant to sell the 24-year-old Republic of Ireland international to a rival Dutch club.

Chelsea inch closer to Henderson move

Chelsea have agreed terms with England midfielder Jordan Henderson.

The 36-year-old will be confirmed as a Chelsea player after putting pen to paper this weekend.

Henderson was a free agent after mutually agreeing cancel his contract with Brentford last week.

Jordan Henderson's path to Chelsea is clear with the two parties agreeing terms after his Brentford exit last month

Bees secure Sangare

Brentford have moved to sign Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare for £39m.

The 24-year-old completed a medical on Friday and is set to sign a five-year contract with an extra year's option.

Tractor Boys revisit Enciso signing

Ipswich Town are in talks with Strasbourg over the permanent signing of forward Julio Enciso.

The 22-year-old Paraguay international had an impressive spell on loan at Ipswich in their last Premier League season in 2024/25. He also worked with Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil at Strasbourg last season.

Meanwhile, Strasbourg may yet take 19-year-old Chelsea right-back Godwin Antwi on loan.

West London calling for Real Madrid talent?

Fulham remain in discussions with Real Madrid over the signing of Thiago Pitarch.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last month, the teenager is wanted by Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa as well as £43million duo Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, who are due in London today.

At 18 years and 226 days, Pitarch became Madrid's youngest player to start twice in the Champions League knockout stages, surpassing Brazil forward Vinicius Jr's record by 10 days.

Thiago Pitarch is one of a number of Real Madrid stars eyed by Fulham's new manager Alvaro Arbeloa, who was interim manager at the Bernabeu last term

He impressed in Madrid's 3-0 win over Manchester City in March and had arrived back in training determined to impress Jose Mourinho and fight for a first team place. But Fulham are hopeful of persuading him to join Palacios and Garcia.

Sports.title: 'I was F1 team-mates with Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton – one is greatest of all time'
Sports.content:
'I was F1 team-mates with Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton – one is greatest of all time'

Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher share the record for the most Drivers' Championships, having competed against one another on numerous occasions

View 2 Images Nico Rosberg claims Lewis Hamilton is F1's GOAT (Image: Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Nico Rosberg believes Lewis Hamilton is the greatest-ever Formula 1 driver, even after competing alongside the iconic Michael Schumacher. The 41-year-old raced with Schumacher between 2010 and 2012 as he made a comeback to the track with Mercedes.

‌



Hamilton replaced the German when he retired for good, and his hugely successful career on the track ever since has kick-started a debate as to which of the two drivers has made the biggest impact on the sport. Rosberg spent two extra years with the British driver and has followed his career since he left F1 in 2016.

‌



The ex-Mercedes star spoke to Sky Sports Germany after the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix as he watched Hamilton soar to his record-extending 106th career win. This was the Brit's first win since he joined Ferrari in 2025 and Rosberg had nothing but praise for his former teammate.

‌



He said: "This is a fantastic day for the sport. It’s historic. He’s the greatest of all time. It’s great that he turned things around, because last year looked so dark and bleak.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Race cancelled just 24 hours after F1 confirm addition to calendar as statement released READ MORE :

"He was practically on his way home, could have said at any moment: I’m quitting. But he persevered, now feels comfortable in the car, and you can see a positive momentum everywhere."

‌



Presenter Peter Hardenacke noted that Rosberg made this huge statement while standing next to Michael's brother, Ralf Schumacher. After it was pointed out, the 41-year-old joked that he was merely trying to create a wedge between the two pundits.

Ralf previously claimed that Hamilton would never reach his brother's heights, stating that the German was "light years" ahead of the Brit. Discussing his sibling's legacy on Formel1.de’s YouTube channel, Ralf said: "I have to say quite honestly and not because he is my brother, maybe Max [Verstappen] can change that in his career if he really continues driving like this, but for me, it’s always what Michael brought with him.

View 2 Images Who is better - Hamilton or Schumacher? (Image: Glenn Dunbar/LAT Images)

‌



"There’s no one else like him; Lewis Hamilton will never come within light years, not from my point of view."

Schumacher won five straight titles with Ferrari in the early 2000s and competed with the likes of Ayrton Senna, Damon HIll, Sebastian Vettel and Fernando Alonso. Meanwhile, Hamilton's success came after he departed McLaren in 2012 when he won four consecutive championships from 2017 to 2020.

The Brit saw Max Verstappen stop his dominant run and he slowly fell out of title contention through the early 2020s. However, Hamilton is now just 50 points behind current F1 leader Kimi Antonelli and may fancy his chances at a record-breaking eighth title.
