Based on this, EPFO subsequently filed a fraud case with CBI against Ambani and RCL.A spokesperson of Anil Ambani said, âThe FIR registered by CBI pertains to Reliance Capital Limited. Ambani served as a non-executive director/chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 until Nov 2021, when Reserve Bank of India superseded the board of directors of the company and appointed an administrator. Ambani denies any wrongdoing, whatsoever, and reserves all rights available to him in law. âEPFO administered the Employeesâ Provident Fund, Pension Scheme and Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme.The fund accumulations with EPFO were vested in Central Board of Trustees (CBT), the statutory governing body which held, managed and invested such funds in trust for benefit of the subscribers.RCLâs financial position deteriorated in 2019, and the company subsequently went into Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process.In 2021, EPFO lodged its claim before the resolution professional and, after NCLT approval in 2024, EPFO received Rs 1,492 crore of its total dues. The remaining amount of Rs 1,007 crore, along with Rs 809 crore interest, remained unpaid.ED, which probed RCL in a separate case, recently shared its findings with EPFO.EPFO said in its complaint to CBI that âthe conduct of and transactions entered into Reliance Capital Limited and the persons in charge of its management during the period 7 Dec 2019 to 6 Dec 2021 disclose various fraudulent transactions...â

World.title: Monsoon hope as WMO sees an El Niño counter
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The risk of overall monsoon rainfall being âbelow normalâ continues to loom over India due to a strengthening El NiÃ±o, but World Meteorological Organisationâs (WMO) latest monthly global seasonal climate update, released late Friday night, offered a ray of hope.

It predicted the possibility of a âpositiveâ Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), which could offset to an extent the negative impact of El NiÃ±o.

El NiÃ±o is a climatic pattern of warming of surface waters of central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean and is associated with a weak monsoon and harsher summer in India. IOD, on the other hand, has to do with the difference in sea surface temperatures between western and eastern parts of tropical Indian Ocean.

It helps in formation of stronger monsoon winds.

âA positive IOD is expected to develop... Combined with exceptionally warm global oceans and the likelihood of a positive IOD, the developing El NiÃ±o is expected to shape weather patterns across many parts of the world in the months ahead,â WMO said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

If WMOâs forecast comes true, there is a possibility of improved rainfall conditions in south peninsular India â the region which had reported a high cumulative rainfall deficit of 22% as of Aug 1 â in particular and over many parts of the country in general.





Monsoon may avoid deficient phase with positive IOD

It may prevent India from slipping from âbelow normalâ phase to âdeficientâ monsoon phase at the end of the rainy season.

El NiÃ±o Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and IOD are two key factors that govern variation in monsoon rainfall. Though IMD Friday flagged the continuation of âneutralâ IOD conditions through the remaining period of southwest (summer) monsoon, it, at the same time, referred to climate forecasts from some international forecasting centres suggesting that positive IOD conditions are likely to develop during Sept.

World.title: Judge Ujjal Bhuyan questions SC collegium’s opacity
World.content:
Citizens have right to know deliberations on elevation, transfer of judges: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan has questioned opacity in the collegiumâs decisions on judicial appointments.âI have noticed that the last three collegium resolutions contain no reasons whatsoever. Is this a step back from the principle of transparency?â said Justice Bhuyan at a panel discussion on Saturday. âBy withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as âantsâ and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional,â he said.To prevent the entry of such people, âthere should be some discussion, there should be some reasons givenâ, said Justice Ujjal Bhuyan. Though the judge didnât name anyone, the comment was an apparent reference to a remark by an Allahabad high court judge at a social event in 2024.He was speaking at the launch of the Judicial Transparency Index: Assessing Disclosure of Information by the Supreme Court and the High Courts, prepared by the Justice, Access and Lowering Delays in India (JALDI) Initiative at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy.The judge stressed that deliberations on the elevation and transfer of judges by the SC collegium largely remain confidential, contrary to the principle of judicial transparency.âWhile carrying out the next assessment on the scale of Judicial Transparency Index, I may request the JALDI team to also look into the aspect of opacity of the collegium system. Deliberations on elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential. Reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full. And the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly disclosed instrument. It is a very important issue. Citizens have a right to know what is happening in the courts. They have a right to know who would be their judges.They have a right to know judgments. These should be in the public domainâ, Justice Bhuyan underlined.The report is the first systematic study assessing transparency practices across Indiaâs higher judiciary and evaluates disclosure of information by the Supreme Court and high courts across judicial processes, institutional governance and administration, and judicial and administrative personnel.Referring to a previous collegium resolution reiterating the recommendation of senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal for appointment as a judge, Justice Bhuyan said he found the reasons recorded by the Supreme Court convincing but noted that despite more than three and a half years having passed, no appointment materialised.Key findings of the JALDI report reveal that only five high courts have published a budget on their websites for FY 2025-26 while none has published the criteria governing case allocation.Of the 813 judges in the higher judiciary, only 87 have publicly disclosed their assets even as only two high courts publish disciplinary sanction orders pertaining to district judicial officers.âThe findings highlight that the level of judicial transparency varies across courts and demonstrate that while individual disclosure measures have emerged...they have not yet translated into a holistic approach...â a release from Vidhi said.

World.title: Kerala heavy rains LIVE: Kerala braces for the possibility of heavy rains today
World.content:
Kerala braced for the likelihood of heavy rains and flooding on Sunday (August 2, 2026), the latest in a string of stormy days that have wreaked havoc across the State.

Also read | Heavy rain in Kerala results in increase in storage level in Mullaperiyar dam; Idukki Collector cautions public to avoid night travel on ghat section

The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for 12 districts. It has warned of heavy rains and the possibility of flash floods, mudslides, and road and neighbourhood inundation in Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasargod districts.

Notably, the IMD has not issued any weather alert for Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam. However, it has cautioned fishers from venturing into the rough seas.

The Government has ordered respective district administrations to prepare themselves to meet any eventuality. It has also requisitioned the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Kerala State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) units for emergency deployment and stationed them in districts most vulnerable to mudslides and flash floods.

World.title: UDF government orders re-investigation into KSU black flag protest against Veena George
World.content:
The Kerala Government has ordered a re-investigation into the black flag protest by the Kerala Students Union (KSU) activists against former Health Minister and Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] leader Veena George at Kannur railway station during the fag end of the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government in February.

Also read | Plea before Kerala HC by KSU worker accused of attacking former Health Minister Veena George withdrawn

Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala’s office said the decision was predicated on a petition filed by KSU activists arrested on allegedly trumped-up charges of attempted murder and armed assault in connection with the incident and subsequently remanded in judicial custody.

Mr. Chennithala’s office said the government was contemplating either forming a Special Investigation Team headed by a Superintendent of Police or referring the case to the State Police Crime Branch.

The protest against Ms. George had precipitated a politically fraught situation, resulting in clashes between CPI(M) and Congress workers in several districts in the State.

Ms. George, who had arrived at the railway station under heavy police escort, was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit of the Kannur District Hospital, reportedly with soft tissue injuries to her neck and hand.

The CPI(M) and Congress offered conflicting views of the incident, which was recorded on camera by television news crews. The CPI(M) called for State-wide protests, accusing KSU activists of being complicit in an entrenched political conspiracy hatched by the Congress to harm Ms. George, with a view to precipitating a law-and-order situation in Kerala in the run-up to the 2026 Assembly elections.

Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan spotlighted the issue and sought to put the Congress, then in the Opposition, on the defensive by visiting Ms. George in the hospital’s ICU. CPI(M) State Secretary M.V. Govindan and his Communist Party of India (CPI) counterpart, Binoy Viswam, termed the “mob violence” against Ms George as premeditated and orchestrated by the Congress leadership.

In contrast, the then Leader of the Opposition in Kerala and current Chief Minister, V D Satheesan, termed the incident CPI (M)-sponsored political theatre to divert public attention and alter the arc of the political narrative away from other controversies plaguing the LDF government, including the dismal state of public health delivery in Kerala.

He alleged that Ms. George, supposedly at the behest of the CPI(M) leadership, had sought to create a political spectacle by getting herself admitted to the ICU to put the United Democratic Front (UDF) opposition in an indefensible position ahead of the declaration of the Assembly polls. Mr Satheesan had also argued that the police cordon had prevented KSU workers from getting close to Ms George and the State had slapped grievous charges on the students out of political spite.

Earlier, the KSU had moved the High Court, stating that they were victims of the LDF government’s high-handedness and that the charges against them were demonstrably false, if television news footage of the event was anything to go by.

World.title: Three go missing, one injured, following landslip due to heavy rains at Tirthahalli
World.content:
Three persons went missing and another was injured following a landslip at Tirthahalli during heavy rains early on Sunday (August 2, 2026).

A portion of a hillock at Gandhi Nagar in Tirthahalli town gave way around 3.30 a.m., damaging nearby houses. The retaining wall constructed to protect the residents collapsed, triggering the landslip.

Three members of a family from Gangavathi in Koppal district are believed to have been trapped under the debris. The taluk administration called in a rescue team early in the morning, and Fire and Emergency Services personnel managed to rescue one person. The injured person was shifted to McGann Hospital in Shivamogga for treatment.

Tirthahalli MLA Araga Jnanendra, who visited the spot early on Sunday (August 2, 2026), said those affected were workers who had come from different parts of the State in search of employment.

“Three members of a family, including a child, are believed to be trapped under the debris. Efforts are on to trace them. Meanwhile, the person who was rescued is out of danger,” he said.

Senior police and revenue officials are camping at the spot and overseeing the rescue operations.

World.title: Assam flood situation improves as number of affected dips to 1.78 lakh
World.content:
The flood situation in Assam improved slightly, with the number of affected people coming down to 1.78 lakh even though the count of districts hit by the deluge increased to seven, an official bulletin said.

No fatalities were reported in the State in the last 24 hours, with the death toll remaining at 82, the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) said in a bulletin on Saturday (August 1, 2026) night.

The Dikhow and Dhansiri rivers were flowing above the danger level at Sivasagar and Numaligarh (Golaghat), respectively, it added.

A total of 349 villages in Golaghat, Sivasagar, Charaideo, Bajali, Dhemaji, Sonitpur and Jorhat districts remained affected by the deluge.

Charaideo was the worst-hit, with 75,199 people affected, followed by 58,824 in Sivasagar.

A total of 1.92 lakh people were affected in five districts on Friday (July 31, 2026).

Forty-four relief camps were operational in the state, providing shelter to around 15,000 displaced people. Another 17 relief distribution centres were also working, catering to 5,569 people.

A crop area of 15,060 hectares remained submerged, while 1,543 animals were washed away and another 6,765 were affected.

Damage to infrastructure, including houses, roads, bridges, schools and cattle sheds, was also reported from various parts, the ASDMA bulletin added.

World.title: West Asia LIVE: Trump says U.S., Israel to hold off on Iran strikes
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday (August 1, 2026) that the United States and Israel had agreed to hold off on any new strikes on Iran, provided a deal to end the months-long conflict is quickly reached.

Also Read : U.S. embassies urge citizens to ‘consider departing’ from West Asia

Fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again, after Mr. Trump threatened to hit Iran “very hard,” and was reportedly considering renewed heavy attacks, including against energy infrastructure targets.

Meanwhile, Iran warned this weekend against any “adventurous action” by the U.S. and said it would retaliate decisively if American forces follow through on President ⁠Donald Trump’s threats of fresh attacks on Iranian targets.

World.title: Plane carrying European tourists crashes in Peru, killing 13 people on Nazca Lines viewing flight
World.content:
A plane carrying European tourists to view the famed Nazca Lines crashed into a field outside the Peruvian city of Nazca, killing 13 people, local authorities said.

Nazca’s municipal government said the plane departed from the nearby city of Ica on Saturday and was operated by Peruvian company Aerodiana. On its website, the airline said that it has offered scenic flights over the Nazca lines for the past 14 years using Cessna Grand Caravan planes.

The Nazca Lines are a group of extensive geoglyphs scraped into the desert around Nazca hundreds of years ago by Peru’s Indigenous inhabitants. The lines form images of animals that can only be fully appreciated from planes or viewing towers.

Among the dead were seven Italian citizens between the ages of 18 and 54, two 52-year-old Spaniards and two Germans of 77 and 78 years, Peru’s Transportation Ministry said. The other two fatalities were the pilot Américo Salazar and copilot Irenka Guanilo del Carpio, it said in an official report.

President Keiko Fujimori expressed regret over the accident and said a “temporary suspension” of the airport was being considered, though the decision will be made once she receives reports from the relevant ministries.

Peruvian authorities said the accident is under investigation. Aerodiana was not immediately available for comment.

World.title: Fleming a 'big reason' for Root's return as England captain
World.content:
Joe Root said Stephen Fleming's appointment as England's test coach was a "big reason" he agreed to ​return as captain of the squad.

Root replaced Ben Stokes ‌after the all-rounder retired following the home series ​against New Zealand. Fleming succeeds compatriot Brendon McCullum, ⁠whose four-year test tenure ended last month, though he remains England's white-ball coach.

"If I'm being brutally honest, it was a big ‌reason why I wanted to do it," Root told the England and Wales Cricket Board.

"I'm very ‌excited by the way he sees the game, ‌where ⁠he sees us sit as a team, and ⁠the work that we have to do to get to where we want to get to. All of that got me very excited ​about taking this role ‌on."

"He's obviously got a wealth of experience and done some amazing things within the game as a player and as a coach, and I'm very much looking ‌forward to the next little while, and us ​trying to build something pretty special together."

Former New Zealand captain Fleming coached Chennai Super ⁠Kings for 17 years in the Indian Premier League before leaving last month. Root led England as their full-time test ‌captain between 2017 and 2022 before he was replaced by Stokes. Stokes and McCullum championed a take-no-prisoners approach, which endeared them to the fans and Root hinted he and Fleming would like to retain that attacking mindset. "The last four years have been the most fun I've ‌had in professional cricket...," said the 35-year-old.

"Clearly, the last little while ​is probably what's fresh in everyone's mind, but you're looking at a four-year period where ⁠we did a lot of amazing things. "I've taken a lot from ⁠that, and I feel it will be a big part of how I want to approach ‌things moving forward as a leader of this team." England host Pakistan for a three-test series beginning ​in Leeds on August 19.

World.title: 3 dead, 7 injured in shooting at restaurant in U.S. State of Idaho
World.content:
Three people were killed and seven more were injured, some critically, in a shooting at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant in southern Idaho on Saturday (August 1, 2026) afternoon, a Twin Falls city spokesman said.

Police who responded to the shooting found the body of the suspected gunman in an area near the restaurant, Twin Falls city public information officer Josh Palmer said. He did not know if the suspect was included in the fatality count.

Officials were still working on notifying the family members of victims and so were not yet releasing the names, ages or other details about the people hurt in the shooting, Mr. Palmer said.

Some of the people injured are in critical condition, Mr. Palmer said.

Police were still trying to determine the shooter’s identity and motive, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said in a news conference earlier Saturday (August 1, 2026).

“We believe the threat to the community is over,” Mr. Hicks said. “It was a very chaotic scene.” Mr. Palmer said investigators were still interviewing witnesses to the shooting. The restaurant is in a busy shopping plaza, and hundreds of people were in the area when it happened around 2 p.m.

Lane Koehn, 34, said he was at a stoplight near the In-N-Out when he saw a person with an AR-style rifle emerge from the drive-thru. A man with a pistol started firing at the shooter.

He then saw someone in an In-N-Out uniform drag a person, also uniformed, bleeding from a gunshot wound in her chest across the parking lot. The employee, Mr. Koehn and the man with the pistol stayed until paramedics arrived for her.

“She was pretty bad off, but I don’t know. I hope she made it,” Mr. Koehn said.

Mr. Koehn said he was told by police to evacuate because the shooting was still active.

He also said the shooter fired at least three or four rounds and it was not clear whether or not anyone in particular was targeted.

Video taken by a driver from across the street captured a shooter, who appeared to be dressed in black, walking up to a white car carrying a long rifle, opening the driver-side door and popping the trunk.

The person then walked to the trunk and reached inside. At that point the driver who shot the video left quickly, fearing that the man might be getting more weapons.

Twin Falls resident Haley Dodaro, 43, and her mother went to In-N-Out for lunch Saturday (August 1, 2026) afternoon. While waiting in the drive-thru line, they saw people running across the road and workers bolting out of the restaurant.

At first Ms. Dodaro thought there might have been a fire, but then a man directing traffic in a reflective vest said there was a shooter.

“So that’s when we knew there was a shooting. People were running out crying and screaming. It was very scary,” Ms. Dodaro said in a text message to The Associated Press.

Nayeli Rodriguez, 40, of Burley, was inside waiting for food with her daughters when she heard shots from the kitchen. An employee said it was a shooting and told people to get down.

Ms. Rodriguez said an older man tried to protect her and her daughters, and they were among the last to run outside.

“We were trying to get as far as we could and some angels let us in their car,” Ms. Rodriguez said, also via text message. “I left my car there in the parking lot.” The In-N-Out opened just about a week earlier, on July 24, as part of the company’s recent expansion to Idaho.

Police said multiple people were taken to St Luke’s Magic Valley Medical Centre.

Hospital spokesperson Taylor Marschner said in a statement that it was “working closely with law enforcement and emergency responders as they manage the situation.” Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people, is about 205 km southeast of Boise and about 120 km north of the Nevada border.

World.title: Trump says US 'locked and loaded' but will hold off on fresh Iran attack in hope of quick deal
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump said late on Saturday he would hold off on a fresh attack on Iran as long as a deal could be reached quickly to halt Iran’s nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran and “other Middle Eastern Countries” asked for a time to complete a deal that would lead to “the Immediate, Complete and Total” reopening of the Strait and “an end to Iran’s nuclear threat,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

“Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL.”

Israel “joins me in this commitment,” Trump wrote.

Israel did not immediately make a public statement on the issue.

Iran warned the US this weekend against any adventurous action and said it would retaliate decisively if American forces followed through on Trump’s threats of fresh attacks on Iranian targets.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchis comments in separate phone calls on Saturday with senior Turkish, Pakistani and Saudi officials came just hours after Kuwait’s army said it destroyed hostile drones launched by Iran against several vital facilities.

Speaking to Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Araqchi said Iran would respond decisively to any “aggression” and discussed the consequences of destabilising actions” by the US, as well as prospects for heightened regional insecurity, according to Araqchi’s Telegram account.

Araqchi later told Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan that any attacks by the US and Israel or participation by regional countries in such actions would be met with a proportionate response.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke to Trump on Saturday and “expressed concern and asked for clarity” about Us plans for Iran, a US official told Axios. The Saudi crown prince spoke to Trump, a White House official told Reuters, but did not provide details.

Nournews, a media outlet affiliated with Iran’s top security body, said on Saturday that US attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure would prompt Iranian strikes on oil fields in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as well as the gas fields of Qatar and Israel, saying, “all will be burned to ashes”.

At a cabinet meeting on Friday at the Camp David retreat, Trump said he believed US negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, could still reach a deal with Iran.

But Trump also said he was losing faith in the Iranians, saying, “They break their word so often” a claim Tehran has frequently levelled at Washington and said he would be “hitting them”.

Strait of Hormuz

Oil prices have stayed high since US and Israeli forces started the war with strikes on Iran on February 28. Trump has argued that his stated goal of keeping Iran from gaining nuclear weapons justifies higher fuel costs in the near term, but the economic pain has put political pressure on him to find a way to end the war.

Benchmark Brent crude futures rose 24 per cent in July, and analysts polled by Reuters expect prices to rise further this year. The risk of Iranian attacks has deterred most shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, an important conduit for global energy supplies, since the start of the conflict, sending shockwaves through the world economy.

A government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian property belonging to a company on Bubiyan Island were hit on Saturday, with falling shrapnel causing material damage but no casualties, the Kuwaiti army said.

Adding to the energy industry’s concerns, the Houthis in Yemen recently began threatening the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait at the other end of the Red Sea from the Suez Canal, another export route for Saudi crude.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Saturday it had received reports of two maritime incidents off Oman, including one in which a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged the engine room.

In the other incident, the master of a tanker reported seeing a large splash and an explosion close to the vessel, though no damage was reported.

World.title: Second phase of AJK polls begins in Muzaffarabad division
World.content:
The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections began on Sunday morning. Polling is being held in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies.

Polling started at 8am and will continue without interruption till 5pm. Over 300 candidates are vying for nine Muzaffarabad seats and 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions.

According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts.

Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu.

A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, while the 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies.

Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad, and Khyber Pakhtun­khwa, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab, and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad.

In Rawalpindi and Islamabad, about 27,000 registered male and female voters will elect lawmakers for LA-43 (Valley-IV), LA-44 (Valley-V), and LA-39 (Jammu-VI) seats. A total of 175 polling stations have been established, out of which 18 polling stations in Rawalpindi have been declared sensitive. A total of 34 candidates are in the fray.

In Gujrat, almost 2,000 policemen will perform security duties at scores of polling stations for the LA-38 elections. The total number of polling stations in these districts is 115, with 75 in Gujrat, 24 in Wazirabad and 16 in Mandi Bahauddin. The total number of voters is 50,225 in the entire constituency. As many as 11 candidates are contesting this seat.

In Sindh, officials said the elections will be conducted on LA-34 (Jammu-I) and LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) with polling stations established across Karachi and other districts of Sindh.

In LA-34 (Jammu-I), a total of 17 candidates are contesting the election, which has 698 registered voters in Karachi’s seven districts and 477 voters in 13 other districts of Sindh. For LA-40 Kashmir (Valley-I), 11 candidates are in the race. The constituency has 4,200 registered voters in Karachi and 403 voters in 17 other districts of Sindh.

In Balochistan, seven polling booths have been established across the province for the Kashmir Valley-I constituency, where 1,174 registered voters are expected to cast their ballots. Balochistan shares this seat with Sindh.

For the Jammu-I constituency, six polling booths have been set up, with a total of 182 registered voters, including 85 men and 97 women, eligible to vote. Polling stations have been established for AJK refugee voters residing in Balochistan at various locations, including Quetta, Pishin, Qila Saifullah, Hub, Loralai, Sibi, Mastung, Zhob and Barkhan.

In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 41 polling stations, mostly in Swat and Mansehra, have been set up for the LA-45 (Kashmir VI) seat.

PPP says agents being prevented from sitting at polling station

The PPP alleged that its polling agents were not being allowed to sit at polling stations in LA-34, calling on the Election Commission to intervene.

Sardar Abdul Shakoor, the in-charge of the PPP’s AJK election cell, said the agents were being excluded due to them not being from the “local area”.

He demanded that the Election Commission take notice of the incident and allow the PPP’s agents to perform their duties.

Allies’ rift continues to widen

The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged victorious in Mirpur in the first phase of AJK elections.

Despite multiple rounds of talks between the two parties in AJK, the tensions between the two allies over the results of the Mirpur elections did not subside, with leaders from both parties continuing to trade rigging allegations ahead of the second phase of the AJK elections.

To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday. Another round was scheduled for Saturday afternoon, but could not be held as the PML-N leaders returned to Islamabad.

A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts.

According to the sources, the PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala. Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK president Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed.

Meanwhile, the Sharif family also held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections.

A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar also attended the meeting.

World.title: Asif reacts to Naqvi's call for governance reset, urges him to begin with his own ministry
World.content:
Reacting to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s call for an overhaul of the country’s governance structure, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has advised him to initiate the change by implementing the National Action Plan (NAP) and with his own ministry.

Speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit on Thursday, Naqvi had said the governance system in the country had “collapsed” and argued that the country needed new administrative units, or provinces, to improve service delivery, accountability and access to justice. He had also said new leadership was needed in the country and argued that the youth wanted justice, merit and jobs rather than stipends and laptops.

A day later, the military’s spokesperson also urged political parties to consider an administrative reset for improving governance, arg­uing that the country’s security and stability depe­nded on adapting its governance structure to the requirements of modern times and a growing population.

Speaking at a news conference, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said governance had long been identified by the military as a prerequisite for nat­ional security. Further recalling the NAP adopted after the 2014 Army Public School attack, he said its 14-point agenda, unanimously endor­sed by political parties, had also rested on effective governance.

On Saturday, Asif reacted to Naqvi’s suggestion in an X post, in which he also mentioned the DG ISPR’s remarks.

“Mohsin Naqvi’s sahib expressed his views on the dire state of the system. I more or less personally agree with these views,” he said, calling the interior minister a “powerhouse”.

Asif added that as a political worker, he too strongly felt the process of the system’s evolution had been “held captive to factional and personal interests for decades, and it needs to be freed”.

He said he had a few requests in this regard, adding: “If the system has to be strengthened and a fundamental change has to be brought about, its forum is Parliament, of which Naqvi sahib is a member. Or this matter could be discussed in the cabinet.

“This way, these institutions and the system would strengthen, and the change would be brought about through a constitutional process.”

Asif went on to point out Naqvi was also a member of the cabinet, further claiming that he rarely attended parliamentary and cabinet sessions.

He said: “In my opinion, [treating] these institutions as irrelevant and making such a big statement to a captive audience after inviting the country’s eminent and respected businessmen doesn’t carry the same weight that speaking at the relevant constitutional forums would have earned.”

Asif said Naqvi had been on a “very powerful post” of the system for the past three years. “Had he wanted, he could have spoken about a change in the system or made progress on it during this time,” he said, moving to cite the DG ISPR’s remarks during Friday’s press briefing.

The defence minister said the military’s spokesperson had referred to the NAP.

“The implementation of one of its points, which is the armed forces’ responsibility, is being done by sacrificing lives. The implementation of the remaining 12 points is the interior ministry’s responsibility, but they have not been implemented.

“Mohsin Naqvi sahib, begin the change in the system with the implementation of NAP; begin the change in the system with your ministry. Not just the respected business community, the entire nation is with you,” he added.

Naqvi’s call for a reset of the system and creation of more administrative units has sparked a debate in the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation.

World.title: Presidential nod delay hits judiciary appointments
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The delay in presidential assent to judicial appointments has begun to affect the functioning of the superior judiciary, with the term of an additional judge of the Sindh High Court (SHC) having already expired and four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court (PHC) facing a similar situation within days, despite recommendations by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) for the continuation of their services.

Justice Khalid Hussain Shahani of the SHC was appointed as an additional judge on Jan 29, 2025, for a one-year term. On Jan 22 this year, President Asif Ali Zardari approved a six-month extension in accordance with the JCP’s recommendation, extending his tenure until July 29.

Before the expiry of his tenure, the JCP, at its meeting on July 20, recommended another six-month extension and forwarded the recommendation through the constitutional channel to the president, who is the appointing authority. However, the summary has remained pending with the Presidency and no notification has yet been issued.

With no formal approval forthcoming, Justice Shahani’s term expired on July 29. Despite this, the SHC included his name in the latest roster of judges constituting benches, anticipating that the notification would be issued in the meantime.

SHC judge’s term lapses as four PHC judges face similar uncertainty

Sources in the Presidency maintained that an additional judge could not continue to hold office beyond the expiry of his tenure unless the president formally approved the extension and the Law Ministry issued the notification.

The sources recalled the case of former Islamabad High Court judge Justice Shaukat Aziz Siddiqui, whose confirmation as an additional judge was rejected by then president Asif Ali Zardari in October 2012 despite the JCP’s recommendation. The matter was later resolved by the Law Ministry, but when it reached the Supreme Court, the apex court observed that, following the 18th and 19th Constitutional Amendments, the president’s role in the appointment of judges had become largely ceremonial and that he was bound to act on the prime minister’s advice.

When contacted, SHC Registrar Asif Qureshi said he would examine the matter.

A similar situation is emerging in the Peshawar High Court (PHC), where the tenure of four additional judges — Justice Farah Jamshed, Justice Inamullah Khan, Justice Sabitullah Khan and Justice Aurangzeb — is due to expire on Aug 4.

The four judges were appointed as additional judges on Feb 4, 2025. When the JCP met on Jan 15 to consider the confirmation of 10 PHC additional judges, it confirmed six as permanent judges while recommending a six-month extension for the remaining four. The president subsequently approved the extension, which is now nearing completion.

The JCP has since recommended a further extension for the four judges, but the matter, like that of Justice Shahani, is awaiting presidential approval.

The uncertainty comes days after the Presidency also delayed assent to the appointment of additional judges to the Islamabad, Lahore, Sindh and Balochistan high courts, prompting concern within judicial and legal circles. The recommendations, approved by the JCP on July 20 and 21, have yet to be notified, while the government is said to be examining constitutional options should the delay persist.

Pakistan Bar Council Vice Chairman Pir Masood Chishti said an additional judge whose notification had not been issued by the president could not continue to perform judicial functions after the expiry of his or her tenure. “Once the president grants approval and the Law Ministry issues the notification, the judges can resume office,” he said.

Supreme Court Bar Association Presi­dent Haroon Rashid criticised the continued delay, arguing that the president could not indefinitely withhold confirmation of, or appointments recommended through, the constitutional process.

World.title: Allies’ rift continues to widen as AJK polls enter 2nd phase
World.content:
• Multiple rounds of talks between PPP, PML-N leaders fail to defuse tensions

• Sanaullah questions Zardari’s election as president after PPP’s Form-47 jibe

• Saeed Ghani alleges PML-N govts came to power through rigging every time

• Sharif family meets at Jati Umra to take stock of ‘mounting’ political challenges

MUZAFFARABAD/LAHORE: Despite multiple rounds of talks between the PML-N and the PPP in Azad Jammu Kashmir, the tensions between the two allies over the results of the Mirpur elections did not subside, with leaders from both parties continuing to trade rigging allegations ahead of the second phase of the AJK elections.

The second phase will be held today in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies.

The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged victorious in Mirpur in the first phase of AJK elections.

In the latest exchange, PML-N senior leader Rana Sanaullah remarked on President Asif Ali Zardari’s role as he responded to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections. Rana Sanaullah, the prime minister’s aide on political affairs, was addressing a gathering in Jhelum valley alongside Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam.

“If you call the votes secured by the prime minister votes of Forms-47, then on what forms has the president gotten votes on?” Mr Sanaullah said.

“If you say to Mian Nawaz Sharif that he became the prime minister for the first time or every time through rigging, […] then remember, it is also discussed here that someone also became the prime minister for the first time after breaking apart the country,” he said in reference to PPP founder Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became the president of Pakistan in December 1971 after the secession of then-East Pakistan following the 1970 elections.

The PML-N stalwart also took a jibe at Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, whose recent remarks have sparked a fresh debate in political circles on the matter of creating new provinces. Calling Mr Naqvi a “blessed one” of President Zardari, the PML-N leader said the interior minister had “made the [political] journey of 30 years in three-and-a-half years”. “You began from where and have now reached where, and now you realise that this system is completely dysfunctional.”

‘PML-N always rigged polls’

Earlier in the day, PPP leader Saeed Ghani alleged that the PML-N had never won a general election without rigging. This followed a press briefing by Punjab’s education and sports ministers, where they said that the chief ministers of Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had nothing to show for their performance.

Addressing a press conference in Karachi, Ghani said: “The PPP did not secure power through rigging in any of the elections held till today. On the other hand, the PML-N has never secured power without rigging.”

The PPP leader alleged that the PML-N had come to power due to rigging in the 2024 polls. The PPP leader alleged that Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz “lost their own seats and then blame us”.

Talks to defuse tensions

To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday. Another round was scheduled for Saturday afternoon, but could not be held as the PML-N leaders returned to Islamabad.

A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts.

According to the sources, the PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala. Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK president Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed.

Sharifs meet at Jati Umra

The Sharif family held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections.

A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar also attended the meeting.

JAAC proposal

Separately, the PPP chairman claimed that he received a positive response from the banned Joint Awami Action Committee to his letter proposing the establishment of a truth and reconciliation commission. He welcomed the committee’s willingness to engage with the proposed commission, describing it as “a possible institutional path forward”, and noted that the proposal had also been endorsed by the AJK Legislative Assembly.

Mr Bhutto-Zardari said he would study the committee’s proposals carefully before consulting AJK Prime Minister Raja Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who would, in turn, approach the federal government and other stakeholders “to seek their initial views and assess whether sufficient common ground exists to take a consensus proposal forward”.

World.title: ‘US may not have enough forces to defend Israel against Iran’
World.content:
• Top American commander warns navy is stretched too thin; US has used nearly half of its THAAD interceptors

• Pentagon may face choice between US interests and Israel

• Missile defences consumed faster than they can be replaced; war tests Washington’s ability to fight on multiple fronts

WASHINGTON: A warning from one of America’s top military commanders has exposed a growing dilemma for Washington: The United States may no longer have enough naval forces to simultaneously defend Israel against Iranian missile attacks and protect its own interests across the Middle East.

General Alexus Grynkewich, commander of US European Command, has privately informed Pentagon officials that American naval assets are becoming stretched too thin as the conflict with Iran continues, according to reports by The Washington Post and other news outlets.

The general reportedly warned that without another US Navy destroyer assigned to the region, commanders could eventually face a difficult choice between protecting American forces and continuing missile-defence operations for Israel.

News outlets noted that the significance of the warning lies not only in the shortage itself, but in who delivered it.

Grynkewich is not an outside analyst; he is one of the senior officers responsible for managing US military commitments. His message reflects an internal military concern that America’s global commitments are exceeding available resources.

Navy destroyers equipped with the Aegis combat system have become a central part of Israel’s missile defence. These ships can track incoming ballistic missiles and launch advanced interceptors such as SM-3 and SM-6 missiles.

But these destroyers are also among America’s most valuable global military assets. They are needed in the Pacific to deter China, in Europe to reassure Nato allies, and in the Middle East to protect American bases and shipping routes.

His warning highlights a difficult military calculation: Every ship sent to defend Israel is a ship unavailable for another potential crisis. The warning comes amid reports that the United States has carried a substantial share of the burden in defending Israel from Iranian missile attacks.

Pentagon assessments cited by The Washington Post indicate US forces fired more than 200 THAAD interceptors during the Iran conflict — roughly half the Pentagon’s reported inventory — along with over 100 interceptors launched from Navy ships.

Israel also used its own Arrow and David’s Sling systems but relied heavily on American support during the most intense missile exchanges.

The issue is not simply the number of missiles fired. Advanced interceptors are expensive, complex weapons that take years to manufacture and replace. Recent assessments have warned that prolonged combat could place pressure on US stockpiles of critical air-defence weapons.

For decades, American military strategy has rested on the belief that Washington can respond to multiple crises simultaneously. The United States maintains alliances in Europe, commitments in the Middle East, and a growing military focus on the Indo-Pacific.

The warning from US European Command suggests that this assumption is being tested. The problem facing Pentagon planners is not whether the United States has the strongest military in the world — it does.

The problem is whether even the strongest military has enough ships, missiles, and industrial capacity to sustain simultaneous commitments. A conflict with Iran may therefore be revealing a broader vulnerability: America’s military power is vast, but not unlimited.

According to an analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies cited by CNN, the military has used a significant portion of its advanced missile inventory in recent weeks of fighting.

The assessment estimates that American forces have consumed about 45pc of their Precision Strike Missiles, at least half of their THAAD interceptors, and around 50pc of their Patriot interceptors.

The analysis also indicates the US has used roughly 30pc of its Tomahawk cruise missiles, over 20pc of its Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles, and around 20pc of its SM-3 and SM-6 interceptors.

Either way, the message from inside the Pentagon is clear: Modern warfare is consuming advanced weapons faster than they can be replaced, and even the US military must make choices when several crises demand the same resources.

World.title: Iranian oil smuggling drops 60pc, claim sources
World.content:
KARACHI: The influx of smuggled Iranian oil has drastically declined as tankers were hit inside Balo­chistan, causing heavy losses to those involved in this illegal business, according to sources in the oil sector.

The oil companies have been demanding that oil smuggling be stopped, but it has continued for years. However, the arrival of Iranian petroleum products increased after the US-Israeli war on Tehran began, pushing crude oil prices above $100 per barrel.

“Over the past month and a half, at least six oil tankers coming from Iran were destroyed by terrorists, but the actual number is not known,” said the source familiar with those in the oil business. However, it was not confirmed by other sources.

Since the US-Israeli attack on Iran on Feb 28, the entire world was shocked due to due to closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which is the world’s most critical energy transit chokepoint, carrying roughly 20pc of global oil, 20pc of liquefied natural gas (LNG), and about one-third of the world’s fertiliser trade.

Influx slows after terrorists destroyed six tankers in 45 days

Reserves of petroleum products began to decline in countries like Pakistan, which depend largely on imported fuel.

Pakistan faced the same situation, but the country did not experience rationing of oil and gas products. Reserves for 25 days were available, while more ships entered Pakistan during the war.

However, the influx of Iranian oil increased significantly. Smuggled petroleum products were available not only in Balochistan but also in Sindh, up to Karachi. Many say that Punjab also benefited from these smuggled oil products, which helped the country avoid rationing of oil products, as seen in India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka in the region.

“It is difficult to determine the proportions of previous and current influxes, but smuggling has decreased significantly, by at least 60pc,” the source claimed.

In FY26, Pakistan spent a record $16.86bn on the import of petroleum products, which was around 22pc of the country’s total import bill. Notably, despite higher prices, the share of petroleum products in the import bill remained within the average. Each year, Pakistan has to spend 22-25pc of its total imports on oil products.

According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, the import bill for petroleum products in FY25 was $15.94bn.

Pakistan’s illegal trade with Iran is worth more than $2 billion per year, and a number of products, such as edible oil, food products, washing powder, soaps, etc., are readily available in Karachi.

It is widely believed in the circles of trade and industry that the smuggling of oil products from Iran was deliberately ignored by the authorities due to the war and to avoid a crisis from a possible shortage of oil supplies across the country.

The government has consistently been passing on the increase in oil prices to consumers, but has successfully avoided a shortage-like situation.

World.title: US govt advises Americans to leave Mideast
World.content:
• US embassies urge citizens to ‘consider departing’ the region

• Iran says any country acting as US defensive shield will be engulfed by flames of war

• Official insists Tehran planning for worst-case scenarios

• 30 commercial vessels redirected by US naval blockade, says Centcom

• Tanker struck by ‘unknown projectile’ off Oman; Kuwait destroys hostile drones

• Houthis deny plans to impose fees on ships sailing through Red Sea

TEHRAN: United States embassies in capitals across the Middle East urged Ame­rican citizens to beware of an “unforeseen escalation” in the regional conflict and asked them to be ready to leave on Saturday as Iran’s military accused the US of “escalating tensions” in the region and warned countries against cooperating with Washington.

US embassies in Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates posted the alerts online.

“Americans in the region should consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation,” said the security alert.

The messages urged citizens to check flight details and to follow safety advice from local authorities.

“Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions,” it said.

Americans in Jordan were told not to visit US military bases there, which have recently come under Iranian missile att­ack, and in Israel they were urged to seek the location of the nearest bomb shelter.

“The Iranian regime is unpredictable, as seen by its recent decisions to attack areas in the region without warning or provocations as well as to expand attacks to areas not previously targeted [such as Egypt],” said a post on the US Embassy Jerusalem site.

The US embassy in Beirut said that the mission remained on “ordered departure status”, meaning that non-emergency US government personnel were still relocated outside of Lebanon.

Iran’s warning

“The United States is rapidly moving down the path of escalating tensions in the region,” said Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran’s military central command.

“Any country serving as a defensive shield for criminal and aggressive America will be engulfed by the flames of war,” he said in a statement read on state television.

The remarks came after US President Donald Trump reiterated threats to hit Iran “very hard”.

US media reported he was considering renewed heavy attacks as soon as this weekend, including against energy infrastructure targets.

This week, Iran and the US resumed overnight exchanges of fire after a days-long lull in fighting although there were no reported strikes overnight Friday to Saturday.

Mohammad Mokhber, adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, also warned against any attacks on Iranian infrastructure.

“You calculate through military equations, but we respond with the logic of history,” he wrote on X. “Attacking Iran’s infrastructure directly awakens the fault lines on which 250 years of your hegemonic architecture have been built.”

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian praised the Iranian people as “heroes” for enduring the US-Israeli war on the country, Al Jazeera reported.

Despite having endured “wars, pressure, and relentless hostilities”, Pezeshkian wrote on X, “The future of Iran will be shaped by the people of Iran.”

Separately, Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref was quoted by the semi-official Fars news agency as saying that the country was preparing supplies for the next two years, without elaborating on the types of supplies, Al Jazeera reported.

The official said maintaining peace among the people would continue to be the main priority and that the government was planning “even for the worst conditions”.

Kuwait ‘destroys hostile drones’

On Wednesday a drone struck a US-owned gas vessel moored in an Egyptian port, causing a fire. Egypt is investigating but has not yet accused any group of launching the attack.

Meanwhile an “unknown projectile” struck a tanker off the coast of Oman, a British maritime agency said on Saturday, as the United States and Iran vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

Kuwait’s army also said on Saturday it had detected and destroyed hostile drones in the country’s airspace since dawn, and that what it described as an Iranian attack had targeted several vital facilities.

A government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian property belonging to a company on Bubiyan Island were hit, it said, adding that falling shrapnel caused material damage but no casualties.

Iran has effectively maintained control over navigation through Hormuz since the outbreak of the war, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.

Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler said on Friday that traffic through the Hormuz strait has dropped “sharply”.

US Central Command (Centcom) said that as part of the naval blockade of Iranian ports, American forces have redirected 30 commercial vessels, boarded two and disabled two others.

Meanwhile, a merchant vessel safely passed through the Red Sea under the protection of the Italian frigate Bergamini, the European Union naval mission ASPIDES said on Saturday.

ASPIDES, the EU’s defensive maritime security operation in the Red Sea, did not identify the vessel or disclose its flag, ownership or cargo details.

Houthis deny plans to impose fees

Separately, Yemen’s Houthi-run maritime coordination body denied on Saturday that it planned to impose fees on commercial ships transiting the Bab al-Mandeb strait, saying no such decision had been taken and that passage through the strategic waterway remained free.

The Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center (HOCC) said its “safe transit service was a voluntary and cost-free service”.

“The HOCC categorically confirms that any individual or entity requesting the payment of money in exchange for transiting the Bab el-Mandeb strait does not represent the Republic of Yemen or HOCC in any capacity whatsoever,” it said in a statement.

“The HOCC urges shipping companies not to make any payments or provide any information to unauthorized individuals or entities,” it said.
